11-3121.00:991.statement: Plan, direct, supervise, and coordinate work activities of subordinates and staff relating to employment, compensation, labor relations, and employee relations.

probe.rule_why: the value is in the relationship, or advice where errors hurt people

opus.short: Lead the 13-person HR team: priorities, one-on-ones, escalations, checking work across recruitment, payroll, absence and ER cases.

today.trigger: Daily stand-ups, weekly one-on-ones, escalations from HRBPs, recruiters and payroll by Teams and mail.
steps: Scan Outlook and Teams for escalations and open cases
Hold one-on-ones and team meetings, assign work
Check status of vacancies in Recruitee, absence cases in AFAS and payroll close
Decide on difficult employee relations and labour relations cases
Report team progress to the management team
drudgery: Chasing status updates across three sites
Building weekly status overviews by hand
Re-reading long mail threads before a decision
today.time_sinks: Collecting status from people and systems before the real conversation starts; meetings that only exchange information.

lenses.faster: A Monday brief built from Recruitee, AFAS absence cases and the payroll calendar replaces status rounds; one-on-ones start from the facts.
lenses.autonomous: Alerts fire on events (a poortwachter deadline nearing, a vacancy stuck in a stage 14 days, a payroll check failing) instead of the director asking.
lenses.ambitious: Real coaching for every team member each month, with a development plan tied to the North Star, instead of firefighting.
lenses.joy: Less chasing and status gathering; more time for coaching and the hard cases people value the director for.
lenses.options: For a tricky case, get three handling options with CAO and legal points before deciding.
lenses.altitude: Design the team's operating rhythm and the dashboards and alerts that run it, rather than collecting status personally.
reach: Team-level reporting that the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst now builds by hand
First-pass case triage that HR Business Partners do today

opus.human_edge: Trust, judgement on people and conflict, accountability for decisions about staff, and the relationship with the works council and site managers.
opus.pattern_why: Leading people stays human; AI only prepares briefs, summaries and options.

in_practice.trigger: Every Monday 07:00 and on event alerts from AFAS and Recruitee.
steps: Pull open vacancies, stage ages and offers from Recruitee
Pull open absence cases and poortwachter deadlines from AFAS
Summarise escalated mail threads and Teams chats
Produce a one-page brief per team member and a team overview
Director uses it in one-on-ones and decides actions
in_practice.human_gate: Director decides all assignments and people decisions; the brief has no authority.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR management folder (weekly briefs)

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot summarises Outlook threads and Teams meetings.
Status briefs combining ATS and HRIS data cut preparation time for team leads.

risks: Team members feel monitored if briefs track individuals (works council consent under WOR art. 27 may apply)
Summaries miss nuance in sensitive cases
AVG: absence data in briefs must stay need-to-know
research_questions: How many hours per week does the director spend collecting status before decisions?
Does the AFAS and Recruitee API give the fields needed for a weekly brief without manual exports?
Would the works council see individual-level briefs as a personnel tracking system needing consent?

sol.short: Set priorities for the HR team and help people resolve difficult work.

today.trigger: Daily requests, team meetings and issues escalated by managers or HR colleagues.
steps: Review requests, deadlines and outstanding work across the 13-person HR team.
Check recruitment, payroll, absence and employee relations updates with the responsible specialists.
Set priorities and assign work across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Coach colleagues, resolve disagreements and make decisions on escalated issues.
Follow up on commitments and explain changes to site managers.
drudgery: Asking several people for the same status update.
Rebuilding action lists from meetings and email.
Checking whether owners have completed promised actions.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: updates are scattered across systems and conversations, so meeting preparation and follow-up consume time that could go into coaching.

lenses.faster: Compile a source-linked briefing of deadlines, workload and unresolved actions before the daily check-in. Draft action notes for review, removing repeated status collection and transcription.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled workflow assembles updates and reminds action owners about agreed deadlines. Priority changes, sensitive escalations and allocation of people remain with the director.
lenses.ambitious: Give every site a weekly view of obstacles to getting new hires productive and retained through day 90. Use the saved preparation time to coach managers and remove recurring obstacles.
lenses.joy: Remove status chasing and repeated note-taking. Keep the conversations where the director helps colleagues make a difficult judgment or develop their skills.
lenses.options: Compare several ways to allocate HR capacity when recruitment peaks, absence cases and payroll deadlines compete. Show the consequences for service levels and the North Star.
lenses.altitude: Design the team's operating rhythm, escalation rules and service standards, then inspect exceptions and outcomes.
reach: Take on initial cross-site service analysis currently prepared by the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Prepare capacity trade-offs with the Finance Director before requesting additional HR resources.

sol.human_edge: Colleagues need a leader who understands workload, recognises conflict, builds trust and takes responsibility for priorities.
sol.pattern_why: copilot: software can assemble the operating picture and draft follow-up, while leadership, coaching and judgments about people remain human.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled morning briefing and preparation for the weekly HR team meeting.
steps: Read approved operational summaries and the shared HR action register using role-based access.
Calculate overdue actions and approaching deadlines with explicit rules.
Draft a briefing with source links, refresh times and conflicting information highlighted.
Let the director set priorities and confirm action owners during the meeting.
After review, record agreed actions and issue routine reminders.
in_practice.human_gate: The director confirms priorities, assignments and sensitive follow-up; generated summaries do not become employee performance assessments.
systems: Microsoft Teams, Outlook and restricted SharePoint
Read-only AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube extracts
data_needed: Agreed action owners, deadlines and status definitions
Operational service measures and escalation rules
Permissions separating routine work from confidential employee cases
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint HR action register containing source links, approved actions and completion dates.

evidence.claim: SharePoint lists can hold shared action records with permissions and version history.
A source-linked briefing can reduce status collection, but its usefulness depends on consistent updates and access boundaries.
The 25% labour saving and 1.2 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: An incomplete briefing can hide urgent work or make one site's workload appear lighter.
Confidential employee relations or absence information could reach inappropriate recipients.
Turning task tracking into individual monitoring may require OR involvement and an EU AI Act assessment depending on intended use.
research_questions: How much of the director's time currently goes into status collection and follow-up rather than coaching or decisions?
Can the team maintain one action register without duplicating its existing work?
Does a four-week pilot reduce preparation time while preserving escalation quality and manager satisfaction?

grok.short: Direct the HR team's daily work on hiring, pay, absence and labour relations.

today.trigger: The working day starts, a site manager escalates, or the payroll, absence or vacancy calendar shows something due.
steps: Ask the HR business partners and specialists what is stuck in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Sort the list across hiring, pay, absence files, the works council and complaints.
Assign an owner and a deadline in the team meeting or by Teams.
Step in when a manager conflict or a labour-relations point needs the director.
Chase items still open at the end of the week.
drudgery: Chasing status across five systems and three sites.
Rewriting the same weekly note for the management team.
Rebuilding the picture of who owns an absence file or an offer.
today.time_sinks: Most of the lost time goes to reconstructing the picture before a useful conversation can start.

lenses.faster: The morning picture is already on one page, so the 'where do we stand' round drops out of the stand-up. The director uses the meeting to assign owners and handle the items that need a judgement.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly AFAS refresh, a brief lists only breaches: vacancies past the agreed age, week-one onboarding incomplete, Wet verbetering poortwachter deadlines inside two weeks, expired certificates, and payroll blockers.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the coordination cost, each site would run the same brief, and the director would see next week's load for hiring and absence across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
lenses.joy: Status chasing and the rewritten weekly note are the parts nobody will miss. The conversation with an HR business partner about a manager, a conflict or a works-council worry stays.
lenses.options: For a peak week the brief can lay out three workable responses, such as overtime within the CAO, a flex order, or moving people between Tilburg and Venlo, each with cost and roster effects.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the thresholds and, once a month, checks whether the brief changed what the team did. Assembly of the status picture sits with the system.
reach: The weekly commentary the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst now holds back for a meeting.
First sort of site escalations that are status, which today wait for an HR business partner to retell them.
A people-operations note for the Finance Director built from the same exception list.

grok.human_edge: Twelve colleagues take direction from a person who knows the three sites and will back them with the works council and the management team. That trust, and the choice of which conflict to take personally, stays with the director.
grok.pattern_why: This is daily direction of people. A prepared picture and a written assignment make the meeting shorter. Priorities, tone and labour-relations calls stay with the director, which matches a low chance that AI can do nearly all of it.

in_practice.trigger: Each weekday at 07:30 after the nightly AFAS extract has refreshed Power BI, and whenever an HR business partner or the works council marks a Teams item urgent.
steps: Pull breaches from Power BI, Recruitee and Studytube: vacancy age, unsigned offers, week-one onboarding, poortwachter deadlines, certificates, payroll-close items.
Draft a one-page stand-up note with site, owner and the ask.
The director reorders the list and assigns in the stand-up.
Owners and deadlines go to the Teams HR channel and a SharePoint action list.
Anything still open after five days returns to the director's calendar.
in_practice.human_gate: The director sets the day's priorities and approves anything sent to a warehouse manager, the works council, a union or a staffing agency.
data_needed: Vacancy age and stage in Recruitee
Forklift, VCA and food-safety expiry dates
Payroll close calendar and open blockers
Who on the HR team is in or out this week
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR action list and the Teams HR-leads channel, dated, with the owner.

evidence.claim: Power BI can push a scheduled view of a nightly AFAS extract and alert when a measure crosses a threshold the director has set.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise an Outlook and Teams thread into a short note the director edits before anyone acts on it.
A works council often has a consent right when an employer introduces a system that monitors staff or processes employee personal data.

risks: The brief becomes a second report nobody trusts if AFAS contract type, cost centre or absence status is coded loosely.
A wide Teams channel with absence deadlines or individual performance can breach AVG and worry the works council; medical content from the bedrijfsarts does not belong in it.
If the brief is used to score the HR team, it slides into personnel monitoring and needs works-council consent under the WOR.
People stop raising a messy problem because it was not on the exception list.
research_questions: What share of the Monday meeting is spent reconstructing status, and what share is already a decision?
Which AFAS fields for contract type, site, cost centre and absence-file status are complete enough to trust a threshold?
Does the works council already have an agreement that covers HR dashboards containing absence deadlines?
Which escalations last month were status, and which needed the director in the room?

steps: Scan Outlook and Teams for escalations and status
Hold one-to-ones and the weekly team meeting
Check progress on open vacancies, verzuim cases and month close
Review and sign off drafts from HRBPs and admins
Reassign work when someone is absent or a peak hits
drudgery: Collecting status from several people and systems before each meeting
Chasing overdue actions by mail
today.time_sinks: Assembling a picture of who is doing what across AFAS, Recruitee and mail before the director can decide anything.

opus.human_edge: Trust, coaching, judging people's performance and wellbeing, and being accountable for the team's decisions.
opus.pattern_why: Leading people is the job; AI only prepares briefings and tracks actions.

steps: Pull open vacancies and stage age from Recruitee
Pull open verzuim cases and poortwachter deadlines from AFAS
Pull month-close status from the payroll checklist in SharePoint
Draft a one-page briefing with risks and owners
Director reviews and uses it in the team meeting
in_practice.human_gate: The director decides priorities and reassignments; the briefing only proposes.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR team site, weekly briefing archive

11-3121.00:987.statement: Advise managers on organizational policy matters, such as equal employment opportunity and sexual harassment, and recommend needed changes.
work_activities: Recommend organizational process or policy changes.
Advise others on legal or regulatory compliance matters.

probe.rule_why: the value is in the relationship, or advice where errors hurt people

opus.short: Answer managers' policy questions (harassment, equal treatment, CAO rules) and propose policy changes to the MT.

today.trigger: A manager calls, mails or meets the director with a policy question or an incident.
steps: Hear the question or incident from the manager
Look up the policy on SharePoint, the CAO text and the law
Give advice by phone or mail, sometimes after legal check
Note patterns and draft a policy change for the MT and works council
drudgery: Answering the same CAO and policy questions repeatedly
Searching policy documents and CAO articles
Rewriting advice mails for each manager
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions from site managers that a well-searched policy would answer; drafting change proposals from scratch.

lenses.faster: Managers get a cited answer from policy and CAO texts in minutes; the director handles only what is new or sensitive.
lenses.autonomous: A Teams policy assistant answers routine questions around the clock and routes harassment, discrimination and dismissal topics straight to HR.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager, including shift leads on all three sites, gets consistent advice, and question logs show which policies are unclear.
lenses.joy: No more answering the same leave or overtime question for the tenth time; time goes to real cases and better policies.
lenses.options: For a policy change, draft three variants with cost, legal risk and works council impact side by side.
lenses.altitude: Own the policy knowledge base and the assistant's answer quality, reviewing logs and fixing gaps.
reach: Routine policy questions now handled by HR Business Partners and HR Administrators
First drafts of policy texts that external counsel writes today

opus.human_edge: Handling harassment and integrity cases with care and confidentiality, judging context, and carrying the advice with managers and the works council.
opus.pattern_why: Routine answers can be retrieved and cited automatically; sensitive cases and any policy change need a person to approve.

in_practice.trigger: A manager asks a question in a Teams HR channel or mail.
steps: Assistant classifies the question; sensitive topics go straight to HR
Retrieve relevant policy, CAO article and legal source from SharePoint
Draft an answer with citations
Routine answers go out; flagged ones wait for HRBP or director approval
Monthly, cluster questions and draft policy change proposals
in_practice.human_gate: Director or HRBP approves flagged answers and every policy change before it goes to MT and works council.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list of questions, answers and approvals

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio can build a Teams agent grounded in SharePoint documents.
Policy Q&A bots reduce routine HR questions to the HR team.

risks: Wrong or outdated answer on CAO rules creates a claim
Harassment reports handled by a bot instead of a confidential adviser
Policies on SharePoint not current, so answers inherit errors
research_questions: What share of manager questions in the last three months were routine and answerable from existing documents?
Are both CAO texts and all policies current and in one SharePoint library?
What accuracy do managers and HRBPs measure on a test set of 50 real questions?

sol.short: Advise managers on HR policy and recommend changes when policies no longer work.

today.trigger: A manager asks how to handle a situation, or a case reveals a gap in policy.
steps: Clarify the facts, urgency and people involved.
Find the applicable policy, CAO provisions and approved guidance.
Discuss sensitive facts with the HR Business Partner or legal adviser where needed.
Explain the recommended action and document the advice.
Propose policy changes and arrange the required consultation or approval.
systems: Applicable CAO texts and legal reference sources
drudgery: Finding the current policy among old copies.
Answering repeated questions about the same rules.
Rewriting similar explanations for different managers.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: policy retrieval and first-draft advice repeat frequently; ambiguous facts, sensitive conversations and approvals take longer.

lenses.faster: Retrieve the applicable passages and produce a cited draft answer with missing facts listed. The director reviews the reasoning instead of searching and drafting from scratch.
lenses.autonomous: New questions enter a controlled queue that retrieves sources, drafts a response and flags sensitive topics. Advice is released after approval, with sensitive cases routed to the appropriate specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Provide consistent guidance for managers on every shift and at every site. Use recurring questions to identify policies that need clearer wording or better training.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated document searches and routine explanations. Preserve the careful conversations that help a manager respond fairly to a difficult situation.
lenses.options: Offer several lawful responses, explaining the employee impact, operational consequences and unresolved facts. Produce different wording for a manager briefing and an employee explanation.
lenses.altitude: Own the policy knowledge base, escalation boundaries and quality checks for manager advice.
reach: Handle first-draft policy queries that HR Business Partners currently prepare.
Give Learning and Development a prioritised list of manager training needs.

sol.human_edge: Harassment, discrimination, dismissal and employee conflict require fair listening, contextual judgment and accountable advice; document retrieval cannot establish what happened.
sol.pattern_why: agent_with_gate with an llm_step: retrieval and drafting can cover much of routine advice, but a person must approve its application to the facts. The earlier automate label fits preparation better than sensitive advice as a whole.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits an HR policy question through an approved intake route.
steps: Collect the minimum necessary facts and identify the applicable employer entity, role and CAO.
Retrieve current approved policies and relevant source passages with effective dates.
Draft advice, identify missing facts and flag conflicts or sensitive issues.
Route the draft to the director, HR Business Partner or legal adviser for approval.
Release approved advice and record any proposed policy change separately.
in_practice.human_gate: An authorised HR reviewer approves every substantive response; harassment, discrimination, dismissal and legal uncertainty receive specialist review. Policy changes follow the applicable OR process before implementation.
systems: Restricted SharePoint policy library and advice register
AFAS Profit for necessary employment facts
data_needed: Versioned policies, owners and effective dates
Approved advice examples and escalation rules
Minimum case facts and access permissions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted HR advice register recording sources, draft, reviewer, approved response and retention date.

evidence.claim: SharePoint supports versioned policy documents and permission-controlled libraries.
Retrieval from approved policies can support cited draft advice, but citations and applicability still require checking.
The 50% labour saving and 1.5 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: A convincing answer may cite an outdated provision or the wrong CAO.
Managers may treat a draft as binding advice or use it to prejudge a complaint.
Case intake may collect unnecessary personal or medical information, contrary to AVG data minimisation.
Employment decision support requires an intended-use assessment under the EU AI Act; meaningful human review must be maintained where required.
research_questions: What share of questions can be answered entirely from current approved policies?
Can reviewers reliably identify the applicable CAO and resolve conflicting sources?
On a blinded sample, do drafts match specialist advice without missing sensitive escalation triggers?
What OR, privacy and AI governance requirements apply to the proposed use?

grok.short: Advise managers on equal treatment, unwanted conduct and the policy change that follows.

today.trigger: A manager asks what the rule is, or a case of unequal treatment or unwanted conduct reaches HR.
steps: Find the current policy on SharePoint, the relevant CAO clause and the complaint procedure.
Talk with the manager, usually with the HR business partner for that site.
Decide whether this is advice, a formal complaint, a confidential-counsellor route or a works-council matter.
Recommend a policy change when the same question keeps returning.
Check that Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo are applying the same rule.
drudgery: Searching for the current version of a policy or house rule.
Writing the same explanation of equal treatment, roster fairness or flex versus permanent again.
Reconstructing how a similar case was handled at another site.
today.time_sinks: Finding the clause and writing the note takes as long as the conversation with the manager.

lenses.faster: The policy clause, the CAO article and the last anonymised similar case are already in the pack, so the search and the first draft drop out. The meeting with the manager stays.
lenses.autonomous: A repeated question, such as a third ask in a month about the same roster or flex rule, opens a change note and puts it on the director's list without waiting for someone to remember.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every manager would get a written answer in the same week, and recurring questions would become one policy update the works council sees, applied the same way on all three sites.
lenses.joy: Hunting the current PDF and retyping the same explanation are the parts nobody will miss. The careful conversation about a person's treatment, and the call on what is fair, stay.
lenses.options: The pack can offer several responses side by side: apply the existing rule, clarify the house rule, change the policy, train the managers, or open the formal complaint route.
lenses.altitude: The director maintains the approved policy set, the sources the drafter may use, and a monthly review of where advice differed by site. Drafting the first pack sits with the system.
reach: First-line answers the HR business partners already give when the question is a settled rule.
A CAO check the Compensation and Benefits Specialist can sign before a pay or roster question reaches the director.
A single policy-gap list for the works council, in place of three site versions of the same problem.

grok.human_edge: A manager accepts hard advice from a director who will say the same thing in the works council and, if needed, to a union or an insurer. The confidential counsellor's conversations and any hearing stay with people, because trust and liability sit there.
grok.pattern_why: The advice pack is documents in, a structured recommendation out: clause, scope, options, and a proposed change. It becomes Noordhaven's advice only when the director sends it. Equal treatment and unwanted conduct are too exposed to run unattended.

in_practice.trigger: A manager's question is logged, or a complaint or counsel intake is opened by an HR business partner.
steps: Retrieve only the current SharePoint policy, the complaint procedure, the applicable CAO extract and anonymised prior positions.

sol.short: Find the people problems behind the numbers and recommend what to change.

today.trigger: A monthly review, a worsening HR metric or a question from a site manager or the management team.
steps: Gather HR, recruitment, learning and agency data for the relevant period.
Reconcile definitions and compare sites, roles, shifts and cohorts.
Investigate unusual patterns with HR colleagues and managers.
Develop possible explanations and assess supporting evidence.
Recommend actions and agree how their results will be measured.
systems: Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract
drudgery: Reconciling employee and vacancy identifiers.
Rebuilding the same comparisons in Excel.
Writing commentary that repeats dashboard figures.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: data preparation and repeated comparisons dominate preparation; confirming causes requires discussions and operational evidence.

lenses.faster: Use governed calculations for recurring comparisons and draft commentary directly from checked tables. Remove manual reconciliation and chart rebuilding from each review.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh, run data checks and flag material changes against agreed thresholds. Produce a review pack that distinguishes observed changes from possible explanations.
lenses.ambitious: Evaluate whether onboarding, manager training and recruitment changes improve productive 90-day hires across all three sites. Include intervention costs and evidence strength in each recommendation.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet assembly and repeated commentary. Keep the investigation with managers and the satisfaction of testing whether an improvement works.
lenses.options: Compare several explanations and interventions for the same pattern, such as shift scheduling, onboarding capacity or hiring delays. Show what evidence would distinguish them.
lenses.altitude: Set the company's people measurement standards and intervention evaluation method, then challenge conclusions rather than build every report.
reach: Prepare first-pass analyses normally requested from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Work with FP&A on the costs and benefits of retention and onboarding interventions.

sol.human_edge: The director must challenge misleading comparisons, understand operational context and decide which interventions are fair and practical.
sol.pattern_why: deterministic_software calculates and checks metrics; an llm_step drafts explanations; agent_with_gate keeps causal claims and recommendations subject to review.

in_practice.trigger: Completion of the nightly refresh, followed by the scheduled monthly people review.
steps: Join approved extracts using governed identifiers and check completeness, freshness and reconciliations.
Calculate agreed metrics using vacancy cohorts, 90-day observation windows, productivity checks and explicit agency-worker scope.
Flag material changes while suppressing small groups and showing uncertainty.
Draft findings with source tables, alternative explanations and evidence gaps.
Review findings with site managers and approve a measurable intervention.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates calculations; the director approves interpretations and actions. Observational differences are not presented as proven causes or individual risk scores.
systems: Power BI and its governed data model
Read-only AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube extracts
data_needed: Stable identifiers and agreed metric definitions
Vacancy opening, offer, start and leaving dates
Role-specific productivity confirmation and onboarding completion
Site, shift, contract type, aggregate absence and agency hours
Intervention dates, costs and relevant operational context
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted analysis register containing data versions, calculation definitions, findings, reviewer decisions and intervention results.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports reusable measures, scheduled refresh and row-level security.

today.trigger: The monthly management report, a spike in absence or early leavers, or preparation for the works council.
steps: Open the Power BI HR dashboards on the nightly AFAS extract, then export to Excel when the cut is missing.
Split figures by site, team, contract type and, where the data allow, flex versus permanent.
Test a suspected cause with the HR business partner for that site.
Write a recommendation on policy, hiring or a manager's practice.
Present the story to the management team or the works council.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same cuts in Excel because the dashboard answers a different question.
Adding flex workers by hand because they sit in agency portals, not in the AFAS headcount.
Writing the narrative again each month from a fresh export.
today.time_sinks: Cleaning and re-cutting the data, then explaining small noisy movements as if they were a cause.

lenses.faster: The standard cuts, 90-day retention, time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding and verzuim by site, are calculated before the director asks. The director starts at the interpretation.
lenses.autonomous: A move past an agreed threshold, such as 90-day retention on a shift or short-term absence on a team, opens a dated note after the nightly refresh and assigns it to the site HR business partner.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every team lead would see a stable monthly page on retention, absence and certificate gaps for their own team, and the director would spend the cycle on the few patterns that repeat across sites.
lenses.joy: Exporting, pivoting and reformatting are the parts nobody will miss. The discussion with a site lead about why new pickers leave in the first ninety days stays.
lenses.options: Each notable move can come with several plausible readings, for example roster, pay step, agency mix or a single manager, each with the comparison that would support or weaken it.
lenses.altitude: The director agrees the definitions with People Analytics, including what 'productive at day 90' means, and reviews misses and small-cell suppressions. Building the monthly cut sits with the analyst and the model.
reach: The monthly note the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst already drafts, read by the director as a decision paper.
The verzuim-cost paragraph the Controller needs in the finance pack, using the same definitions.
A site page the HR business partner can use without asking for a fresh export.

grok.human_edge: Deciding that a pattern is real, and that a manager or a policy should change because of it, depends on site knowledge and on someone who will defend the recommendation to the works council. The figures do not make that judgement.
grok.pattern_why: The rates themselves are a calculation on structured data. A cause is only a hypothesis, labelled with the comparison that supports it, and a recommendation changes personnel practice only after the director agrees. That is a gated workflow, not a dashboard left to speak for itself.

in_practice.trigger: The morning after the nightly Power BI refresh, and immediately when 90-day retention, time to hire or verzuim crosses a threshold the director has set.
steps: Refresh the agreed cuts: site, role family, tenure, contract type, and flex versus permanent where the agency data has been loaded.
Suppress groups below the cell size the privacy officer has set, and keep diagnoses out of the file.
Draft a short note: what moved, since when, the two or three hypotheses, and the comparison that would decide between them.
The director and the site HR business partner accept, reject or amend the recommendation.
The accepted action, its owner and the review date go to the SharePoint action list.
in_practice.human_gate: A recommendation that changes a policy, a roster practice or a manager's targets is issued only after the director signs it. Figures below the agreed cell size are not shown.
data_needed: AFAS headcount, contract type, site, function and start date
Leavers in the first 90 days and stated exit reason
Time to hire, offer acceptance and week-one onboarding from Recruitee
Agency hours by site, so flex workers are in the base
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint 'People analysis' folder, one dated note per decision, next to the Power BI report version it used.

Observational HR data can show where a rate moved and for whom. Naming a cause from that cut alone is a weak inference and needs a check with someone who knows the site.

risks: A shift that looks like a management problem is an older workforce, a harder client or a coding change in AFAS.

autonomous.text: Each month a drift report flags sites or teams where verzuim or 90-day leavers moved beyond a set range.

ambitious.text: Link 90-day retention to recruitment source, agency, onboarding completion in Studytube and first team lead, for every hire, not once a year.

joy.text: No more pivot rebuilding; the director spends time on why the numbers move and talks to the sites.

options.text: Three explanations for a verzuim spike, each with the data that supports or weakens it and a test to run.

altitude.text: The director defines the questions and metric definitions with the analyst and checks the reasoning, not the spreadsheet.

probe.rule_why: the value is in the relationship, or advice where errors hurt people

opus.short: Plan and steer HR, training and labour relations activities across the three sites through the year.

today.trigger: Annual HR plan, quarterly reviews, CAO changes, works council meeting cycle.
steps: Draft the yearly HR plan with priorities and owners
Plan training calendar with L&D (mandatory certificates)
Prepare works council and union consultations
Track progress in quarterly reviews
drudgery: Compiling progress updates from owners
Making the same slides for MT and works council
Tracking certificate expiry overviews
today.time_sinks: Collecting progress and rewriting the plan into several audiences' formats.

lenses.faster: Plan, progress and works council papers come from one source; drafts for each audience are generated.
lenses.autonomous: Studytube certificate expiries (forklift, VCA, food safety) trigger enrolments and manager reminders without HR action.
lenses.ambitious: Plan workforce, training and labour relations as one plan linked to the North Star, refreshed quarterly instead of yearly.
lenses.joy: Less slide-making and chasing; more time with the works council and site leads.
lenses.options: Scenario plans for peak season vs. low season, or with and without a new site contract.
lenses.altitude: Set the planning framework and decision rules; the system keeps status and drafts.
reach: Training calendar planning by L&D Specialists
Works council paper drafting by HR Business Partners

opus.human_edge: Setting priorities, negotiating with the works council and unions, and keeping site managers on board.
opus.pattern_why: The director leads planning and consultation; AI drafts and tracks.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly review and each works council meeting cycle.
steps: Pull progress from the plan tracker and Studytube
Draft quarterly update and works council paper
Director edits and decides priorities
Publish to MT and works council
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves every plan and every paper going to the works council.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR plan site

evidence.claim: Copilot drafts PowerPoint and Word documents from source files.
LMS platforms send automatic certificate expiry reminders.

risks: Generated works council papers sound generic and damage trust
Automatic enrolments clash with shift rosters
research_questions: How many hours per quarter go into progress collection and slides?
Can Studytube trigger enrolments on expiry by API or rule today?
Does the works council accept AI-drafted papers if the director signs them?

sol.short: Run the HR programme across recruitment, training and labour relations.

today.trigger: The annual HR plan, monthly programme reviews or a major operational or labour relations change.
steps: Translate business priorities into HR programmes and intended outcomes.
Agree milestones, owners, resources and dependencies across sites.
Coordinate recruitment, training, employee lifecycle and labour relations activities.
Review delivery, risks and results with specialists and site leaders.
Adjust the programme and arrange management or OR decisions where required.
drudgery: Combining several programme status reports.
Maintaining duplicate milestone lists.
Chasing dependencies between HR, operations and managers.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: programme reporting and coordination are fragmented. This task concerns the monthly and annual programme, while daily team supervision is covered separately.

lenses.faster: Maintain one programme register and generate the monthly review from current milestones and outcomes. Draft dependency warnings and decision papers from that register.
lenses.autonomous: Routine milestone checks, certificate expiry checks and owner reminders run on a schedule. Changes affecting priorities, labour relations or employee arrangements go to the director.
lenses.ambitious: Run an integrated vacancy-to-day-90 programme with training places, manager capacity and onboarding readiness visible together. Test improvements across sites instead of managing separate departmental targets.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated status packs and calendar chasing. Keep programme design, negotiation and collaboration with site leaders and the OR.
lenses.options: Compare programme sequences that favour speed, lower cost or lower operational disruption. Show how training capacity and consultation requirements affect each sequence.
lenses.altitude: Design the HR delivery system and its decision rules, then intervene when outcomes or dependencies depart from plan.
reach: Prepare cross-site training capacity proposals with Learning and Development.
Develop the people readiness part of operational change programmes with site leadership.

sol.human_edge: The director builds commitment, negotiates competing priorities and maintains constructive labour relations when plans affect employees.
sol.pattern_why: copilot supported by deterministic_software for milestones and reminders: programme administration is repeatable, while priorities, consultation and organisational change require leadership.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly programme review, a milestone change or a certificate expiry entering the agreed warning period.
steps: Read the programme register and approved recruitment, learning and HR summaries.
Check milestone dependencies, training capacity and mandatory certificate dates using explicit rules.
Draft a portfolio review showing outcome gaps, options and decisions needed.
Let the director agree changes with programme owners, site leaders and the OR where applicable.
Record approved milestones, communicate decisions and follow up on dependencies.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves programme changes and employee-facing communications. Managers verify task eligibility and certificates; absence coordination uses permitted administrative information, not medical judgments.
systems: Read-only AFAS Profit and Recruitee summaries
data_needed: Programme objectives, owners, milestones and dependencies
Course places, certificate requirements and expiry dates
Approved absence process deadlines under Wet verbetering poortwachter
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint programme register with approved decisions, milestone history and links to formal consultation records.

evidence.claim: SharePoint lists can maintain programme records and versioned changes.
Combining milestones and dependencies can reduce reporting work, but does not remove consultation or negotiation time.
The 30% labour saving and 1.2 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Automated status reporting may look complete while owners have not updated the underlying register.
A completion record may be mistaken for a valid certificate or operational authorisation.
Programme changes may bypass required OR advice or consent if consultation is treated as an optional milestone.
These savings overlap daily supervision unless the two activities are measured separately.
research_questions: Which programme reports and milestone lists can be replaced by one shared register?
Are certificate expiry dates and operational training requirements complete and reliable?
Does the programme review improve week-one onboarding and 90-day outcomes without increasing owners' reporting work?

grok.short: Plan and steer training, personnel and labour relations across the three sites.

today.trigger: The monthly planning cycle, a CAO change, a works-council agenda, or a certificate deadline before peak season.
steps: Set the quarter's priorities for hiring, training and labour relations with the specialists.
Check Studytube for missing or expired forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates.
Align the works-council calendar with roster, privacy and policy items that need advice or consent.
Hand CAO changes to payroll and compensation as concrete work.
Review at month end whether the plan happened.
drudgery: Maintaining a spreadsheet of who may not be scheduled because a certificate lapsed.
Repeating the same priorities in three site conversations.
Collecting progress by hand from L&D, payroll, compensation and the HR business partners.
today.time_sinks: The follow-up on completion takes longer than the decision about what the quarter is for.

lenses.faster: The certificate gaps, the open CAO actions and the works-council agenda arrive as one monthly pack. Collecting progress from four specialists drops out of the director's week.
lenses.autonomous: A certificate that will expire before the next peak, or a poortwachter deadline with no owner, opens a task for L&D or the site HR business partner as soon as Studytube or AFAS shows it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, Noordhaven would run a live rule that nobody is planned onto a shift without a valid certificate, and every CAO change would have an owner before payroll runs.
lenses.joy: Chasing completion lists is the part nobody will miss. The works-council meeting and the conversation with a union official about the warehouse CAO stay.
lenses.options: The quarterly plan can show several mixes of permanent hiring, flex and training capacity, with the effect on week-one onboarding and on who is allowed to drive a forklift in November.
lenses.altitude: The director sets the operating calendar and the gates, such as no go-live of a vacancy without a function code, and reviews exceptions. Chasing the specialists for status sits with the calendar.
reach: The compliance calendar and the chase, which today sit with the two Learning and Development Specialists, while course design stays with them.
The CAO implementation checklist the Payroll Specialist and the Compensation and Benefits Specialist rebuild at each change.
The site certificate list an HR business partner needs before a roster is agreed.

grok.human_edge: What the quarter is for, and how hard to push a works-council or union point, is a judgement about relationships and about the 90-day north star. A calendar cannot hold that conversation.
grok.pattern_why: The director still plans and steers the function. The gain is a prepared calendar and an exception list for training, CAO follow-through and works-council items. Direction of the specialists and the labour-relations stance stay in the room.

in_practice.trigger: The first working day of the month, a published CAO or statutory change, and any Studytube certificate due to expire within 60 days.
steps: Build the monthly pack: certificate gaps by site and role, open CAO actions, poortwachter files with an administrative deadline and no owner, works-council items due.
Draft a proposed priority order tied to peak season and to the 90-day north star.
The director agrees the month's plan with L&D, payroll, compensation and the three HR business partners.
Owners and dates are written to the SharePoint HR calendar.
Items that would block a shift or a payroll run are reviewed weekly. Exceptions are explicit.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves the month's priorities and any item that goes to the works council, a union or a change in who is allowed to work a shift.
data_needed: Studytube enrolments, completions and expiry dates for forklift, VCA and food safety
AFAS function and site, so the certificate can be tied to a person who is scheduled
Open CAO actions and their payroll effective dates
Works-council agenda and which items need consent or advice
Administrative owners of absence files, without medical content
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR operating calendar, one row per action with owner, site and due date.

evidence.claim: Studytube stores enrolments, completions and certificate status for the mandatory courses this company already runs.

CAO follow-through that starts before the text is final will put the wrong scale into AFAS.
Peak season will overwhelm a monthly cycle if the only review is monthly.

Which labour-relations items last year truly needed the director, against items payroll could have closed from a checklist?

Report progress to MT

Chasing certificate expiry lists from Studytube

11-3121.00:1001.statement: Prepare and follow budgets for personnel operations.

probe.rule_why: judging, creating or advising: the person stays the lead

opus.short: Build and track the HR and personnel cost budget, including flex workers, CAO raises and training.

today.trigger: Annual budget round with Finance; monthly variance review.
steps: Export headcount and salaries from AFAS
Apply CAO increases, step raises and social charges in Excel
Add flex worker volumes and agency rates
Agree with Controller and FP&A, then track monthly variance
drudgery: Rebuilding the Excel model each year
Reconciling agency invoices to orders
Explaining variances line by line
today.time_sinks: Manual model assembly and reconciling flex hours from three agency portals.

lenses.faster: A standing budget model reads AFAS and agency data and applies CAO rules, so the round starts from a draft.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly variance report on personnel and flex cost lands in Power BI with explanations of the largest gaps.
lenses.ambitious: Monthly reforecast of people cost per site, linked to the hiring forecast and season.
lenses.joy: No more Excel rebuilding; focus moves to trade-offs with Finance.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios: CAO outcome low/high, flex share 15 vs 25 percent, absence at 5 vs 7 percent.
lenses.altitude: Own the model's assumptions and rules; FP&A and HRIS run it.
reach: Personnel cost modelling done by FP&A Analysts
Flex invoice checks by Bookkeepers

opus.human_edge: Making trade-offs and defending the budget with the Finance Director and MT.
opus.pattern_why: CAO scales, charges and rates are written rules on structured data; output can be checked.

in_practice.trigger: Budget kick-off in September; monthly close.
steps: Load AFAS headcount, scales and contracts
Apply CAO and social charge rules
Add flex volumes and rates from agency data
Produce scenarios and variance with short LLM-written comments
Director and Controller review and approve
in_practice.human_gate: Director and Controller approve the budget and each reforecast.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI finance workspace, budget versions in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Rule-based personnel cost models on HRIS data are common practice in FP&A.

risks: Rule errors in CAO raises spread to the whole budget
Agency data formats differ and break the load
research_questions: Do all three agency portals offer an export or API for hours and rates?
How far did last year's Excel budget miss actual personnel cost, and why?
Who in FP&A or HRIS would own the model?

sol.short: Build the HR budget and explain where spending differs from plan.

today.trigger: Annual budgeting, a forecast update or the monthly finance close.
steps: Agree budget scope and assumptions with Finance and HR specialists.
Collect staffing, recruitment, training, employment terms and agency cost inputs.
Build the budget and compare options with available funding.
Reconcile actual spending and commitments against budget.
Explain variances and recommend corrective action.
systems: AFAS Profit payroll, general ledger and accounts payable
drudgery: Copying actuals into budget workbooks.
Reconciling agency invoices, accruals and payroll totals.
Rewriting standard variance commentary.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: reconciliation and workbook maintenance take time before the director can assess trade-offs; HR operating costs and company-wide personnel costs may have different owners.

lenses.faster: Populate a controlled budget model from reconciled actuals and approved assumptions. Draft variance explanations with supporting transactions and unresolved questions.
lenses.autonomous: After Finance closes the period, refresh actuals and flag material variances or missing accruals. Keep budget approval, journal posting and payments within existing controls.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling view of the cost of getting a productive hire to day 90, including recruitment, training and early turnover. Reallocate spending based on outcomes as well as budget consumption.
lenses.joy: Remove copying, formula repair and repetitive commentary. Keep the conversations about which investments improve staffing reliability and retention.
lenses.options: Compare base, peak-season and constrained-budget scenarios with explicit CAO, agency rate and hiring assumptions. Show cash timing separately from recognised expense.
lenses.altitude: Own the budget assumptions, investment priorities and variance thresholds rather than assembling each workbook.
reach: Prepare the first HR forecast and variance pack currently supported by FP&A.
Work with the Controller on agency accruals and the financial benefits of retention improvements.

sol.human_edge: The director weighs employee outcomes and operational needs against cost, challenges assumptions and owns spending commitments.
sol.pattern_why: deterministic_software maintains financial calculations and reconciliations; an llm_step drafts explanations; agent_with_gate requires approval of assumptions and the resulting budget.

in_practice.trigger: A closed accounting period or the start of an approved budget round.
steps: Import approved actuals, commitments and staffing assumptions into a versioned model.
Reconcile totals to AFAS and check cost-centre mappings, agency accruals and duplicate costs.
Calculate scenarios using approved rates, employer costs, shift allowances and CAO effective dates.
Draft variance commentary that separates verified drivers from questions for cost owners.
Obtain Finance validation and the director's approval before publishing the budget or forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: Finance validates accounting treatment and reconciliations; the director approves HR assumptions and spending proposals. Existing approval limits govern commitments, journals and payments.
systems: Read-only AFAS Profit financial and payroll extracts
data_needed: Budget scope, cost centres, account mappings and approval limits
Closed-period actuals, accruals and committed spending
Approved headcount, hiring and learning plans
CAO rates, employer charges, agency rates and effective dates
Rules distinguishing HR operating costs from total personnel costs
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted budget library with reconciled input snapshots, model versions, assumptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query supports repeatable import and transformation of structured data.
Rule-based financial models can calculate scenarios reproducibly when inputs and accounting mappings are controlled.
The 45% labour saving and 1.6 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Agency invoices, accruals and payroll costs may be counted twice or in different periods.
Outdated CAO rates or missing employer charges can understate costs.
Generated commentary may invent a reason for a variance when only the numerical difference is known.
Savings may be double-counted with FP&A or Controller work unless responsibilities are measured separately.
research_questions: Does this task cover the HR department budget, total personnel spending or both?
Can a pilot reproduce the last three closed periods and their reconciliations?
Which assumptions and variance explanations still require substantial manual investigation?
How much director time disappears after allowing for Finance review and model maintenance?

grok.short: Prepare the personnel budget and follow it through the year.

today.trigger: The budget round, the monthly close, or a forecast revision from finance.
steps: Take payroll actuals and the HR cost centres from AFAS.
Add vacancies, agency spend, training, the arbodienst and the expected CAO increase in Excel.
Compare with the FP&A forecast and explain the gap.
Re-forecast the rest of the year, including the flex swing.
Report the personnel-operations budget to the Finance Director.
systems: Staffing agency invoices in accounts payable
drudgery: Copying actuals into a workbook only the director can follow.
Reconciling three agency invoices with the flex plan.
Explaining vakantiegeld, shift allowances and employer charges again each cycle.
today.time_sinks: Assembly and reconciliation, concentrated in the budget round and again at each month close.

lenses.faster: Actuals, known vacancies and booked agency cost land in a standard variance pack, so the director stops rebuilding the workbook. The time goes to the gap that needs a decision.
lenses.autonomous: After each AFAS month close, a variance note is waiting when a cost centre or the agency total moves past the threshold agreed with FP&A. Nobody has to remember to pull it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the assembly cost, finance and HR would keep one monthly people-cost view, by site and by permanent versus flex, accurate enough to place the next agency order on purpose.
lenses.joy: Copying ledgers and chasing which invoice belongs to which site are the parts nobody will miss. The argument about whether to add a recruiter, a trainer or another flex block stays.
lenses.options: The pack can show several year-end paths, for example fill with permanent staff, cover the peak with flex at pay-parity cost, or defer a vacancy, each with employer charges and CAO allowances.
lenses.altitude: The director agrees the drivers and the threshold with FP&A and reviews the monthly exceptions. Maintaining the workbook sits with the model that finance already refreshes.
reach: The people-cost phasing the FP&A Analysts now build from a separate headcount file.
A monthly personnel-cost variance note the Controller can drop into the close pack.
A flex-versus-permanent view the Finance Director asks for at budget time, with agency invoices included.

grok.human_edge: Choosing where to spend the HR budget, and what workforce bet to defend to the Finance Director, is a management call. The pack can price the options. It cannot choose the one the company will stand behind.
grok.pattern_why: The arithmetic of actuals, vacancies and agency invoices is structured and checkable, and the director remains responsible for the budget. A draft pack makes the review faster. Publishing a forecast into the company's numbers stays a human decision shared with FP&A.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS month close completing, and the budget calendar date set by the Finance Director.
steps: Load payroll actuals, HR cost centres, open vacancies and booked agency invoices into the variance pack.
Separate the movements that are timing, such as vakantiegeld and shift allowances, from movements in heads or rates.
Draft a short explanation of each gap over the threshold, with a proposed full-year view.
The director reviews the pack with FP&A and amends the assumptions.
The agreed version is stored and used in the next management report.
in_practice.human_gate: The director and FP&A both sign the version that enters the company forecast. A hire, a flex block or a training spend above the agreed limit still needs the normal approval.
data_needed: Payroll actuals and employer charges by cost centre and site
Headcount and FTE by function and contract type
Recruitee vacancies and accepted offers not yet in payroll
Agency invoices and hours by site for all three agencies
CAO increase, vakantiegeld month and shift-allowance rules
The FP&A forecast version this must agree to
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder, one workbook version per month, with the assumption log on the first sheet.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit posts payroll and supplier invoices into the general ledger, so personnel actuals and agency cost already sit in finance.
Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract can present a monthly variance against a budget table without a fresh manual export.
A driver-based personnel budget, built from heads, scale, allowances, employer charges and agency hours, is ordinary FP&A practice and can be checked line by line.

risks: HR and FP&A keep two forecasts if ownership of the drivers is not agreed, and the management team will not know which one to trust.
Agency invoices arrive late, so the flex cost in the close is wrong in the month the peak actually happened.
A workbook at employee level exposes salaries. The pack needs a threshold below which a site or role is grouped, under AVG.
A CAO increase that is not yet in the AFAS scales will make the rest-of-year view look better than payroll can deliver.
research_questions: Who owns the personnel forecast today, the HR director or FP&A, and which workbook does the Finance Director actually use?
Are shift allowances, vakantiegeld, employer charges and the three agencies visible as separate AFAS accounts?
How large was the flex-invoice timing gap at the last three month closes?

lenses.ambitious: Review comparable roles across all three sites for inconsistent treatment and outdated descriptions. Establish a clearer explanation and challenge route for employees.

sol.human_edge: A fair evaluation requires understanding work as performed, hearing challenges and defending a decision under the applicable method.

steps: Identify the applicable CAO and evaluation method before collecting role evidence.
Extract duties and responsibilities from approved documents, with citations and missing facts.
Assemble comparator evidence and an evaluator worksheet without personal performance data.
Have Compensation and Benefits validate duties, apply the method and document the rationale.
Let the director or authorised panel approve the outcome and follow the required notification and challenge process.
in_practice.human_gate: Qualified evaluators determine the classification and an authorised person approves it; the workflow cannot update pay or contracts. Applicable OR and CAO procedures remain part of approval.

grok.short: Oversee how jobs are described, graded and placed in the function house.

today.trigger: A new role, a regrade request, a vacancy whose pay looks wrong, or a periodic review of the function house.
steps: Compare the proposed duties with the CAO reference functions and the company's warehouse function house.
Ask the compensation specialist for a grade and a salary scale.
Check AFAS for people paid off scale or sitting in an outdated function.
Decide the exception or the change in grade.
Involve the works council when the system itself changes, and the manager when one job changes.

Line-by-line comparison of duties against a reference function.
Finding employees whose AFAS function no longer matches the work they do, especially where sites invented local titles.
today.time_sinks: The comparison and the data cleanup, repeated each time a role is added or a site uses its own job title.

lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the comparison cost, every role on three sites would sit on a maintained function house, and local titles such as teamcoach and shift lead would map to one grade and one pay band.

grok.pattern_why: The director oversees classification. The comparison of duties with a reference function can be prepared and checked. The grade becomes real only when compensation and the director sign it, because it sets pay for people under two CAOs.

opus.short: Forecast staff needs per site and season, including flex workers.

today.trigger: Annual budget, new customer contract, peak season planning.
steps: Get volume plans from operations
Estimate FTE per site with turnover and absence
Split permanent and flex
Share with MT and agencies
drudgery: Manual Excel forecasting
Re-doing it when volumes change
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the forecast each time operations change volumes.

lenses.faster: A forecast model recalculates in minutes when volumes change.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly refresh from AFAS turnover and absence data, alerting on gaps.
lenses.ambitious: Rolling twelve-month forecast per site and shift, shared with agencies early.
lenses.joy: No rebuilding; focus on choices.
lenses.options: Scenarios for contracts won or lost, turnover high or low.
lenses.altitude: Own the assumptions and check outcomes.
reach: Workforce planning by FP&A

sol.short: Forecast how many permanent and flex workers each site will need.

today.trigger: Annual planning, a seasonal peak forecast or a significant change in expected workload.
steps: Obtain workload forecasts and staffing assumptions from operations.
Establish current employee and agency capacity by site, role and shift.
Estimate future capacity after turnover, absence, leave, hiring and training lead times.
Compare demand and capacity under alternative scenarios.
Agree proposed recruitment and flex requirements with operations and Finance.
systems: Operations planning inputs supplied by site leaders
drudgery: Combining site spreadsheets with different assumptions.
Converting people, contract hours and agency hours into comparable capacity.
Rebuilding seasonal scenarios after each assumption changes.
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: input reconciliation and scenario rebuilding take time. The listed HR systems do not establish workload forecasts, shift rosters or productivity standards.

lenses.faster: Use a repeatable demand-and-capacity model that updates approved inputs and generates site and shift gaps. Remove manual scenario rebuilding and unit conversion.
lenses.autonomous: On each approved planning cycle, rebuild the forecast and publish it when input checks and agreed tolerances pass. Exceptions go to the director; hiring and agency orders require separate approval.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling forecast that includes the time needed to recruit, train and reach productive capacity. Use it to smooth peak demand and reduce repeated emergency agency requests.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet consolidation and repeated calculations. Keep the discussion with operations about assumptions, resilience and a workable staffing mix.
lenses.options: Compare demand, turnover, absence, productivity and agency-availability scenarios with ranges. Show the cost and service consequences of different permanent and flex mixes.
lenses.altitude: Own the workforce planning assumptions, forecast accuracy and decision thresholds rather than producing each spreadsheet.
reach: Prepare the workforce component of FP&A forecasts.
Give Recruiters and agency coordinators an earlier, approved view of likely demand.

sol.human_edge: Operations and HR must judge whether assumptions are credible, whether proposed shifts are workable and which staffing risks the company should accept.
sol.pattern_why: deterministic_software should calculate demand, capacity and scenarios using explicit assumptions; an optional llm_step explains results. A language model should not generate the staffing numbers.

in_practice.trigger: An approved operations forecast or the scheduled workforce planning refresh.
steps: Load approved workload forecasts, employee capacity, recruitment pipeline and agency availability.
Validate units, dates, completeness and reconciliation of people, hours and productive capacity.
Calculate requirements by site, role and shift using agreed productivity and availability assumptions.
Generate scenarios and backtest forecast error; withhold publication when checks fail or thresholds are exceeded.
Publish forecasts that pass the rules and route exceptions for review before any staffing commitment.
in_practice.human_gate: Operations approves demand and productivity assumptions; HR and Finance approve material staffing decisions. Conditional publication covers forecasts only, with no automatic requisitions, agency orders or individual scheduling decisions.
systems: Read-only AFAS Profit, Recruitee and Studytube extracts
data_needed: Operations workload forecasts by site, activity and planning period
Agreed productivity standards, shift constraints and available working hours
Contract hours, aggregate absence and leave assumptions, turnover and start dates
Recruitment lead times, training capacity and valid qualification requirements
Agency hours, availability, rates and historical forecast outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted forecast register containing input snapshots, assumptions, model version, forecast errors, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query can repeat structured data preparation for a workforce model.
Explicit demand-and-capacity models can generate reproducible scenarios, but useful accuracy depends on operations data and valid assumptions.
The 55% labour saving and 1.8 times end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates.

risks: Headcount may be confused with FTE, paid hours or productive hours, especially for 150 to 300 seasonal flex workers.
Missing workload forecasts or unreliable productivity assumptions can make a precise forecast unusable.
A model may assume workers are interchangeable across sites, shifts or certificate requirements.
Forecasts can become self-confirming if hiring is constrained by the forecast and unmet demand is never recorded.
research_questions: Can operations supply reliable workload forecasts and productivity assumptions at the required site and shift detail?
Can employee and agency capacity be reconciled in productive hours without duplicate workers or missing availability?
Does backtesting outperform a simple seasonal baseline at the lead times needed for hiring and training?
What error and data-quality thresholds justify automatic forecast publication?

grok.short: Forecast how many people each site needs, by role and by season.

today.trigger: The budget cycle, peak-season planning when flex moves between about 150 and 300, or a large customer win or loss.
steps: Start from AFAS headcount, known leavers and the absence rate.
Ask operations and finance for volume by site.
Ask warehouse managers how many agency workers they expect to order.
Build an Excel forecast by role and site.
Turn the gap into vacancies for the recruiters and a flex assumption for finance.
drudgery: Rebuilding last year's workbook and retyping the assumptions.
Chasing volume numbers that sit in operations mail.
Adding agency hours that are not in the AFAS headcount.
today.time_sinks: One heavy build a year, then a forecast that is already stale by the time the peak starts.

lenses.faster: Once volume, productivity, absence and attrition are explicit inputs, the headcount arithmetic is recalculated without rebuilding the workbook. The director spends the cycle on the assumptions.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly refresh runs after the AFAS extract and the agency-hour load. It flags a site where the gap versus the approved plan exceeds the threshold, without a separate request.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the build cost, Noordhaven would keep a rolling 13-week plan by site and role, so permanent vacancies open before the peak and flex orders match real volume.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the spreadsheet and chasing last year's tab are the parts nobody will miss. The argument with operations about whether Venlo really needs forty extra pickers in November stays.
lenses.options: The same drivers can produce a low, base and high volume path, plus a permanent-versus-flex mix, with the cost at pay parity for agency workers shown on each path.
lenses.altitude: The director owns the planning rules: the drivers, the review rhythm and the rule that a forecast is not yet permission to hire. Running the arithmetic sits with the model FP&A can audit.
reach: Headcount as a driver in the financial forecast the FP&A Analysts maintain.
A month-by-month vacancy opening plan for the two Recruiters, tied to accepted offers already in Recruitee.
A flex-order proposal per site, within the approved plan, for the HR business partners to take to warehouse managers.

grok.human_edge: The bet on volume, and the choice between a permanent team and a larger flex pool, affects the CAO, the works council and the 90-day north star. Operations and the director have to own that bet. A model can only reprice it.
grok.pattern_why: With structured inputs and written drivers, next month's heads by site and role are a calculation with a checkable result. A language model is not required for the arithmetic. The director approves the assumptions and the published plan because the plan starts hiring and flex spend.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly, after the AFAS refresh and the agency-hour load, and again when operations issues a revised volume figure or a site gains or loses a large customer.
steps: Load headcount, known leavers, absence rate, certificate constraints, open vacancies and agency hours.
Apply the signed productivity and volume assumptions and calculate the gap by site, role and week.
Price permanent cost and flex cost, including agency pay parity, on the low, base and high paths.
The director reviews the assumptions with operations and FP&A and publishes one path.
Recruiters and HR business partners receive only the approved vacancy and flex numbers.
in_practice.human_gate: The director and FP&A publish the plan. No vacancy is opened and no agency order is treated as approved until that publication. A new customer or a lost contract is an exception the director handles before the next automatic refresh is trusted.
data_needed: AFAS headcount by function, site, contract type and FTE
Known leavers and absence rates, not diagnoses
Agency hours and invoices by site for the three agencies
A volume figure from operations by site and week
Signed productivity assumptions, such as orders per picker hour or stops per driver
Recruitee vacancies and accepted offers with start dates
CAO hours and the pay-parity rules that change the cost of a flex hour
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint workforce-plan folder: input versions, assumption log, published path and the names who signed it.

Flex workers missing from AFAS make the baseline too low and the peak gap too high.
Warehouse managers who order flex directly in the three agency portals will ignore a plan that arrives after they have already ordered.
A published forecast gets treated as permission to hire, or as a target that discourages a needed hire.

How far off was last year's headcount forecast by site at the peak, and which single assumption caused most of the miss?

sol.human_edge: The HRBP distinguishes a recruitment problem from an operational or management problem and gains commitment to changes that managers can actually deliver.

The HRBP tests explanations through manager and employee conversations and develops costed options.
Management approves a bounded experiment with owners, comparison measures, and a review date.

Read each CV and motivation letter in Recruitee
Check hard requirements: driving licence C/CE, code 95, forklift, VCA, shift availability, Dutch or English level
Tag and move the candidate to a pipeline stage
Note doubts for a phone screen
drudgery: Reading many near-identical warehouse CVs in peak season
Checking certificates and licences by hand
Re-reading the intake notes for each candidate
today.time_sinks: Volume peaks before Q4 and summer, when warehouse vacancies get hundreds of applications and the same hard criteria are checked by eye.

lenses.faster: Hard criteria (licence, certificates, shifts, location) are checked by rules on a structured screening form; an LLM summarises each CV against the job profile so the recruiter reads one paragraph instead of the full CV.

lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning 200 CVs for a code 95 card; what is left is talking to the borderline and interesting candidates.

reach: HR Administrator: certificate and right-to-work checks before contract
Hiring managers' first CV pass

Recruiter confirms stage move or rejection

Historic hires and 90-day outcomes for calibration

Chasing handoff acknowledgements
today.time_sinks: Working out event dependencies and correcting mismatches between approval, contract and payroll records.

lenses.altitude: The administrator designs employment-event workflows and checks that each event completes correctly.
reach: Prepare payroll-impact summaries for the Payroll Specialist
Prepare standard contract amendments for HR Business Partners

sol.human_edge: Checking that the approved change reflects the actual agreement and recognising cases requiring legal or employee-relations advice.

Apply an event-specific checklist with CAO, date and payroll checks.

lenses.faster: Copying the offer into AFAS and walking a standard workflow disappear. The administrator sees only events the rules block.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted offer, or a submitted leave, transfer, promotion, or leaver request, opens the matching AFAS workflow the same day.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every event would be in AFAS before it takes effect, including the small transfers between sites that nobody finishes today.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses clicking through the same screens. The work that remains is the settlement or the return to work that does not fit a template.

Attach the documents the event checklist already holds.
