steps: Interview the manager and job holders
Observe the work on the warehouse floor or in transport
Write or update the job description
Compare with similar jobs and the CAO grading system
Propose a grade
drudgery: Writing job descriptions from interview notes
Comparing against dozens of existing descriptions
today.time_sinks: Turning notes into a structured description and comparing with other jobs.

lenses.faster: A model turns interview notes into a description on the four factors and proposes a grade with reasons; the specialist checks it.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly scan compares AFAS job data and Recruitee vacancy texts with job descriptions and flags drift.
lenses.ambitious: Every non-CAO job at Noordhaven described and graded consistently before the pay transparency law starts.

steps: Specialist interviews and observes, records notes
Model drafts description and per-factor grade with reasons
Model lists the three closest existing jobs and their grades
Specialist decides and records the reasons
Grade stored in AFAS job scheme

13-1141.00:3366.statement: Assess need for and develop job analysis instruments and materials.
13-1141.00:3366.onet_title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
work_activities: Analyze jobs using observation, survey, or interview techniques.

probe.rule_why: judging, creating or advising: the person stays the lead

opus.short: Decide which job analysis tools we need and build questionnaires and interview guides.

today.trigger: New job family, regrading wave, or CAO grading change
steps: Review existing questionnaires and guides
Draft new questionnaire items in Word or Forms
Test with a few managers
Adjust and roll out
drudgery: Writing items from scratch
Formatting forms
Coding open answers by hand
today.time_sinks: Drafting items and processing open-text answers.

lenses.faster: An LLM drafts questionnaire items mapped to the CAO grading factors and codes open answers into those factors.
lenses.autonomous: Open answers from Forms are coded automatically and the specialist sees a summary per job.
lenses.ambitious: Job analysis covers every job family, including flex roles, instead of only disputed ones.
lenses.joy: No more hand-coding of answers; time goes to testing whether the questions work.
lenses.options: Several versions of an instrument (short for shift workers, longer for office) to test.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the instrument family and checks coding quality.
reach: Survey design support for People Analytics

opus.human_edge: Knowing whether a question makes sense to a forklift driver on a night shift.
opus.pattern_why: Turning open answers into structured grading factors is unstructured-to-structured work inside a fixed process.

in_practice.trigger: Job analysis round started
steps: LLM drafts items per grading factor
Specialist edits and pilots with managers
Forms collects answers
LLM codes open answers into factors with a confidence score
Specialist reviews low-confidence codes
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves the instrument and checks a sample of coded answers
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint job analysis folder with coded data

evidence.claim: LLMs can classify open text into given categories

risks: Coding errors move a job into the wrong grade
Questions not understood by non-native Dutch speakers
research_questions: Does the CAO grading system prescribe its own instrument?
How accurate is LLM coding against a hand-coded sample?
How many job analyses a year are needed?

sol.short: Build practical questionnaires and interview guides for consistent job analysis.

today.trigger: A job evaluation or organisational change requires a new or improved way to capture job evidence.
steps: Define the decision the instrument must support and the job groups it must cover.
Review existing questionnaires and the approved job-evaluation method.
Draft questions, examples and instructions.
Pilot the instrument with jobholders and managers from relevant sites and shifts.
Revise the instrument and agree how evidence will be assessed.
drudgery: Reusing questions by copying between files
Writing examples for each job family
Comparing pilot responses manually
Maintaining multiple form versions
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: drafting and organising pilot feedback are repetitive, while testing whether questions measure the right things needs specialist judgment.

lenses.faster: Draft questionnaires from an approved factor framework and generate role-specific examples. Automatically check missing factors, duplicate questions and inconsistent instructions.
lenses.autonomous: A new job-analysis request produces a draft instrument from the approved question bank. Unclear or incomplete responses generate clarification prompts for human review.
lenses.ambitious: Test whether the instrument captures physical work, responsibility and tacit skills consistently across office and shift roles. Maintain evidence on which questions produce useful answers.
lenses.joy: Remove form formatting and repeated wording changes. Keep instrument design, pilots and learning how people describe their work.
lenses.options: Compare a short questionnaire, a guided interview and an observation checklist against completion burden and evidence quality.
lenses.altitude: Own a tested question bank and the standards for reliable job evidence.
reach: Help HRBPs conduct consistent job interviews
Give Recruiters a clearer role-intake questionnaire
Help People Analytics improve survey and form quality

sol.human_edge: The specialist judges whether questions capture job value fairly and whether people with different literacy or language needs can answer them.
sol.pattern_why: Copilot: drafting and consistency checks are repeatable, but validity, accessibility and acceptance require pilots and specialist judgment.

in_practice.trigger: A job-review request specifies the approved evaluation framework and respondent groups.
steps: Select relevant approved questions and map them to evaluation factors.
Draft plain-language instructions and examples without changing factor definitions.
Check coverage, duplication, reading difficulty and unnecessary personal questions.
Pilot with representative respondents and compare how different reviewers interpret the answers.
Approve a versioned instrument and retain pilot findings for the next revision.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the instrument after pilot review; any change to formal evaluation factors or scoring follows the applicable CAO and governance process.
data_needed: Existing question bank and factor definitions
Role examples validated by job owners
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint instrument library containing factor mappings, version history, pilot evidence and approval records.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft questionnaire variants and check coverage against a supplied framework; this does not establish measurement validity.
The estimated 45% effort saving assumes reusable approved questions and a manageable pilot cycle.

risks: Leading questions may favour office work over operational work
Simplification or translation may change the meaning of evaluation factors
Automatic scoring could influence pay or progression without valid evidence and appropriate AI Act assessment
Forms may collect unnecessary personal or health information
Licensed evaluation methods may restrict reuse or uploading
research_questions: Is there an approved evaluation framework and permission to use its materials in the proposed tools?
Do pilots produce consistent interpretations across sites, shifts and job families?
Which questions create missing, vague or contradictory answers today?
Does the revised instrument reduce completion effort while preserving evidence quality?

grok.short: See which jobs need a proper analysis form, and make the form.

today.trigger: A role that has drifted, a new activity such as a more automated warehouse line, or a grade dispute with no recent questionnaire.
steps: Judge from memory and manager complaints which jobs are out of date.
Copy last year's Word questionnaire and edit the questions.
Ask an HRBP to send it to supervisors.
Collect replies by mail and summarize them in Excel.
Store the form wherever the previous one was stored.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same questionnaire from an old file
Chasing supervisors for replies during a shift week
Rekeying mailed answers into a sheet
today.time_sinks: Drafting and chasing replies take longer than deciding whether the job needed a new instrument.

lenses.faster: A first draft of the task inventory, physical-demand checklist and interview guide is prepared from the last accepted profile and the CAO factors. The specialist edits factors. Supervisors are not asked to endure a long form unless the job is actually new or disputed.
lenses.autonomous: A job code with no completed instrument, or a Recruitee vacancy that fits no profile, opens a draft pack and a recommendation to use the short form or the full form. Nothing is sent to supervisors until the specialist releases it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every warehouse and driver job would have a current instrument, including lifting, cold store, night work and certificates, refreshed when the work changes. Grade disputes would start from that form. Hiring would start from the same form.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding last year's Word file is the work nobody will miss. A short, fair form is something supervisors will still tolerate. The specialist keeps the part worth doing: a factor structure that matches the work.
lenses.options: Each job can have a 15-minute supervisor checklist or a full evaluation used when the grade is disputed, and a warehouse version beside a transport version. The specialist picks one to send.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the factor library and the rule for when a job needs a new instrument, then reviews completed forms that fail checks. Question design becomes a maintained system.
reach: Recruiter: the intake questions for a new vacancy, taken from the same factor library.
Learning and Development Specialist: physical and certificate requirements translated into Studytube courses.
HR Business Partner: a standard question set for a reorganisation that creates or merges jobs.

grok.human_edge: Choosing the factors that matter on a warehouse floor and in a driver's cab, and judging whether the form is honest enough to base a grade on.
grok.pattern_why: The specialist must decide which job needs an instrument and which factors the CAO and the supervisors will recognise. AI can draft the form and the short and long variants. A weak form sent to shift supervisors contaminates every grade built from it, so the person remains the author of what goes out.

in_practice.trigger: A job profile is older than the agreed age, a new job code has no instrument, or a grade is disputed.
steps: List jobs missing a current instrument, using AFAS job codes and the catalogue from the job-profile work.
Draft the short checklist and, where needed, the full form from the factor library and the CAO function factors.
Specialist cuts the draft to what a supervisor can answer about the job, and removes any question about a named person.
HRBP or the specialist sends the released form and books time that fits the shift.
Answers land in a structured sheet. The specialist reviews forms that fail checks before they can update a profile or a grade.
in_practice.human_gate: No form is sent until the specialist releases that version. No answer updates a grade or a function group until the specialist accepts it.
data_needed: Job code, site, CAO and last instrument date
Approved factor library and CAO function factors
Supervisor and shift pattern for who is asked
Certificate list from Studytube for that job family
A rule that responses describe the job, stored without employee names
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint instrument library: version sent, date, jobs covered, response count, and which responses were accepted into a profile.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Forms, included with Microsoft 365, can collect a fixed questionnaire into a spreadsheet.
Drafting a task inventory from an existing job profile and a factor list is a plausible language-model step when a person releases the form.

Write the report or guide in Word and prepare supporting charts or slides.

Reformatting source notes and references.
Rewriting technical findings for different audiences.
Reconciling comments across document versions.
today.time_sinks: The supplied baseline is 16 hours a year. Source reconciliation, drafting and review take most of the effort; waiting for reviewers can dominate elapsed time.

lenses.faster: Draft from an approved evidence pack, with charts linked to checked Excel tables. Manual copying, first-draft writing and repeated formatting largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved evidence pack can trigger a draft and a list of missing references. Publication stays with the specialist after factual and policy review.
lenses.ambitious: Produce a manager briefing, an employee guide and a shift-friendly one-page summary from the same findings. Explain how benefits work for different employee groups without exposing individual pay.
lenses.joy: Remove reference formatting, repetitive rewriting and document assembly. Keep the work of explaining trade-offs and making reward policies understandable.
lenses.options: Generate several outlines and explanations of the same finding, including plain English and Dutch versions. Compare readability and likely misunderstandings before choosing.
lenses.altitude: Own the publication standard, evidence requirements and review process. Improve reusable templates and checks instead of rebuilding each report.

sol.human_edge: The specialist judges whether findings are fair, locally relevant and consistent with the applicable CAO, and whether wording could create an unintended promise. The HR Director retains policy decisions, with OR involvement where legally required.
sol.pattern_why: AI can structure and rewrite supplied research, but this low-volume task depends on interpreting compensation evidence and explaining sensitive findings. Use deterministic checks for numbers and references; keep conclusions and publication under human control.

steps: Assemble dated, approved sources and aggregated tables, identifying the applicable CAO and employee groups.

Use an approved enterprise AI service to draft the chosen publication, linking factual claims to supplied sources and flagging unsupported statements.
Generate audience variants and check every figure, reference, translation and policy statement against the source pack.
Resolve reviewer comments and publish the approved document in SharePoint.

risks: AI may invent references, misstate study findings or apply an outdated CAO clause.

Draft wording can imply a benefit entitlement or policy commitment that has not been approved.
Report drafting alone does not establish an EU AI Act high-risk use; reassess requirements if the workflow expands into individual pay, promotion or other employment decisions.

How many hours per month go to rebooking today?
Are flex workers' certificates tracked in Studytube or only at the agency?

sol.short: Book training around shifts, rooms, equipment and instructor availability at our three sites.

today.trigger: A course is requested, new starters need training, or a mandatory certificate approaches expiry.
steps: Check Studytube for enrolments, training needs and certificate expiry dates.
Ask site managers about shift coverage and agency workers who need places.
Compare instructor, room and equipment availability using Outlook and local booking records.
Agree a date, register participants in Studytube and send invitations.
Update bookings and chase responses when attendance or availability changes.
drudgery: Copying participant lists between systems.
Exchanging emails to find a workable slot.
Checking the same booking constraints after every change.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: shift coverage and incomplete agency-worker records probably cause more delay than finding an empty classroom.

lenses.faster: A scheduling service checks availability and constraints together, removing spreadsheet comparisons and most booking emails.
lenses.autonomous: A new enrolment or certificate-expiry threshold starts scheduling automatically. Standard sessions are booked within approved rules; staffing conflicts go to the site manager.
lenses.ambitious: Give every starter a week-one training plan and reserve refresher places before certificates expire, including agency workers.
lenses.joy: Remove invitation chasing and repeated calendar checks. Spend the time helping managers release people for training and improving attendance.
lenses.options: Show several feasible schedules with travel, shift coverage, instructor cost and expiry risk for each.
lenses.altitude: Own the scheduling rules, capacity and exception process across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
reach: HR Administrator: onboarding training bookings.
Site planning team: forecasts of training-related staffing demand.
Agency coordinators: allocation of flex workers to approved training sessions.

sol.human_edge: Managers judge operational coverage and unusual attendance needs; qualified instructors determine safe class sizes and equipment requirements.
sol.pattern_why: Dates, capacities, prerequisites and availability are structured constraints with checkable results. Build a rules-based scheduler; a language model is unnecessary for booking decisions.

in_practice.trigger: An approved training request, a new-starter record or a certificate entering its agreed renewal window.
steps: Load eligible participants, certificate dates, approved shift-release windows and training requirements.
Find slots that satisfy room, equipment, instructor, capacity and travel constraints.
Book a standard session if all constraints and spending limits are satisfied; otherwise present alternatives to the responsible manager.
Write the approved enrolments and invitations through verified integrations, or prepare an import where direct writes are unavailable.
Monitor changes, prevent duplicate bookings and route conflicts or failed writes to L&D.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers approve shift-release windows and L&D approves scheduling rules in advance. Exceptions, spending above the limit and changes outside those windows require approval before booking.
data_needed: Employee and agency-worker identifiers with permitted contact details.
Certificate expiry dates, prerequisites and course capacities.
Actual shift rosters and manager-approved release windows.
Instructor availability, qualifications and cancellation terms.
Room and equipment availability at each site.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint scheduling register recording constraint versions, approvals, booking identifiers, changes and integration failures.

evidence.claim: Outlook Scheduling Assistant supports availability checks for people and configured room resources; it does not establish warehouse shift coverage.
Rules-based scheduling can combine capacities, prerequisites and release windows when reliable structured data is available.
The 75% human-time saving and threefold completion speed are planning estimates, not measured results at Noordhaven.

risks: An empty calendar can be mistaken for permission to leave a warehouse shift.
Missing agency-worker records can leave flex workers outside mandatory training.
Studytube and roster integration permissions may limit automatic booking.
Paid training time, rest periods and travel must follow the applicable CAO and working-time rules.
Calendar and personnel access must be limited under AVG/GDPR; fixed instructor availability can still dominate elapsed time.
research_questions: Can each site supply current shift rosters and explicit training-release windows, including for agency workers?
Do our Studytube and Outlook configurations support reliable enrolment writes, resource bookings and change notifications?
In a pilot, how many bookings satisfy all rules without intervention, and does attendance remain at least as good?

grok.short: Schedule classes around rooms, trucks, instructors and shifts.

today.trigger: A batch of forklift, VCA or food-safety certificates is nearing expiry in Studytube, a group of new hires has a start date in AFAS, or a site manager asks for a class.
steps: Export who is due from Studytube and who has just started from AFAS, including site and contract.
Check instructor calendars in Outlook and the room and truck list held in Excel or on SharePoint.
Ask Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo which shifts can release people, then wait for replies.
Move names between Studytube, Outlook and the spreadsheet until one date still works.
Send the invites, tell the managers, and rebook anyone who is absent, on nights, or already booked.
drudgery: Copying the same names between Studytube, Excel and Outlook.
Chasing three sites for a reply on who may leave the floor.
Rebuilding a whole session because one instructor or one reach truck was already taken.
today.time_sinks: Most of the hours go on waiting for replies and on rebooking, not on choosing the plan.

lenses.faster: Matching expiry lists, free/busy and room capacity in one pass removes the copy-paste between Studytube, Excel and Outlook and the mail chase that follows.
lenses.autonomous: A night job can open a draft when a Studytube certificate enters a 60-day window or AFAS records a start date, with no reminder in someone's calendar.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every expiring certificate, including flex workers in the peak season, would have a seat before the expiry week on all three sites.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the chase and the room spreadsheet. What is left is judging a real clash with a peak outbound day.
lenses.options: Each run can show three feasible plans, such as one class per site, a shared Tilburg and Venlo day, and an early or late slot, each with the headcount taken off each shift.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops building each timetable and maintains the rules: capacities, instructor qualifications, blackout days and the CAO code for training hours.
reach: The HR administrator's room bookings, Outlook invites and Studytube enrolments for standard sessions.
The site supervisor's first pass at who can leave a shift, once the roster and the rules are both data.
A list of paid training hours the payroll specialist can code from the approved session register.

grok.human_edge: Knowing which Friday in Rotterdam must not lose the outbound crew, and which instructor may teach a reach truck rather than only a counterbalance.
grok.pattern_why: Who needs which class, and which room, truck and instructor are free, is a set of rules with a checkable result: no double booking, capacity held, every due person seated or listed as overflow. A solver does that without a language model. A person still releases the plan, because it takes people off a shift and training time sits under the CAO.

in_practice.trigger: A Studytube certificate enters a 60-day expiry window, AFAS records a start date with required certificates, or a manager submits a class request.
steps: Read who is due, their site and their contract type from Studytube and AFAS, and flex names from the agency order where the site requires the certificate.
Read instructor and room free/busy from Outlook and equipment capacity from the SharePoint list.
Build sessions that respect capacity, qualification, site and the blackout dates L&D maintains.
Show who would leave which shift, and who still has no seat.
After approval, create the Outlook invites and the Studytube enrolments.
in_practice.human_gate: The L&D specialist approves every run before invites go out, and the site supervisor confirms any session that takes more than the agreed number of people off one shift.
systems: A constraint scheduler built on those exports
data_needed: Certificate expiry, course and validity from Studytube
Employee site, contract and weekly hours from AFAS
Flex workers on site whose certificate the hirer must arrange
Room and truck capacity, and shift blackout dates
The CAO rule for whether the hour is paid working time
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint schedule log storing the rule version and the approval, plus the Studytube enrolment for each person.

Studytube holds enrolments, completions and expiry dates for mandatory certificates such as forklift, VCA and food safety.

Shift rosters in Dutch warehouses often sit outside the HR system, so a scheduler that only reads HR records double-books peak shifts.

risks: If the live roster sits in a site spreadsheet or a planner's head, the plan will take people who are already on the outbound shift.
Flex workers live in the agency portals, so a run that only reads AFAS misses people the site still has to instruct.
CAO rules on paid training time, and any works council agreement on working hours, will be broken if they are not written into the rules.

A later change that ranks who may attend from performance or verzuim would move into employment decision territory under the EU AI Act.

opus.short: Plan training sessions around rooms, forklifts, instructors and shift rosters on three sites, then send invites.

today.trigger: A certificate (forklift, VCA, food safety) is close to expiry, a new group of hires or flex workers starts, or a manager asks for a course.
steps: Pull expiring certificates and open enrolments from Studytube into Excel
Check shift rosters in AFAS and ask team leads who can be released
Check room calendars and forklift or training-equipment availability per site by mail and Teams
Agree dates with the external instructor or training provider
Book in Studytube, send Outlook invites, and rebook when people swap shifts or call in sick
drudgery: Copying names between Studytube, AFAS and Excel
Chasing team leads for release from shifts
Rebooking after shift swaps, absence and no-shows
today.time_sinks: Matching three calendars (shift roster, room or equipment, instructor) by hand and redoing it when one changes; flex workers from agencies are not in AFAS rosters.

lenses.faster: A scheduler reads expiry dates from Studytube and rosters from AFAS and proposes filled sessions per site; the copy-paste and calendar matching steps disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Each night a job finds certificates expiring within 60 days, books the person on a session on a day they are rostered, and sends invites to employee and team lead.
lenses.ambitious: Nobody works a shift with a lapsed forklift or VCA certificate, and every new hire, including agency staff, is booked on mandatory training before the first shift.
lenses.joy: No more chasing team leads and redoing schedules after every shift swap; the specialist keeps the conversations with instructors and site leads.
lenses.options: The scheduler offers two or three session plans per site (fewer, fuller sessions against faster certification) with the cost and lapse risk of each.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the scheduling rules (lead times, group sizes, release limits per shift, which certificates block which tasks) and reviews the weekly exception list.
reach: HR Administrator: keeping certificate data in AFAS and Studytube in sync
Site and shift planners: release planning for training
Recruiter: booking mandatory training as part of the offer-to-first-shift flow

opus.human_edge: Negotiating release with site leads in peak season and judging when a lapse can be covered by reassigning tasks instead of pulling someone off a shift.
opus.pattern_why: Inputs are structured (expiry dates, rosters, room and instructor calendars) and the rules can be written down; the output is a checkable booking, so no model is needed at run time.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly run after the AFAS extract refresh, plus new-hire and agency-start events.
steps: Read certificate expiry dates and enrolments from Studytube and rosters from AFAS
Read room and equipment calendars in Outlook and instructor availability
Fill sessions by rules: rostered day, site, group size, release limit per shift
Book in Studytube and send Outlook invites to employee and team lead
Put conflicts, agency staff without rosters and unfillable sessions on an exception list
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the exception list and any session that pulls more people off a shift than the release limit.
data_needed: Certificate types, expiry dates and which tasks they block
Agency worker start dates and planned shifts
in_practice.logs_to: A scheduling log in SharePoint with every booking, rebooking and override, plus the Studytube enrolment history.

evidence.claim: Studytube holds courses, enrolments and mandatory certificates with expiry dates that a scheduler can read.
Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling fit deterministic software at autonomy 4, booking shift staff from Studytube expiry dates and AFAS rosters before a lapse.
Constraint-based scheduling of sessions against rosters and room calendars is routine software.

Agency flex workers are outside AFAS rosters, so the riskiest group is the least covered
Automated booking off shifts can clash with CAO rest and working-time rules if not encoded
A tool that tracks attendance per person may count as monitoring-capable and need works council consent (WOR 27(1)(l))

probe.rule_why: judging, creating or advising: the person stays the lead

13-1151.00:20476.statement: Monitor training costs and prepare budget reports to justify expenditures.
work_activities: Prepare financial documents, reports, or budgets.

probe.rule_why: several steps over a stream of cases, with exceptions

opus.short: Track training spend against budget and explain it to the HR and Finance Directors each quarter.

today.trigger: Month close and the quarterly budget review with Finance.
steps: Export training invoices and cost lines from AFAS general ledger and accounts payable
Match invoices to courses and participants from Studytube in Excel
Split costs per site, department and mandatory versus development
Build a budget versus actual report in Excel and PowerPoint
Explain overspend and justify next year's request
drudgery: Matching invoices to courses line by line
Fixing wrong cost centres
Rebuilding the same slides each quarter
today.time_sinks: Invoices with vague descriptions and training costs hidden in agency invoices that must be traced by hand.

lenses.faster: A Power BI page joins AFAS cost lines with Studytube completions; matching invoices by hand disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Each month after close the report refreshes and an LLM drafts a short variance note for review.
lenses.ambitious: Cost per certified employee and per retained hire, so training spend links to 90-day retention and the North Star.
lenses.joy: No invoice matching in Excel; time goes to the conversation about what training is worth.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios for next year: flex volume high or low, in-house versus external trainers, with or without sector training fund subsidies.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the cost-coding rules and dashboard definitions and checks the monthly numbers.
reach: Invoice coding of training costs now done by Bookkeepers
Training budget lines in FP&A forecasts
Claiming sector training fund subsidies

opus.human_edge: Arguing the value of a programme with the HR and Finance Directors and deciding what to cut.
opus.pattern_why: The joins and totals are deterministic; an LLM step codes messy invoice descriptions to courses and drafts the variance text, both checkable.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS month close completed and nightly Power BI refresh.
steps: Pull training cost lines from AFAS and completions from Studytube
LLM codes uncoded invoice lines to course and site, with confidence
Power BI shows budget versus actual, cost per participant and per certificate
LLM drafts a variance note; specialist edits and sends
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves low-confidence coding and the variance note before it goes to Finance.
data_needed: Training cost ledger accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset history and a SharePoint folder with signed-off monthly notes

evidence.claim: Power BI can combine AFAS and LMS extracts in one report
LLMs classify invoice lines to categories with reviewable confidence

risks: Training costs booked on generic accounts, so the base data is unreliable
Training paid via agencies hidden in flex invoices
Numbers drift from Finance reporting if definitions differ
research_questions: Which AFAS ledger accounts and cost centres carry training costs today, and how clean are they?
What share of training spend arrives via agency invoices?
Does the Controller accept an L&D-owned Power BI page as the source for budget reviews?

sol.short: Track training spending and explain the budget to HR and Finance.

today.trigger: Monthly reporting, a budget review or a request to justify a training purchase.
steps: Collect AFAS training expenses, supplier invoices and known commitments.
Match costs to courses, sites and participants using Studytube and Excel.
Resolve missing cost codes, duplicate entries and invoices covering several activities.
Compare actual spending and commitments with the approved budget.
Write explanations and review the report with HR and Finance.
systems: AFAS Profit general ledger and accounts payable
drudgery: Rebuilding cost tables each month.
Matching invoice descriptions to course names.
Rewriting similar variance explanations.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: inconsistent cost coding, unrecorded commitments and reconciliation to Finance's reporting period.

lenses.faster: A reconciled cost model produces the tables and variance flags automatically. AI drafts explanations from verified figures and supporting records.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh updates a draft training-cost view and opens exceptions for missing codes or unmatched commitments.
lenses.ambitious: Compare cost per completed course and per starter who becomes productive and stays 90 days, while keeping claims about training effects appropriately cautious.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet rebuilding and invoice-description searches. Keep the discussions about which training deserves funding.
lenses.options: Compare budget scenarios for onboarding volumes, renewal demand and internal versus external delivery.
lenses.altitude: Design the cost definitions and decision rules that make training investment visible and comparable across sites.
reach: Controller: training cost-centre variance analysis.
FP&A Analyst: training demand and spending forecasts.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: agreed learning-cost measures.

sol.human_edge: L&D and Finance decide what counts as training cost, whether spending is justified and what conclusions the evidence supports.
sol.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations and reconciliation produce the financial facts. A bounded language-model step turns those facts into a draft explanation that a person checks.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly extract completes successfully or the monthly reporting period is ready for review.
steps: Load AFAS expenses, the approved budget, recorded commitments and Studytube completion data.
Apply Finance-approved mappings, reconcile totals and flag incomplete or inconsistent records.
Calculate actuals, commitments, forecast spending and variances using deterministic formulas.
Draft explanations with references to the underlying figures and mark unsupported causes as unknown.
Have L&D and the Controller resolve exceptions and approve the report before publication.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the expenditure explanation and the Controller approves reconciliation and accounting treatment. The workflow cannot approve invoices, change ledger entries or release payments.
data_needed: Ledger lines, invoice references, cost centres and reporting periods.
Purchase commitments, cancellations and expected invoice dates.
Finance-approved treatment of VAT, accruals and internal trainer time.
Course enrolments and completions, using aggregate data where possible.
in_practice.logs_to: The restricted SharePoint monthly training-budget archive, including source refresh dates, reconciliation results, mapping versions and report approvals.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports refreshed data models and reports; Noordhaven's stated nightly AFAS extract supplies an existing reporting starting point.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI; user-supplied company system description

evidence.claim: A language model can draft variance commentary from supplied figures, but the figures and causal explanations need separate checks.
The 70% human-time saving and 2.5-fold completion speed depend on clean mappings and recorded commitments and have not been measured.

risks: Invoices alone understate future spending when commitments and accruals are missing.
Uncontrolled mappings can double-count shared invoices or misallocate costs between sites.
Generated commentary can invent reasons for a variance.
Training and retention correlations can be mistaken for causal effects.
A nightly refresh can produce a complete-looking report before month-close corrections are available.
research_questions: What proportion of training costs and commitments can be mapped reliably to a course, site and reporting period?
Which cost definitions and reconciliation tolerances will the Controller approve?
Does a two-cycle pilot reduce preparation time while matching the approved financial totals and preserving explanation quality?

grok.short: Report monthly training cost and explain the movements.

today.trigger: Month close, a budget question from the HR Director or the controller, or a vendor invoice that does not match what L&D expected.
steps: Pull actuals from AFAS for the training cost centres and chase invoices coded somewhere else.
Add payroll hours for paid training time and the Studytube licence, usually in a separate Excel tab.
Compare the total with last month's workbook and with the budget the controller holds.
Rewrite the same variance explanations: timing, a late invoice, or a course that ran twice.
Send the workbook to finance and answer the same questions again in Teams.
drudgery: Rebuilding the monthly workbook from an AFAS export and VLOOKUP.
Splitting one Studytube invoice across three sites by a homemade key.
Hunting invoices that were coded to a warehouse cost centre instead of training.
today.time_sinks: The hours sit in reconciling sources that do not share a key, and in explaining differences that are often just timing or a wrong cost centre.

lenses.faster: The export, the VLOOKUP and the reformat disappear once ledger accounts, payroll wage types and the Studytube licence map to one training table.
lenses.autonomous: On the night the AFAS extract refreshes Power BI, the training table updates and flags any line that crossed an agreed euro or percent threshold.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every programme would show cost per completion and cost per person still in the job 90 days after hire or after a move, which the company does not see today.
lenses.joy: Coding invoices and rebuilding the workbook is the part nobody will miss. Judging whether an external trainer in Venlo is worth the rate is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The same actuals can be cut by site, by permanent staff and flex, by mandatory certificate and elective course, and as a year-end forecast under a high and a low hiring month.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops assembling the workbook and owns the definitions: what counts as a training euro, which wage types are in, and which exceptions the controller has already accepted.
reach: The FP&A analyst's rebuild of the training lines during month close.
The controller's first-pass variance questions on the training cost centre.
The people analytics analyst's cost-per-completion figures on the HR dashboard.

grok.human_edge: Telling a real overrun from a late invoice or a miscode, and deciding whether a programme should stop, shrink, or run again next quarter.
grok.pattern_why: The report is a join of AFAS ledger lines, payroll wage types and Studytube completions against an agreed budget. The totals are checkable against the ledger. The justification sentence is filled from those computed variances, so a model is not asked to produce a number the controller cannot trace to a journal line.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract lands, and again at month close before the controller locks the period.
steps: Join general-ledger actuals, accounts-payable invoices and payroll training-hour wage types to the agreed training categories.
Attach Studytube completions for the same period and the same course names.
Flag lines over the threshold, new suppliers, and amounts with no matching completion.
Fill a one-page note from those flags: site, programme, amount, and whether it is timing or a true overrun.
File the pack in the same SharePoint place the controller already uses for month-end.
in_practice.human_gate: L&D approves the monthly note before it goes to the HR Director, and the controller approves any change to the account mapping. Corrections are made in AFAS coding, not by typing over the figure.
data_needed: General-ledger actuals and budget by cost centre and period
Supplier and invoice reference from accounts payable
Payroll wage types for CAO paid training time
Studytube completions by course and site

Collect approved site procedures and examples of current waste or inefficiency.
Create training materials and practical exercises for the affected roles.
Arrange delivery across sites, shifts and relevant agency workers.
Check understanding and review operational results with the process owner.
systems: Power BI where suitable operational data exists
drudgery: Turning long procedures into short lessons.
Reworking the same lesson for each site and language.
Writing quizzes and combining course feedback.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow to validate: obtaining accurate site-specific procedures and arranging practical instruction during busy shifts.

lenses.faster: AI turns approved procedures into draft short lessons, quizzes and shift briefings, reducing repeated writing and formatting.
lenses.autonomous: A published procedure revision creates a training-impact review and draft updates. Approved lessons can then be assigned to the relevant groups automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Build short lessons around recurring errors in waste sorting, packaging and energy use, and test whether the relevant behaviour improves.

sol.human_edge: Site experts validate technical instructions and instructors observe practical performance. Workers explain why a procedure succeeds or fails under real operating conditions.

Have the process owner and a suitable language reviewer check instructions and translations.
Pilot the approved materials on one relevant shift, adjust them and assign the final training through Studytube.
Compare practical observations and operational measures before and after delivery, accounting for changes in workload.
in_practice.human_gate: The operational and safety or environmental owner approves every technical instruction before publication. Practical competence and any regulated certification require the appropriate human assessment.
systems: Excel or an authorised operational Power BI dataset

Site-specific waste streams, equipment and operating constraints.
Target roles, shifts, languages and literacy needs.
Approved examples and permission to use workplace photographs.
Relevant baseline measures, workload denominators and observation criteria.

grok.short: Develop short training on waste, damage and fuel use.

today.trigger: A site manager complains about damage or waste, a customer asks what the crews are taught, or someone remembers the yearly environment slides.
steps: Find last year's PowerPoint on SharePoint, often written for one site only.
Ask finance whether damage, waste or fuel even has a number, and wait.
Rewrite a general session that tries to cover recycling, driving and the dock in one hour.
Deliver it once in Rotterdam; Tilburg and Venlo get a shortened retell.
Do not check whether damage or waste moved afterwards.
drudgery: Searching SharePoint for the last version of a deck nobody owns.
Rewriting generic sustainability slides that do not mention a Noordhaven dock.
Chasing attendance lists after a toolbox talk that was never written down.
today.time_sinks: The few hours go into making a deck and getting one room booked. None of them go into a before-and-after look at damage or waste.

lenses.faster: A first script and a short quiz can be drafted from the site procedure and last quarter's damage or waste figure, so the specialist's time goes to checking it on the floor.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly breach of an agreed damage or waste threshold on the finance extract can open a draft toolbox script. Someone still has to give the talk at the start of the shift.
lenses.ambitious: Done properly for the first time, each site would run one ten-minute talk tied to its own damage or waste figure, and L&D would look at that figure again eight weeks later.
lenses.joy: The generic slide deck is the part nobody will miss. Walking the dock and picking the one behaviour people will follow with gloves on is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Five ten-minute talks, on wrap waste, forklift battery care, loading damage, dock sorting and engine idling, can be drafted from the same procedure so the site picks the one that matches its number.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the rule for how a site figure becomes a ten-minute talk, and checks whether that figure moved, instead of writing a new course from scratch each year.
reach: The controller's damage and waste lines, turned into a talk a site manager can run at shift start.
The HR business partner's evidence when a customer asks which crews were trained and on which version of the procedure.

grok.human_edge: Seeing which waste is real on a night shift, and signing that the talk does not contradict the VCA rules or the food-safety procedure already in force on that site.
grok.pattern_why: The procedure and the cost line can feed a draft script and a quiz, and each quiz item can be checked back to a sentence in the procedure. Choosing the one behaviour, confirming it is safe next to VCA and food safety, and having it given on a shift, stays with the specialist and the site manager.

in_practice.trigger: Damage or waste cost on the AFAS extract crosses a threshold the controller agrees, a customer asks for proof of training, or the yearly check of the module comes due.
steps: Read the current site procedure on SharePoint and the last months of damage or waste cost from the finance extract.
Draft a ten-minute toolbox script and a short Studytube quiz that quote the procedure.
Have the site manager and L&D strike anything that conflicts with VCA or food safety.
Deliver it on one shift per site and record who attended.
Read the same cost line eight weeks later before writing anything new.
in_practice.human_gate: The site manager and the L&D specialist both approve the script before it is used. It becomes mandatory only if the HR Director decides so, after the works council is consulted where the change is a standing work instruction.
data_needed: The current waste, damage or fuel procedure on SharePoint
Damage, waste or fuel cost by site from the finance extract
VCA and food-safety instructions the script must not contradict
in_practice.logs_to: The script version stored on SharePoint next to the procedure, and the Studytube completion or the attendance list for the toolbox talk.

evidence.claim: Studytube can publish a short module with a quiz and record who completed it.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft a short document from a procedure the user opens in SharePoint, for a person to edit before anyone uses it.

On a warehouse floor, a ten-minute talk at shift start is more likely to change a handling habit than a yearly e-learning course, and the effect is visible only if a cost line is read again afterwards.
Damage and residual-waste costs are often already booked in the ledger as write-offs or claims, so a finance extract can supply the outcome line if the accounts are identifiable.

risks: A talk written from a generic model can contradict the site's VCA or food-safety procedure, which is worse than no talk.
Without a damage or waste line that finance already trusts, the module becomes another Studytube item with a completion rate and no result.
Tracking who failed to recycle, person by person, would be workplace monitoring and needs an AVG purpose; a crew-level cost line does not.
Making the talk mandatory, or changing how people must work, can be a matter for the works council if it becomes a standing instruction.
This is a small, low-frequency task; a heavy build will cost more than the hours it replaces.

Report participation for audits or customer questions

opus.pattern_why: Unstructured source documents become a structured course, quiz and translations inside the Studytube workflow, with a person approving before release.

Language profile of the target group

probe.rule_why: judging, creating or advising: the person stays the lead

opus.short: Build the monthly HR and flex reports for the HR Director, site managers and the works council from AFAS and Power BI.

today.trigger: Calendar: month close, MT meeting, quarterly OR meeting, or an ad-hoc request from a manager or the HR Director.
steps: Check that the nightly AFAS extract in Power BI refreshed and the numbers match AFAS
Export headcount, verzuim, hires and flex hours to Excel per site
Merge agency portal hours and Recruitee pipeline data by hand
Write commentary on what moved and why
Paste charts into PowerPoint or Word and mail them out
drudgery: Copying the same charts into slides every month
Reconciling agency hours with AFAS cost centres
Rewording the same commentary
today.time_sinks: Data checks and manual merging of agency and Recruitee data take more time than the analysis; one-off requests interrupt the planned work.

lenses.faster: Standard reports come from one Power BI model that already joins AFAS, Recruitee and agency data; an LLM drafts the commentary from the month-on-month changes, and the analyst edits it in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh passes its data checks at month close, the report pack builds itself and waits for the analyst's sign-off before it goes out.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager gets a monthly one-page report on their own team: verzuim, 90-day retention, flex share and open roles, with the three things that need action.
lenses.joy: No more pasting screenshots into slides; the analyst spends the time on the question behind the numbers.
lenses.options: For an ad-hoc request the analyst gets three report angles (by site, by shift, by contract type) and picks the one that answers the question.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the report catalogue, the metric definitions and the commentary rules instead of producing each report.
reach: Monthly management commentary that HR Business Partners now write
Flex labour cost reporting that FP&A Analysts compile
OR information pack the HR Director assembles

opus.human_edge: Knowing which number will trigger a difficult conversation with a site manager or the OR, and framing it so it leads to action rather than defence.
opus.pattern_why: Data extraction and charts are deterministic Power BI work; only the written commentary is unstructured and needs an LLM inside a fixed pipeline with human sign-off.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh succeeds on the first working day after month close.
steps: Power BI runs data quality checks (row counts, totals versus AFAS payroll journal)
Paginated report pack renders per audience
LLM drafts commentary from the variance table, citing the figures it used
Analyst reviews, edits and approves
Power Automate distributes to the mailing list and SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves commentary and figures before distribution; reports for the OR are also checked by the HR Director.
data_needed: AFAS headcount, contracts, absence and payroll extract
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint report archive with version, approver and date; Power BI refresh history.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report pages.
Power BI paginated reports and subscriptions can distribute reports on a schedule.
LLM commentary drafted from a variance table saves most of the writing time while the analyst still checks it.

risks: LLM commentary states a cause that is not in the data
Small-team figures in site reports identify individuals (AVG/GDPR), especially absence data
Agency data arrives late and the pack goes out incomplete
research_questions: How many hours per month go into standard versus ad-hoc reports today?
Can the three agency portals deliver hours data in a machine-readable export on a fixed date?
Does the OR accept AI-drafted commentary if the analyst signs it, and does it want this noted?
What minimum group size must reports use to avoid identifying employees in absence figures?

sol.short: Produce HR reports showing hiring, onboarding, retention, absence and workforce costs across our three sites.

today.trigger: A scheduled management report or a request from HR, Finance or a site manager.
steps: Check the nightly AFAS extract and retrieve recruitment or training data needed for the report.
Reconcile employee counts, dates and site assignments across the sources.
Calculate agreed measures in Power BI or Excel.
Investigate unusual movements and write an explanation.
Check access and distribute the report to its intended audience.
drudgery: Repeating exports and reconciliations
Copying figures into management updates
Explaining the same metric definitions repeatedly
today.time_sinks: Custom cuts by site, shift and contract type; inconsistent definitions; checking whether apparent movements are data errors.

lenses.faster: Scheduled data loads and reusable measures replace exports, spreadsheet calculations and formatting. AI drafts commentary from validated aggregates, with links to the figures behind each claim.
lenses.autonomous: After a successful refresh, standard reports run and reach approved audiences automatically. Failed checks stop distribution and create an exception for me.
lenses.ambitious: Follow every hiring cohort through day 90 by site, role and recruitment channel. Show productive retained hires alongside time to hire so faster recruitment does not hide poor outcomes.
lenses.joy: Remove copying and formatting. Keep the conversations about why a cohort struggled and what managers can change.
lenses.options: Generate alternative views by site, shift, channel and employment type using the same definitions. Compare operational and executive presentations without rebuilding calculations.
lenses.altitude: I own the reporting definitions, checks and distribution rules. I spend more time testing whether the reports lead to useful decisions.
reach: Prepare recurring workforce reporting for HR Business Partners
Supply reconciled workforce cost inputs to FP&A
Prepare aggregate evidence for works council discussions

sol.human_edge: Agreeing what productive means for different jobs, interpreting operational causes and deciding which findings deserve management attention.
sol.pattern_why: Standard calculations and publication rules are checkable and should run without a model. An optional llm_step can draft commentary, but its claims must match approved figures.

in_practice.trigger: A successful nightly refresh or a scheduled reporting deadline.
steps: Load available AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data through approved interfaces.
Check freshness, join coverage, totals and cohort eligibility before calculating measures.
Generate standard reports from approved definitions and suppress small groups under the agreed disclosure policy.
Draft commentary using only validated aggregates and flag unexplained changes.
Distribute approved standard reports and send novel requests or failed checks to the analyst.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve definitions, audiences and templates before activation; review novel reports and substantive AI commentary before publication.
data_needed: Vacancy, offer, start and exit dates
Agreed productivity milestones and day-90 cohort rules
Site, role, shift and employment type
Approved absence and workforce cost definitions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint reporting register recording refresh time, checks, definition version, recipients and approvals.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh, reusable measures and report subscriptions.
The proposed savings are planning estimates; Noordhaven's integrations and review workload have not been measured.

risks: Productivity or retention definitions can distort the North Star, especially when recent hires have not reached day 90.
Small site or shift groups can reveal personal information even in aggregate reports.
AI commentary can imply causes that the data does not establish.
Nightly data cannot support claims about live staffing.
research_questions: How many reporting hours go to exports and formatting versus interpretation and approval?
Can recruitment records be reliably linked to AFAS hires and agreed productivity milestones?
Which reports can use preapproved templates, and which require review every time?
What access and small-group disclosure rules have HR and the privacy owner agreed?

drudgery: Rebuilding the same monthly tables and the FTE bridge in Excel

today.time_sinks: The time goes into definition clashes at month close and into rebuilding packs that differ only by site, CAO and fixed versus flex.

lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the report calendar and the definitions behind it, and reviews the release. The generation of the standard pages leaves the desk.

The controller's monthly FTE bridge

Tell colleagues where to find things

Keeping definitions in sync with the Power BI model

lenses.joy: No filing; the analyst decides which definition wins.

sol.short: Keep HR reporting templates, definitions and reusable analysis assets current.

today.trigger: An asset changes, a new reusable item is created or a periodic library review is due.
steps: Locate relevant templates, definitions, queries and guidance.
Check ownership, approval status and current versions.
Compare duplicates and identify stale material.
Update metadata, links and review dates.
Archive superseded assets and notify affected users.
drudgery: Searching for the latest approved version
Fixing broken links and missing metadata
Chasing owners for routine reviews
today.time_sinks: 53.3 hours a year; finding, labelling and checking existing assets are the main assumed sinks.

lenses.faster: Automatically index assets, suggest metadata and detect duplicates, broken links and overdue reviews.
lenses.autonomous: A changed file or scheduled scan updates the catalogue and sends exceptions to the correct owner.
lenses.ambitious: Give every important metric, report and template a named owner, approved version, source lineage and review date.
lenses.joy: Remove library housekeeping so I can improve the assets people actually reuse.
lenses.options: Show approved variants by audience, site and CAO, with explicit applicability instead of near-duplicate files.
lenses.altitude: I design the knowledge lifecycle and ownership rules rather than maintain every entry manually.
reach: Maintain template catalogue metadata for HR administrators.
Support L&D with reusable reporting guides.
Help Finance catalogue shared workforce models.

sol.human_edge: Decide whether two assets are genuinely interchangeable and recognise when an apparent wording update changes contractual or policy meaning.
sol.pattern_why: Deterministic scans handle versions, links and review dates; a model proposes summaries and classifications within owner-controlled publishing rules.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised library changes or a scheduled catalogue scan runs.
steps: Inventory assets within existing permissions and read ownership and version metadata.
Check links, duplicates, review dates and references to superseded material.
Suggest searchable summaries, tags and related approved assets.
Apply permitted administrative metadata updates and route content changes to owners.
Mark superseded assets after approval and preserve required history and retention controls.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine checks and permitted metadata updates run automatically; owners approve content, applicability and archival decisions, especially for CAO, policy and contract assets.
data_needed: Links between metrics, reports and source definitions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint asset register with version history, scan findings, metadata changes, owner decisions and archival references.

evidence.claim: SharePoint provides document libraries, metadata, version history and content approval capabilities.
Power Automate can trigger workflows when SharePoint files are created or modified.

risks: An obsolete asset appears authoritative because its summary is current.
Search summaries reveal information beyond the reader's permissions.
Similar templates have different CAO or site applicability.
Automatic archival hides an asset still referenced by a live process or subject to retention requirements.
research_questions: What share of assets already has a reliable owner, approval status and review date?
Can indexing and search preserve existing document permissions throughout retrieval and summarisation?
Which metadata changes are safe to automate, and which require owner review?
Does a pilot reduce time spent finding approved assets without increasing incorrect reuse?

grok.short: Keep the metric dictionary and report templates up to date.

today.trigger: A definition changes, a template is copied and starts to diverge, or someone cannot find the current version of a report or a measure.
steps: Search SharePoint and the Power BI workspace for the current dictionary, the report template and the request form.
Update the definition, the owner and the source field, and archive the copy that is no longer current.
Tell the people who keep their own version: payroll for absence, recruiters for funnel stages, learning and development for certificates.
Chase the review that was due last quarter and never happened.
drudgery: Hunting 'final' and 'final v2' files
Copying one definition into the dictionary, the dashboard tooltip and the works council note
Reminding owners whose review date has passed
today.time_sinks: The hours go to finding which copy is current and to chasing owners, more than to writing the definition itself.

lenses.faster: The current file, the owner and the review date are already on the record. A changed measure proposes the dictionary update, and the search for the latest copy disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A review date, or a saved change to a measure, opens a proposed update. The old text stays in force until the analyst accepts the new one.
lenses.ambitious: Noordhaven would have one library for the North Star, the absence definition, the FTE bridge and the certificate rules, and private Excel definitions in payroll, recruitment and finance would lapse.
lenses.joy: Hunting for the latest file is the part nobody will miss. Writing a definition that a site manager and the works council will both accept is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: A proposed change can be stored as three wordings: the precise rule for the dictionary, the sentence for the dashboard, and the sentence for the works council.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the required fields and the review calendar for the library, and approves changes. Keeping the files in line becomes the system.
reach: Payroll's written rule for what counts as verzuim
The recruiters' definition of the Recruitee stages that count as an offer and a hire
Learning and development's rule for which roles require heftruck, VCA or food safety

grok.human_edge: Deciding that a definition has really changed, and getting payroll, the HR business partners and the works council onto that one version.
grok.pattern_why: The library rules, the review dates and the link to a changed measure can run without a model, and replacing a definition is the point where a person has to agree, because every report copies it.

in_practice.trigger: A measure changes in Power BI, a spec is accepted, or a dictionary review date falls due.
steps: Each asset has an owner, a review date, a source field, a version and the audiences that use it.
A change proposes a new version with the old text kept beside it and the reports that still use the old text listed.
The three wordings (rule, dashboard sentence, works council sentence) are drafted for the analyst to edit.
The analyst accepts the new version or sends it back. Acceptance retires the old file from the current folder.
Overdue reviews are listed each Monday until the owner confirms or the analyst escalates them.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst accepts every replacement of a definition. A change to verzuim, pay, FTE or the 90-day figure also needs the named owner, and the HR Director when the works council uses that figure.
data_needed: The list of current reports and measures, and who owns each
The field catalogue and the accepted specs
in_practice.logs_to: Version history on the SharePoint dictionary, including who accepted the version and which reports still pointed at the previous one.

evidence.claim: SharePoint version history and a required-column library can hold one current definition and keep the previous versions readable.
Power BI measures can carry a description, so the dashboard text and the dictionary can be checked for drift.
A scheduled comparison can list reports whose displayed definition differs from the dictionary. The organisational fact of whether owners will give up their private files is unproven here.

sol.short: Track HR technology changes and recommend improvements to hiring, onboarding, reporting and workforce administration.

today.trigger: Assumed company interpretation of the O*NET task: an HR technology review, vendor release or recurring process problem prompts research.
steps: Gather release notes, vendor information and relevant Dutch regulatory updates.
Check which changes apply to AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft 365.
Compare capabilities with Noordhaven's hiring, onboarding and reporting problems.
Estimate integration effort, costs and privacy or works council implications.
Write a recommendation and discuss priorities with the HR Director and affected specialists.
drudgery: Checking several vendor websites for changes.
Reading repeated marketing claims.
Copying feature descriptions into comparison spreadsheets.
Rechecking whether a feature is released, licensed and available in the Dutch environment.
today.time_sinks: Separating useful capabilities from sales claims and establishing whether a change actually fits Noordhaven's licences, interfaces, shift workers and Dutch obligations.

lenses.faster: Collect changes from a fixed source list, remove duplicates and draft a comparison with links to the original material. The analyst checks shortlisted changes instead of reading every announcement.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled scan creates an internal digest and flags changes that match recorded HR problems. Buying software, starting trials and changing employee processes remain human decisions.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a continuous improvement backlog tied to productive hires retained after 90 days. Evaluate small changes such as clearer onboarding handoffs before considering a major system replacement.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive searching and marketing summaries. Keep conversations with warehouse managers, hands-on trials and the judgment about what will help people on shifts.
lenses.options: For each problem, compare configuring an existing system, building a small integration, buying a tool, changing the process and leaving it unchanged. Show costs, dependencies and expected effects using the same assumptions.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the technology watchlist, evidence standard and trial scorecard. Their work becomes choosing and validating improvements across the HR system landscape.
reach: Prepare evidence briefs for the HR Director's technology priorities.
Help Recruiters and L&D Specialists assess features in Recruitee and Studytube.
Prepare integration and licence-cost assumptions for the Controller and FP&A Analysts.

sol.human_edge: The analyst judges fit with actual warehouse work, challenges vendor evidence and tests whether an improvement affects the North Star. HR leadership, IT and affected process owners retain decisions about investment and employee impact.

Have the analyst validate shortlisted claims and route any proposed trial or purchase to the responsible owners.

opus.short: Work out where we stand financially now and in three to twelve months: cash, margin, covenants.

steps: Pull trial balance and debtor/creditor ageing from AFAS Profit into Excel
Ask the FP&A Analysts for the latest forecast and flex worker cost run-rate
Rebuild the cash and covenant headroom view by hand
Check margin per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) against budget
Write a short view for the management team

Matching agency invoices to hours to get the real flex cost

lenses.faster: A nightly pipeline from AFAS and Rabobank keeps a 13-week cash and covenant view current, so the manual rebuild disappears.

lenses.ambitious: A rolling 18-month view per site and per large customer, refreshed weekly instead of a quarterly snapshot.
lenses.joy: No more copying exports; the Finance Director spends the time on what the numbers mean for the business.

Finance Director reviews, edits and releases

sol.short: Assess Noordhaven’s financial position and forecast cash, profit and funding needs across the three sites.

today.trigger: Monthly forecasting, a management question, or a material change in trading or cash.
steps: Pull actuals from the nightly AFAS extract and check the latest available period.
Collect volume, staffing and spending assumptions from the sites and FP&A.
Update Excel forecasts and reconcile them to the general ledger.
Investigate changes in margins, cash and working capital.
Explain the outlook and recommend action to management.
drudgery: Reconciling slightly different versions of actuals
Copying site assumptions into forecast workbooks
Rewriting explanations for recurring variances
today.time_sinks: Waiting for site assumptions and tracing differences between spreadsheets and the nightly extract.

lenses.faster: Reconciled actuals, calculated forecast movements and linked supporting records arrive together. Copying figures and assembling the first explanation disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Each successful nightly refresh updates approved forecast calculations and flags material changes. A new forecast remains a draft until its assumptions are approved.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling cash outlook and site-level downside scenarios between monthly closes. Test whether the forecast would have predicted previous cash and margin problems.
lenses.joy: Remove workbook repair and number chasing. Keep the conversations about what is changing in the business and which action matters.
lenses.options: Compare base, lower-volume, higher-agency-cost, slower-payment and combined-stress scenarios using the same reconciled starting point.
lenses.altitude: Design the forecasting rules, assumption ownership and quality checks. Review exceptions and forecast errors instead of rebuilding the analysis.
reach: FP&A Analyst: first-pass forecast consolidation and variance analysis
Controller: cross-site financial health checks

reach: Sales pricing support
Controller margin analysis

steps: Fetch diesel, CBS CPI and Euribor data
LLM extracts indexation clauses from SharePoint contracts into a table, checked once by a person
Calculate cost and margin effect per contract
Draft indexation letters and alerts
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director and Sales approve any price change before it goes to the customer.
in_practice.logs_to: Indexation register in SharePoint
