sol.short: Review market prices and securities transactions if Noordhaven has investments or related treasury exposure.

today.trigger: If applicable: a treasury review, an investment transaction or a material market-price change.
steps: Confirm which holdings, transactions or treasury exposures need review.
Collect authorised transaction reports and relevant dated price or rate information.
Reconcile holdings and transactions to financial records.
Assess valuation changes, concentration, liquidity and policy limits.
Explain material movements and recommend any action for approval.
systems: Rabobank reports where the relevant information is available
drudgery: Re-entering transaction details
Checking dates and units across price lists
Preparing repeated market-movement summaries
today.time_sinks: Obtaining comparable prices and separating market movement from transaction effects. No securities portfolio or market-data source was specified.

lenses.faster: Reconcile transactions and calculate price movements from approved sources automatically. Re-keying reports and normalising units disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Receipt of an authorised transaction report or dated market-data update triggers reconciliation and limit checks. Stale or missing prices stop valuation output.
lenses.ambitious: If exposure is material, monitor liquidity, concentration and policy limits between scheduled treasury reviews.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive price checking and table preparation. Keep judgement about treasury risk and whether action serves Noordhaven’s operating needs.
lenses.options: Compare holding cash, deposits and other policy-permitted instruments under interest-rate, liquidity and counterparty stress scenarios.
lenses.altitude: Set treasury policy, approved data sources and risk limits. Review exceptions rather than read every price list.
reach: Controller: treasury exposure and valuation monitoring
Accountant: transaction reconciliation and supporting valuation schedules
FP&A Analyst: sensitivity of cash income and funding costs to rate changes

sol.human_edge: Judge acceptable treasury risk, verify unfamiliar instruments and approve investment or hedging decisions within company authority.
sol.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic reconciliation and valuation checks prepare the assessment, with optional source-linked market summaries; people approve interpretations and any transaction.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised treasury statement, transaction report or approved market-data update.
steps: Verify the exposure scope, data permissions, timestamps, currencies and instrument identifiers.
Reconcile holdings and transactions to the approved ledger or treasury records.
Calculate movements and policy-limit checks using instrument-appropriate rules.
Prepare a source-linked exception and sensitivity report.
Obtain review before releasing recommendations or requesting any trade.
in_practice.human_gate: The director verifies material valuations and recommendations; authorised signatories approve trades or hedges. The workflow has no trade-execution authority.
systems: An approved market-data source to be confirmed
An approved language-model service for source-linked summaries
data_needed: Confirmed holdings, instruments and relevant treasury exposures
Approved prices or rates with timestamps and usage rights
Instrument valuation rules and currency conventions
Treasury policy, liquidity needs and counterparty limits
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint treasury register containing source timestamps, reconciliations, valuation-rule versions, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query supports importing and transforming authorised structured files for transaction and price comparisons.
Reconciliation and limit monitoring are plausible deterministic workflows when instrument data and valuation rules are available.
The proposed 65% effort saving and 2.5-times speedup are conditional estimates; neither a portfolio nor this workload is established.

risks: The task may have little relevance if Noordhaven holds no securities or related treasury exposure.
Stale prices, wrong identifiers or currency errors produce misleading valuations.
Simple price calculations are applied to instruments requiring specialist valuation.
Generated market commentary is mistaken for a supported forecast or authorised investment recommendation.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven hold securities or other relevant treasury exposures, and what work does the director actually perform?
Are holdings, transaction reports and licensed price data available in a usable format?
Which instruments can be valued with simple rules, and which require external expertise?
Would faster review change a material decision, or is the current review already sufficient?

grok.short: Check price lists and rates against margin and cash.

today.trigger: A new customer tariff, a carrier or agency price list, a diesel-surcharge change, or a change in the Rabobank rate.
steps: Save the list from mail into the contract folder on SharePoint.
Read the change: base rate, diesel clause, staangeld, agency fee or interest.
Compare it with the rate already in the forecast and in the customer or supplier agreement.
Work out the year effect on margin and, for interest, on cash.
Tell FP&A and, if it is material, the management team.
drudgery: Reading PDF rate cards and side letters that all use a different layout.
Re-doing the diesel-surcharge maths each time the reference price moves.
Hunting the current contractual rate because the forecast copy is old.
today.time_sinks: The time goes into finding the binding rate and turning a PDF into rows, not into the margin decision.

lenses.faster: A saved price list comes back as rows: rate, unit, surcharge, start date and euro effect. Re-keying and the first comparison disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A file added to the rate-card folder, or a known diesel reference move, starts the comparison without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would check every carrier, agency and customer rate against margin every month, which it now does when a list happens to arrive.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping tariffs. The useful remainder is the call on whether a surcharge is absorbed or reopened with the customer.
lenses.options: Each material change shows absorb, pass on, or reopen the contract, with margin and cash for the rest of the year.
lenses.altitude: The director sets which clauses matter, the euro threshold, and the rule that the forecast may use only registered rates.
reach: The FP&A update of the forecast rate.
Procurement's comparison of carrier tenders, as a finance check on margin.
The bookkeeper's check that an agency invoice uses the registered rate card.

grok.human_edge: Whether to absorb a diesel or carrier increase, or to reopen a customer rate, is a commercial decision made with sales. Finance supplies the checked effect; it does not own the relationship.
grok.pattern_why: Rate cards arrive as PDFs and mixed spreadsheets. The useful output is a structured table a person can tie back to the contract and to AFAS. The arithmetic after that is ordinary calculation.

in_practice.trigger: A rate card or term sheet is saved to the SharePoint contract folder, or the agreed diesel reference is updated.
steps: The job reads the file and extracts rate, unit, surcharge rule, start date and party.
A person checks the extracted rows against the PDF before they are stored.
The checked rows are compared with the forecast and with the last registered card.
Changes under the threshold update a watch list. Changes over it go to the director with three commercial options.
FP&A may change the forecast only from a registered card the director has released.
in_practice.human_gate: The director releases any rate change above the threshold before it enters the forecast or a customer position. Extraction errors are caught by the row check before that.
data_needed: Customer tariffs, carrier lists and the three agency rate cards
The diesel-surcharge clause and the reference series named in the contract
The rate version inside the live forecast
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint rate-card register, one row per party and start date, linked to the forecast version.

evidence.claim: Once rates are rows, Excel or Power BI can compute a margin and cash effect and tie it to a forecast version.
Microsoft Document Intelligence can extract tables from PDFs into rows a person then checks.
Dutch side letters on dieseltoeslag and staangeld are often messy enough that unchecked extraction will misstate the year effect.

risks: A misread surcharge clause posts a clean-looking margin bridge that is wrong for the whole year.
This O*NET line may be almost empty here if the company holds no securities and commercial owners keep the price lists.
A forecast fed from an unchecked PDF becomes the number the board later calls forecast accuracy.

Where do the binding price lists live, and what share are searchable text rather than scans or side letters?
How often does a rate-card change move margin by more than the threshold the director would act on?

opus.short: Follow diesel prices, interest rates and currency to see what they do to costs and the facility.

today.trigger: Monthly, and when diesel or interest moves sharply.
steps: Check diesel prices, Euribor and exchange rates
Compare with fuel surcharge clauses in customer contracts
Estimate the effect on margin and interest
Decide whether to adjust surcharges or hedge
Inform management
drudgery: Looking up prices on websites
Recalculating surcharges by hand
today.time_sinks: Manual data lookup and surcharge recalculation per contract.

lenses.faster: Price feeds land automatically and the effect on margin, surcharges and interest is calculated, with a short AI note.
lenses.autonomous: When diesel or rates cross a set threshold, the system calculates the surcharge change and alerts the Director and sales.
lenses.ambitious: Surcharges adjusted on time for every contract, and a clear view of interest risk on the facility.
lenses.joy: No more website lookups; the Director decides on hedging and pricing.
lenses.options: Scenarios for diesel and rate paths with surcharge and hedge options.
lenses.altitude: The Director sets the market risk policy and thresholds, and reviews whether surcharges recover costs.
reach: Sales: surcharge updates to customers
Controller: interest cost accruals

opus.human_edge: Hedging and pricing decisions, and talks with the bank and customers.
opus.pattern_why: Feeds and calculations are deterministic; the LLM writes a short checkable note; decisions stay human.

in_practice.trigger: Daily price feed and threshold breaches.
steps: Load diesel, Euribor and FX data
Calculate surcharge and interest effects per contract
LLM drafts a short market note
Director decides on surcharge changes or hedging
in_practice.human_gate: Surcharge changes and hedges need the Director's approval.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint market risk log

11-3031.01:8861.statement: Receive, record, and authorize requests for disbursements in accordance with company policies and procedures.

probe.rule_why: judging, creating or advising: the person stays the lead

opus.short: Check and approve invoices, agency bills and payment batches above my limit before Rabobank pays them.

today.trigger: Supplier invoices, staffing agency invoices and expense claims land in the AFAS approval workflow; the weekly payment batch is ready for sign-off.
steps: Open the invoices waiting for controller approval in AFAS Profit
Check each against the purchase order, contract or agency hours in the agency portal
Chase budget holders on Teams or Outlook for missing approvals or cost centres
Approve or reject in AFAS and note the reason
Review and sign the payment batch in Rabobank internet banking
drudgery: Matching agency invoice lines to hours worked per flex worker, site and week
Chasing site managers for approvals
Re-checking IBAN changes and duplicate invoices by hand
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices from three agencies with different layouts and hourly rate tables, which swing with the season (150 to 300 flex workers).

lenses.faster: Invoices that match PO, contract rate and agency hours arrive pre-checked with a green flag, so the controller only reads the exceptions instead of every line.
lenses.autonomous: Each new invoice in AFAS triggers a check against policy, approval matrix, PO and agency hours; clean ones under the threshold go straight to the batch.
lenses.ambitious: Every agency invoice checked line by line against CAO rates, shift allowances and actual clock hours, recovering overbilling that today slips through.
lenses.joy: No more scrolling through agency PDFs; the controller keeps the judgement calls on odd spend and new suppliers.
lenses.options: For a disputed agency invoice, the system proposes pay in full, short-pay with credit note request, or hold, with the euro effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the approval matrix and matching rules and reviews a monthly report of what was auto-approved and why.
reach: Bookkeeper first-line invoice coding
Credit and Collections Officer supplier dispute follow-up
HR Administrator check of flex worker hours

opus.human_edge: Saying no to a manager's spend, judging unusual or first-time payments, and signing the bank batch as the person accountable under the four-eyes rule.
opus.pattern_why: Several sources (AFAS, agency portals, contracts) and messy exceptions; the match itself is rule-based but the agency invoices need extraction, and payment release must stay with a person.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice registered in AFAS Profit or agency invoice received by e-mail.
steps: Extract invoice lines and match to PO, contract rates and agency hours
Apply approval matrix and fraud checks (IBAN change, duplicate, new supplier)
Route clean invoices under threshold to the batch; flag exceptions with a short reason
Controller approves exceptions and signs the Rabobank batch
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every flagged invoice and every payment batch; bank release keeps two signatures.
data_needed: Agency rate cards per CAO function group
Hours per flex worker from agency portals
Open POs and supplier master data
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS Profit workflow history plus an exception log in SharePoint for the auditor

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit has configurable workflows for invoice approval with mandate limits.
LLMs can extract line items from varied invoice layouts reliably enough for matching with human review of mismatches.

risks: Payment fraud through changed supplier IBANs if checks are trusted blindly
Auto-approval drifting past mandate limits if the matrix is not maintained
Auditor rejects the control if the log is not complete
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices would have matched PO and rates without any touch?
Do the three agency portals export hours per worker in a usable format or only PDF?
How much overbilling did a manual sample of agency invoices find last year?
Will the external auditor accept rule-based auto-approval under a threshold as a key control?

sol.short: Check payment requests, record the decision and approve spending within my authority.

today.trigger: A payment request or invoice arrives for controller approval.
steps: Collect the request, invoice, budget code and evidence of receipt.
Check the supplier, amount, possible duplicates and approval authority.
Ask the requester or bookkeeper to resolve missing information.
Approve or reject the expenditure and record the reason.
Pass approved items into the payment process with separate bank authorization.
drudgery: Finding attachments and earlier approvals
Repeated checks of limits and budget codes
Chasing incomplete requests
today.time_sinks: Missing evidence and unclear approval ownership cause repeated handoffs between sites, finance and requesters.

lenses.faster: Validate required fields, duplicates and approval limits automatically. Present one evidence pack so I only investigate exceptions and judge the expenditure.
lenses.autonomous: An AFAS workflow checks each submitted request and routes it under the approved authority matrix. Routine checks run without reminders; payment release follows the bank mandate.
lenses.ambitious: Check every request for split purchases, repeated exceptions and unusual supplier changes. Use the findings to improve purchasing controls across all three sites.
lenses.joy: Remove attachment hunting and approval chasing. Keep the conversations about whether spending is justified and how to prevent recurring problems.
lenses.options: For a problematic request, show rejection, correction, deferral and escalation options with their cash and operational consequences.
lenses.altitude: I maintain the approval rules, review exceptions and test whether the control system catches real errors.
reach: Bookkeeper: resolve recurring invoice intake problems
Accountant: test purchasing controls and preserve approval evidence
Finance Director: propose changes to delegated spending limits

sol.human_edge: Judging commercial necessity, conflicts of interest and exceptions remains a human responsibility. Spending approval and bank release must remain separate where policy requires it.
sol.pattern_why: agent_with_gate fits document collection, validation and exception routing before controller approval. deterministic_software handles limits and duplicate checks; an llm_step can extract document fields for validation.

in_practice.trigger: A request enters the AFAS approval queue.
steps: Extract request fields and attach links to the original evidence.
Run deterministic completeness, duplicate, budget and authority checks.
Route missing information to the requester and flag supplier bank changes for independent verification.
Present the controller with the proposed decision and failed checks.
Record the approved decision in AFAS and pass eligible items to the separate payment workflow.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves expenditure within delegated authority; higher amounts go to the Finance Director. Rabobank release requires the authorized signatories.
data_needed: Supplier master data and change history
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS approval history, with evidence references and validation results in a restricted SharePoint control register.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports purchasing invoice processing and approval workflows; the available configuration must be checked.
The proposed document extraction and exception workflow could reduce controller handling effort by about 60%; this is an untested estimate.

risks: False duplicate matches or incorrect extracted amounts block legitimate payments.
A changed supplier bank account could enable payment fraud if verification is automated away.
Combining requester, approver and bank release permissions defeats segregation of duties.
Document content could manipulate an AI step unless documents are treated only as input data.
research_questions: What proportion of requests is complete on arrival, and how many minutes does each approval take?
Can the AFAS configuration expose documents, workflow status and approval limits with a usable audit history?
Which spending exceptions require controller judgment, and which checks can be expressed as fixed rules?
How are supplier bank changes and Rabobank signatory separation verified today?

grok.short: Approve payment requests that sit above the bookkeepers' mandate.

today.trigger: A bookkeeper routes a disbursement the mandate does not let them release: a supplier invoice, a flex-agency invoice, a credit note, or a one-off payment request.
steps: Open the AFAS workflow item and the PDF invoice or request.
Check the purchase order, goods receipt, cost centre, VAT code and whether the amount sits inside policy.
For a flex-agency invoice, compare hours and rates with the agency portal, usually by retyping totals into Excel.
Send gaps back to the site or the bookkeeper, or approve and record the coding.
Co-sign the SEPA batch that AFAS sends to Rabobank.
drudgery: Opening invoices the match already explains
Re-keying agency hours into a side sheet
Chasing Tilburg, Venlo and Rotterdam for a missing receipt
Ticking duplicates and VAT codes one by one
today.time_sinks: Most of the 147 hours sit in exceptions and in agency invoices that do not match the portal, plus waiting on site managers before a batch can be released.

lenses.faster: The match to order, receipt, mandate, VAT, duplicate and IBAN is finished before the item reaches the controller, so the queue is the failures only. Coding and the policy clause travel with the item, and the retyping into Excel drops out.
lenses.autonomous: An in-policy invoice that matches posts to the ledger and joins the payment proposal when the receipt is booked, with no daily prompt to the controller. A failed rule opens a task on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would tie every agency line to portal hours and every warehouse receipt to the invoice in the same week, including the small invoices that now pass unread.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss confirming a match the system has already made. What remains is a real dispute: a haulier rate, a damaged delivery, a site that ordered outside the contract.
lenses.options: Each exception arrives with the treatments the mandate allows, such as pay, split across site cost centres, hold for a receipt, or return, each with the euro effect and the policy line.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the mandate matrix, the match tolerances and the weekly sample of auto-released payments, and stops clearing items the rules already cover.
reach: The bookkeepers' exception coding on purchase invoices
First-line review of the three agencies' weekly invoices
The accountant's accrual for received-not-invoiced warehouse deliveries

grok.human_edge: Noticing a request that passes the written rules and is still wrong: a changed IBAN on a known haulier, a May volume spike that the shifts do not support, or a site manager approving spend they raised themselves.
grok.pattern_why: The check is a rule, but the money moves only after a recorded decision, and agency PDFs, missing receipts and new suppliers are genuine exceptions. An agent can assemble the evidence across AFAS, the portals and Rabobank; a person clears what failed before it enters the batch.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice or payment request is booked in AFAS, or a nightly match job flags an agency invoice against the portal export.
steps: AFAS pulls the order, receipt, supplier, VAT code and mandate limit.
Rules test three-way match, duplicate, VAT, cost-centre rights and whether the IBAN equals the master record.
Flex invoices are matched to the agency export of hours and agreed rates.
Clean items inside mandate post and enter the payment proposal. Exceptions open a task with the failed rule and the policy line.
The controller decides the exception. A second authorised person releases the Rabobank batch.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller decides every exception, every supplier IBAN change and a weekly sample of auto-released payments. A different authorised user releases the SEPA batch in Rabobank.
data_needed: Written mandate matrix by amount, cost centre and site
Open purchase orders and goods receipts
Supplier master IBANs and VAT numbers
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS workflow log, kept with the weekly sample so the external auditor can re-perform the match.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can route a purchase invoice, match it to an order and a receipt, and build a payment proposal from approved items.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit purchase-to-pay and payment proposal (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: Rabobank business banking accepts SEPA batches and returns statements that a ledger can import.
evidence.source: Rabobank Business Banking batch payments and CAMT/MT940 statements (named product, model knowledge)

evidence.claim: A large share of Dutch mid-market invoice fraud is a changed supplier IBAN sent by mail, so the IBAN check has to stay outside the invoice approval itself.

risks: Auto-release without a mandate the Finance Director has signed, and without a stored sample, will fail the four-eyes test the auditor expects.
An IBAN change that rides inside an invoice approval is the usual payment-fraud path; it has to stay a separate dual-controlled master-data change.
Agency PDFs name individual flex workers. That file stays in AFAS and the tenant, under AVG, and does not go into a public chat tool.
Inlenersbeloning disputes are an HR and CAO question. Finance can flag a rate that does not match the contract and should not invent the legal rate.

Where is a supplier IBAN changed today, and can that change be entered from the same screen as the invoice approval?
Can each of the three agency portals produce an hour-and-rate export AFAS can match, or only a PDF?
What mandate thresholds and cost-centre rights are actually written down, and who last signed them?

today.trigger: A large outflow is coming, the balance sits above the operating need, or the Finance Director asks whether to draw or repay the facility.
steps: Build a cash forecast from AFAS open items, the payroll calendar, agency orders and the Rabobank balance.

sol.short: Run the planning cycle and align site budgets, purchasing and investment decisions.

Request site inputs and check their completeness.

Discuss trade-offs with site managers and finance colleagues.
Obtain decisions, assign actions and track completion.

Comparing spreadsheet versions
Rewriting meeting actions

today.trigger: The annual budget round starts, a site asks for equipment or extra flex, or a quarterly reforecast is due.
steps: Issue the timetable and the templates to FP&A, the accountants and the three site managers.
Chase Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for volume, headcount, overtime and flex assumptions.
Review procurement commitments and investment proposals against the budget and the cash view.
Consolidate versions in Excel and sit with FP&A until the bridge explains.
Present the pack to the Finance Director and record the decisions.
drudgery: Merging site workbooks that do not use the same cost centres
Chasing version numbers by mail
Rebuilding the bridge after one site changes volume
today.time_sinks: The cycle slips on site assumptions and on meetings, not on the arithmetic. Consolidation and the story of the bridge take the rest of the 69 hours.

lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would reforecast the three sites on the same drivers every quarter, and would cost a warehouse investment properly the first time, including flex, maintenance and cash.

lenses.options: Each investment proposal comes with a low, base and high volume case and the effect on the year, the cash low point and the site result.

in_practice.trigger: The planning calendar reaches a budget, reforecast or investment deadline, or a proposal is submitted in SharePoint.
steps: Open the round with a locked chart of accounts, cost centres per site and a template filled from last year's actuals.

Build the consolidated result, cash and headcount, and a bridge from the previous approved version.
Score each investment proposal for completeness: cost, timing, site, payback and whether works-council advice is required.
The controller reviews the bridge with FP&A and takes the open assumptions to the Finance Director.
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director approves the budget and any investment above the mandate. The controller approves the pack that is allowed into that meeting. A proposal that changes work in a warehouse is flagged for the works council route before it is treated as approved.

opus.short: Answer site managers' and department heads' questions on budget rules, cost codes, approvals and spending control.

today.trigger: A Teams message or mail from a site manager, HR or operations lead asking how to book, budget or approve something.
steps: Read the question and find the relevant policy on SharePoint
Check the cost centre or budget position in AFAS or Power BI
Write an answer or call the person
Sometimes update the policy or a FAQ after repeated questions
drudgery: Answering the same questions about cost codes and approval limits each month
Looking up budget remaining for a cost centre by hand
today.time_sinks: Repeated questions from three sites, and pulling budget-versus-actual for one cost centre on request.

lenses.options: For a manager facing an overrun, the assistant drafts three options (shift budget, defer spend, accept overrun with a reason) with the effect on the site forecast.

reach: FP&A Analyst: routine budget-versus-actual explanations to budget holders

sol.short: Help site managers apply finance policies and make sound spending and budget decisions.

today.trigger: A manager asks about spending, budget ownership, coding, credit terms or an exception to policy.
steps: Clarify the question and identify the relevant site, budget and decision owner.
Find the current policy in SharePoint and supporting figures in AFAS or Power BI.
Work through the financial effect and explain the applicable procedure.
Agree the action, obtain any required approval and record the advice.
drudgery: Finding the latest approved policy and repeating familiar explanations.
Copying budget figures into emails and chasing missing context.
today.time_sinks: Switching between documents and figures, then clarifying incomplete requests.

lenses.faster: Prepare a response with the relevant policy clause, current budget position and a worked example. The controller checks the interpretation instead of searching and assembling the answer.

lenses.ambitious: Offer each site a regular finance clinic using recurring questions and actual budget exceptions. Improve procedures before the same mistake appears across all three sites.
lenses.joy: Remove document hunting and repeated explanations. Keep the conversations where understanding the operation changes the financial decision.
lenses.options: Show compliant alternatives such as delaying expenditure, reallocating an approved budget or seeking an exception. State the cost, approval route and operational trade-off for each.
lenses.altitude: Own the quality of financial guidance: policy clarity, exception patterns and whether managers can apply the rules themselves.
reach: Take on routine budget-holder training currently supported by the Finance Director.
Help FP&A turn recurring manager questions into clearer budget guidance.

sol.human_edge: Understanding a site's constraints, challenging a manager constructively and accepting responsibility for sensitive advice.

Present the draft to the controller and record the approved response.

Save the answer in the mail thread, where the next person cannot find it.

Rebuilding a small actuals table that the nightly extract already holds.

work_activities: Manage control system activities in organizations.

probe.rule_why: several steps over a stream of cases, with exceptions

opus.short: Prepare for and coordinate the year-end audit and internal checks on accounts and transactions.

today.trigger: Year-end audit planning by the external auditor, or an internal control review.
steps: Receive the auditor's request list (PBC list)
Gather reconciliations, contracts, invoices and payroll evidence from AFAS and SharePoint
Assign items to accountants and bookkeepers and chase them
Answer auditor questions and agree adjustments
drudgery: Pulling samples of invoices and payment proofs one by one
Chasing colleagues for evidence
Tracking the PBC list in Excel
today.time_sinks: Collecting and matching evidence for samples, and the back-and-forth with the auditor on open items.

lenses.faster: An agent pulls sample evidence (invoice, PO, payment from the Rabobank statement) from AFAS and SharePoint and assembles it per PBC item, so the controller only reviews.
lenses.autonomous: Continuous checks run monthly: duplicate payments, vendor bank account changes, journal entries posted by unusual users or outside hours, payroll to AFAS headcount.
lenses.ambitious: Full-population testing of payments and journals instead of samples, so audit adjustments drop and the auditor relies more on internal controls.
lenses.joy: No more digging through folders for a 2025 invoice; the controller focuses on the judgement items the auditor raises.
lenses.options: For each audit finding, AI drafts alternative remediation plans with effort and risk reduction.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the control-testing rules and the evidence library, and reviews exceptions rather than gathering.
reach: Accountant: preparing balance sheet reconciliations for audit
Bookkeeper: answering sample requests on AP and AR

opus.human_edge: Negotiating with the auditor on judgement items, deciding which adjustments to accept, and signing off as the responsible person.
opus.pattern_why: Several steps across systems with exceptions; evidence packs and test results must be reviewed by the controller before they go to the auditor.

in_practice.trigger: Auditor uploads a PBC list or sample selection; monthly control tests on the closing calendar.
steps: Agent parses the PBC list and sample selection
Retrieves documents and ledger lines from AFAS, SharePoint and bank statements
Builds evidence folders and marks missing items with an owner
Runs rule-based tests over the full population and lists exceptions
Controller reviews and releases to the auditor
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every evidence pack and every exception explanation before sharing with the auditor.
in_practice.logs_to: PBC tracker on SharePoint with status and reviewer per item

evidence.claim: Rule-based full-population tests on journals and payments are established audit analytics practice.
An LLM agent can assemble evidence packs from document stores against a request list.

risks: Wrong document attached to a sample undermines auditor trust
Payroll evidence contains personal data, so AVG/GDPR access limits apply
Auditor may not accept AI-assembled evidence without a clear trail
research_questions: Will the external auditor accept evidence packs and full-population tests prepared this way?
What share of PBC items can be retrieved from AFAS and SharePoint without manual search?
How many hours did the last audit take internally, by item type?

sol.short: Coordinate audit evidence and test whether financial controls work.

today.trigger: An external accountant's request list, an internal review or a significant financial control incident.
steps: Agree the review scope, applicable Dutch requirements and evidence requests.
Collect ledger extracts, reconciliations, invoices, approvals and supporting records.
Select or support selection of transactions and trace them through the process.
Investigate exceptions with process owners and document findings.
Coordinate responses and track corrective actions.
drudgery: Renaming and indexing evidence files.
Answering duplicate requests and chasing missing approvals.
Repeating completeness checks across extracts and folders.
today.time_sinks: Locating evidence, demonstrating its completeness and coordinating responses across owners.

lenses.faster: Match audit requests to existing evidence and build an indexed pack with transaction references. Automated checks identify missing records before the controller starts reviewing.
lenses.autonomous: An approved request list can trigger evidence collection and completeness checks within defined access limits. Exceptions and unclear requests enter a controller review queue.
lenses.ambitious: Run agreed control checks throughout the year, covering complete transaction populations where suitable. Resolve recurring weaknesses before the annual audit.
lenses.joy: Remove file chasing, duplicate requests and evidence formatting. Keep investigation, professional challenge and improvements to the control environment.
lenses.options: Compare control tests by coverage, expected effort and the failure they could detect. Let the controller and external auditor choose the appropriate approach.
lenses.altitude: Own evidence quality and remediation effectiveness instead of personally assembling every audit folder.
reach: Coordinate the accountants' recurring evidence submissions.
Give the Finance Director a current view of control findings and overdue remediation.

sol.human_edge: Assessing materiality, challenging suspicious explanations and exercising professional scepticism; the external auditor retains independent audit judgments.
sol.pattern_why: Agent with gate: evidence assembly and defined tests are checkable, while scope, exceptions and conclusions require accountable professional review.

in_practice.trigger: An approved audit request list or a scheduled internal control test.
steps: Map each request to an owner, period, evidence source and access restriction.
Collect read-only records and reconcile population totals to AFAS.
Run approved checks and index original evidence with stable references.
Draft findings that distinguish missing evidence from demonstrated control failures.
Route the pack for review and track agreed remediation.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves findings and evidence release; the external auditor determines their own scope, sampling, reliance and audit opinion.
data_needed: Audit requests, control descriptions and agreed test definitions
Complete transaction populations and reconciliation totals
Prior findings, remediation owners and deadlines
Applicable reporting framework and retention requirements
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint audit register containing evidence references, extraction dates, test versions, results, reviewer decisions and remediation status.

evidence.claim: Structured exports can support repeatable completeness, duplicate and approval checks, provided population integrity is established.
AI-assisted evidence indexing and draft findings do not establish audit assurance or replace an external auditor's judgment.

risks: An incomplete export passes every test and creates false reassurance.
Generated summaries misrepresent evidence or treat a missing record as proof of wrongdoing.
Payroll and bank records are exposed through an overly broad audit workspace.
Automated selections or workpapers do not meet the external auditor's requirements.
research_questions: Which recurring requests account for most preparation and follow-up time?
Can completeness be reconciled to independently established AFAS totals?
Will the external auditor accept the proposed evidence format and traceability?
Can seeded missing approvals and duplicate transactions be detected without excessive false alarms?

today.trigger: The external accountant starts interim or year-end work, the Belastingdienst asks for support, or a finding from last year is still open.
steps: Agree the request list and the samples with the auditor.
Pull journals, revenue cutoff, agency accruals and bank lines from AFAS into Excel.
Chase Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for proof of delivery, timesheets and agency hour backing.
Explain exceptions on cutoff, VAT on transport and the flex accrual.
Track findings and draft the management response for the finance director.
drudgery: Renaming exports to the request-list index.
Tying sample invoices back to the general ledger.
Chasing the same missing warehouse document across three sites.
today.time_sinks: The file waits on sites and on the three staffing agencies, and several versions of the same tie-out sit in the folder.

lenses.faster: The population, the sample and the tie-out to the ledger are prepared from AFAS with the selection rule written on the file. Building the sample workbook disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A new auditor request, or a posting on a watch-list, opens the file and lists the missing documents. Manual journals, late revenue and agency invoices without hours are the watch-list.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, journals, VAT codes, three-way match and bank reconciliations would be tested on the full population every month, and the year-end sample would be a check on that work.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses renaming files to a request list. The work worth keeping is explaining a real cutoff or VAT judgment to the auditor.
lenses.options: Each finding can carry three responses: correct the posting, disagree with the evidence attached, or add a compensating check, each with the effect on the audit-adjustment count.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the control list and the monthly tests, and reviews the exceptions that go to the auditor.
reach: The sample tie-outs the bookkeepers now prepare for the auditor.
A first draft of the management-letter replies the finance director now writes.
A clear request to the payroll specialist for wage-cost totals, leaving employee detail in AFAS.

grok.human_edge: What the company states to the statutory auditor and to the Belastingdienst, and whether a finding is accepted.
grok.pattern_why: Samples and tie-outs follow written rules and come out of AFAS. Anything sent outside the company is a statement of the company, so the controller approves the file first. The external accountant forms the opinion.

in_practice.trigger: The external auditor opens a request, the Belastingdienst asks for support, or a watch-list posting appears during the month.
steps: Build the population from AFAS and draw the sample with the selection rule stored on the file.
Tie each item to the invoice, the contract, the proof of delivery or the Rabobank line.
List documents still missing from the sites or the staffing agencies.
The controller reviews the exceptions and sends the file.
Log the finding and the management response against the control it belongs to.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves every file before it is sent. The external accountant remains responsible for the opinion in the wettelijke controle.
data_needed: A locked trial balance and the journal listing
Revenue cutoff support and agency hour backing
The bank reconciliation and the payment-batch log
in_practice.logs_to: The year's audit folder on SharePoint, with sample parameters, the sender and the date.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can produce an XML auditfile of the ledger in the Dutch auditfile format that auditors and the Belastingdienst use.
MindBridge analyses a full general-ledger population and flags unusual entries for auditors.
Whether Noordhaven's external accountant will rely on a company-drawn sample depends on the engagement, and is untested here.

risks: A tie-out that does not reperform will add findings.
Full-population tests can flood the close with false exceptions and create false comfort.
Payroll and flex-worker lines in a sample are personal data under the AVG and stay restricted to the people who already handle them.
The EU AI Act does not move the auditor's duty. A model output is company preparation, and the accountant does their own work.

in_practice.trigger: The controller releases a versioned year-end ledger snapshot for tax preparation.
steps: Import the trial balance and supporting schedules using adviser-approved mappings.
Calculate reconciliations and book-to-tax bridges using maintained rules.
Extract supporting facts from documents and flag uncertain classifications.
Build the evidence-linked tax pack and a list of unresolved questions.
Obtain controller and adviser review before any authorised filing.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves source-data completeness; the external tax adviser validates tax treatment and the designated authorised person approves filing. The workflow has no filing credentials.
data_needed: Final trial balance, year-end adjustments and entity scope
Prior-year return, tax schedules and adviser request list
Fixed-asset, provision and other relevant supporting schedules
Current tax rules and positions validated by the adviser
Documented book-to-tax mappings and unresolved judgments

risks: Outdated rules or incorrect entity assumptions produce an incorrect tax position.
A late journal changes balances after the pack has been reviewed.
Model-generated explanations imply support that the evidence does not establish.

Can every schedule reconcile to the final ledger and prior-year opening position?

grok.short: Prepare the year-end figures so the adviser can file the tax return.

today.trigger: The year-end ledger is closed and the external adviser sends the information request for the vennootschapsbelasting return.
steps: Export the trial balance from AFAS and rebuild the commercial-to-fiscal bridge in Excel.
List depreciation differences, non-deductible costs, mixed costs and provisions.
Tie wage cost in the ledger to the payroll returns with the payroll specialist.
Summarise the VAT returns and any suppletie, and send the pack to the adviser.
Answer follow-up questions and read the draft return before it is filed.
drudgery: Copying account codes into last year's bridge.
Retyping permanent differences that did not change.
Collecting invoices for small non-deductible items.
today.time_sinks: The trial balance still moves after it was called final, and the wage-cost tie-out waits on payroll.

lenses.faster: Once the year-end periods lock, the trial balance, the fiscal bridge and the tie-out to the VAT returns and the wage-cost totals are assembled from the mapping. Rebuilding the Excel bridge disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Locking the year-end periods opens the pack and lists movements on timing and permanent differences. The controller starts from that list when the adviser writes.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, the fiscal bridge would be kept every month, so the tax line in the forecast is the number the return will use, and a VAT suppletie is found before the Belastingdienst raises it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying the trial balance into a workbook. The work worth keeping is the review with the adviser of the few lines that change the tax.
lenses.options: The pack can show two or three acceptable treatments of a provision, a depreciation life or a claim, with cash tax and the effective rate for each.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the mapping from AFAS accounts to fiscal categories and reviews the lines the mapping cannot classify.
reach: The wage-cost tie-out at totals level that now sits between the payroll specialist and the adviser.
A tax figure for the FP&A analysts that uses the same bridge as the return.
The fixed-asset fiscal values that the depreciation work should already have on the register.

grok.human_edge: The fiscal positions, and the sign-off that the pack matches the locked ledger and can go to the adviser.
grok.pattern_why: The bridge is a structured roll-forward of a locked ledger. Filing the return is a legal act, so the controller releases the pack and the external adviser signs the return.

in_practice.trigger: The year-end periods are locked in AFAS, or the external adviser issues the annual information request.
steps: Export the locked trial balance and the VAT return totals.
Roll the commercial result through the approved mapping to the vennootschapsbelasting bridge.
Tie wage-cost totals in the ledger to the payroll returns, without employee-level lines.
List open judgments: provisions, mixed costs and VAT on cross-border transport.
The controller reviews the pack, sends it, and reviews the adviser's draft return before filing.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller releases the pack against the locked ledger. The adviser signs the return. A person at the company approves the filing.
data_needed: The locked trial balance and the commercial-to-fiscal mapping
Payroll totals reconciled to the ledger
Fiscal values from the fixed-asset register
in_practice.logs_to: The year's tax folder on SharePoint, with the ledger lock date and the pack version that was sent.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces the trial balance, the VAT administration and the financial statements that a corporate-tax pack starts from.

risks: A bridge on a ledger that is still moving can understate or overstate taxable profit, with interest and penalties once filed.
A calculated line can hide a judgment on a provision or a VAT place-of-supply point. The adviser still has to take that position.
The wage reconciliation uses totals. Employee-level payroll data stays in AFAS under the AVG.
Under the EU AI Act the filing duty stays with the company and the adviser. A person approves the return before it is sent.

opus.short: Work with the tax adviser on choices that lower tax: investments, timing, entity structure, VAT.

today.trigger: Budget season, large investment plans (trucks, warehouse equipment, solar panels), or adviser's annual meeting.
steps: List planned investments and expected results
Check possible schemes (KIA, EIA, MIA/Vamil) and timing effects
Discuss scenarios with the tax adviser
Propose choices to the Finance Director
drudgery: Rebuilding scenario spreadsheets per question
Checking scheme conditions and thresholds every year
today.time_sinks: Researching current scheme conditions and building scenario models.

lenses.faster: AI summarises current scheme conditions from official sources and fills a standing scenario model from the investment plan.
lenses.autonomous: When an investment request above a threshold enters the approval flow, a check runs for possible tax schemes and deadlines (such as notification periods for EIA/MIA).
lenses.ambitious: Every qualifying investment is checked for schemes in time, instead of only the big ones the adviser notices.
lenses.joy: Less reading of scheme texts; more time discussing real choices with the Finance Director.

Finance Director: first draft of investment business cases

steps: Pull investment plan and forecast results
LLM summarises applicable schemes with source links for the adviser to verify

Controller discusses with adviser and proposes to the Finance Director

sol.short: Assess lawful tax options for investments, financing and other planned business decisions.

today.trigger: A proposed investment, financing decision, restructuring or annual tax-planning review.
steps: Clarify the business decision, timing, entity scope and commercial constraints.
Collect forecasts, asset details and relevant prior tax positions.
Ask the external adviser which current rules and options apply.
Model tax, cash and accounting effects under alternative assumptions.
Recommend an option and document approvals, conditions and deadlines.
drudgery: Rebuilding cash-flow comparisons and assembling adviser briefing material.
Checking which assumptions changed between scenario versions.
today.time_sinks: Obtaining complete facts and validating current rules and eligibility before scenarios are decision-ready.

lenses.faster: Prepare an adviser briefing and calculate consistent after-tax cash scenarios from approved assumptions. The controller reviews the trade-offs instead of rebuilding models.
lenses.autonomous: A logged investment proposal can trigger a fact checklist and scenario template. Tax interpretations and recommendations remain adviser-validated human work.
lenses.ambitious: Screen material proposals early enough to consider legitimate incentives and timing choices before commitments are made. Track whether expected benefits are realised.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated modelling and document assembly. Keep the commercial discussion about cash, uncertainty and business value.
lenses.options: Compare purchase, lease and timing alternatives where relevant, including a base case with no assumed incentive. Show sensitivity to eligibility, profit levels and financing assumptions.
lenses.altitude: Set the tax-planning decision framework and ensure material business decisions receive timely specialist input.
reach: Support FP&A investment appraisals with adviser-approved tax assumptions.
Prepare concise decision briefs for the Finance Director and external tax adviser.

sol.human_edge: Balancing commercial purpose, uncertainty, reputation and cash needs while recognising when specialist advice is essential.
sol.pattern_why: Copilot: AI helps structure facts, questions and scenarios, but tax interpretation and commercial judgment remain central.

in_practice.trigger: A material investment or financing proposal enters the review process.
steps: Collect the proposal facts and flag missing eligibility or entity information.
Draft questions for the adviser and identify assumptions requiring current confirmation.
Calculate after-tax scenarios using adviser-approved rules and deterministic formulas.
Draft a decision brief with sensitivities, conditions and unresolved issues.
Record the approved decision and relevant follow-up dates.
in_practice.human_gate: The external tax adviser validates rules and eligibility; the controller signs off the model and the Finance Director approves the business recommendation.
data_needed: Investment or financing proposal and cash-flow forecasts
Relevant taxable-profit outlook and prior tax positions
Entity structure and any applicable group arrangements
Current adviser-validated tax rules, incentives and conditions
Discount rates, financing terms and scenario assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint decision dossier with source facts, model versions, adviser confirmations, sensitivities, approvals and follow-up obligations.

evidence.claim: Deterministic scenario models can compare after-tax cash flows once applicable rules and assumptions have been established.
Language models can help prepare structured adviser briefs but cannot establish current eligibility or the defensibility of a tax position.

risks: An apparently attractive scenario assumes an incentive or deduction for which Noordhaven is ineligible.
Outdated rates, deadlines or entity assumptions invalidate the analysis.
Tax savings distract from a weaker commercial investment or adverse cash consequences.
Sensitive forecasts or proposed transactions enter an unapproved model service.
research_questions: How many material decisions currently receive tax input before commercial commitments?
Which recurring scenarios can the adviser validate as reusable templates?
Can the workflow identify missing eligibility facts without presenting speculative benefits as available?
Does faster preparation change decision quality or merely shorten document production?

grok.short: Work out the tax the company will pay on the forecast and large buys.

today.trigger: The budget cycle starts, FP&A issues a new forecast, or a large capex or lease request needs a cash and tax view.
steps: Take the forecast profit and apply last year's fiscal differences in Excel.
Test one or two ideas, such as the timing of a provision or the life of a fleet investment, with the adviser.
Check whether any current investment incentive applies before relying on it.
Write a note for the finance director and put a tax-cash line in the forecast.
Revise the line again when the forecast profit moves.
drudgery: Rebuilding the tax-cash line for every forecast version.
Searching mail for the adviser's memo from last year.
Recalculating depreciation differences that the asset register should already hold.
today.time_sinks: The tax line is finished late, so the forecast the business sees carries a stale cash-tax figure.

lenses.faster: Each new forecast version gets a cash-tax line from the approved fiscal bridge, including the loss position and the standing depreciation differences. Rebuilding that sheet disappears.
lenses.autonomous: When FP&A stores a forecast version, the tax-cash line recalculates and the movements are listed. A capex request over the threshold opens a one-page comparison. Both wait for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every material truck, racking, fit-out or WMS decision would be priced buy-versus-lease on cash, vennootschapsbelasting and BTW before the order is placed, and the forecast would carry a tax line the adviser would recognise.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses maintaining a side spreadsheet of tax cash. The work worth keeping is choosing a position the company can explain to the Belastingdienst.
lenses.options: Each case can show buy, finance lease and operating lease, or recognising a provision this year or next, with cash, VPB and BTW, and a note of the treatments the adviser has already refused.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the planning rules and the boundary of positions that always go to the adviser, and checks that the model still uses this year's rules.
reach: The tax-cash line inside the forecast the FP&A analysts maintain.
The employer-cost effect of a werkkostenregeling change, worked with the compensation and benefits specialist.
A capex case for the finance director before a site orders a fleet or a racking project.

grok.human_edge: Which legal position the company is willing to take and to have the adviser sign.
grok.pattern_why: The arithmetic can follow an approved bridge. The planning choice is a legal position under rules that change, and the controller leads it with the adviser.

in_practice.trigger: FP&A stores a new forecast version, or a capex or lease request comes in over the threshold.
steps: Apply the approved fiscal bridge to forecast profit and compute cash tax.
For a large purchase, price buy, finance lease and operating lease on cash, VPB and BTW.
Mark any position outside the boundary the adviser has already agreed.
The controller writes the recommendation and the finance director decides.
Write the accepted tax-cash line into that forecast version.
in_practice.human_gate: No tax figure enters the forecast the business sees until the controller accepts it. Anything outside the agreed boundary waits for the adviser.

The adviser's latest memo and the incentive rules the adviser has confirmed for this year

ambitious.text: Every truck, forklift and solar panel investment screened, so no deduction is missed.

joy.text: No hunting through scheme lists; the work is choosing timing with the Finance Director.

options.text: Three to five timing and financing scenarios with their tax effect.

altitude.text: The controller owns the screening checklist and the deadline rules.

steps: Check asset category and useful life policy

Advise the Finance Director and operations

Rebuilding buy-versus-lease models per request

lenses.ambitious: Fleet and equipment decisions across all three sites based on real lifetime cost, maintenance and residual values, not one request at a time.

sol.short: Set defensible depreciation assumptions and compare buying, leasing and disposing of assets.

today.trigger: A capital purchase, lease proposal, disposal or review of an asset's useful life or residual value.
steps: Collect asset specifications, cost, expected use, quotes and lease or disposal terms.
Determine the applicable accounting policy, useful life and residual value.
Calculate book depreciation and any separate tax treatment.
Compare purchase, lease and disposal cash flows and operational implications.
Obtain approval and pass reviewed asset instructions to the accountant.
drudgery: Rekeying quotes and asset details.
Rebuilding depreciation schedules and purchase-versus-lease comparisons.
Checking that approved assumptions match the accounting instruction.
today.time_sinks: Extracting contract terms and resolving missing useful-life, maintenance and residual-value assumptions.

lenses.faster: Extract quote terms into a checked template and calculate depreciation and cash comparisons with approved formulas. Draft the asset instruction directly from the reviewed assumptions.
lenses.autonomous: A complete capital proposal can trigger schedules and policy-consistency checks. Non-standard assets, uncertain residual values and unusual lease terms are routed for review.
lenses.ambitious: Evaluate material assets over their whole economic life, including maintenance, downtime and disposal. Compare forecast assumptions with realised costs to improve future decisions.
lenses.joy: Remove rekeying and repeated schedule preparation. Keep discussing operational needs and judging the assumptions that determine value.
lenses.options: Compare purchase, lease, refurbishment, delayed replacement and disposal where feasible. Vary utilisation, energy cost, maintenance and resale value to reveal fragile choices.
lenses.altitude: Own asset economics and the quality of useful-life assumptions across sites, supported by consistent calculations.
reach: Prepare standard asset-accounting schedules for the accountants.
Support FP&A and site managers with capital-investment comparisons.

sol.human_edge: Judging useful life and residual value from actual operating conditions and weighing reliability, safety and flexibility alongside financial returns.
sol.pattern_why: Agent with gate: deterministic software should calculate schedules, while an LLM extracts terms and drafts the brief; material assumptions and recommendations require approval.

in_practice.trigger: A capital proposal or disposal request has the minimum required facts and supporting documents.
steps: Extract asset and contract terms, linking each field to its source and flagging ambiguity.
Apply approved accounting policy and separate adviser-validated tax rules.
Calculate depreciation, cash flows and sensitivities using tested formulas.
Draft the recommendation and proposed asset-register instruction.
Obtain approval and reconcile the accountant's final entry to the approved instruction.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves useful life, residual value, classification and recommendation; the delegated investment approver authorises the commitment and the accountant controls posting.
systems: AFAS Profit ledger and available asset records
Approved document extraction or language-model service, to select
data_needed: Asset records, current carrying values and depreciation policies
Purchase quotes, lease contracts and disposal offers
Expected utilisation, maintenance, downtime and residual values
Applicable reporting framework and lease-accounting policy
Adviser-validated tax rules and approved discount rates
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint capital dossier containing source terms, extraction corrections, calculation versions, approved assumptions, decision and AFAS posting reference.

evidence.claim: Depreciation schedules and discounted cash-flow comparisons are deterministic calculations once policies and assumptions are set.
Document extraction can reduce rekeying, but ambiguous contract clauses and economically important assumptions still require review.

risks: Incorrect lease-term extraction changes the apparent economics or accounting treatment.
Book depreciation is confused with fiscal depreciation.
Standard useful lives ignore heavy shift use, maintenance history or obsolescence.
An incorrect reporting-framework assumption applies inappropriate lease accounting.
The comparison omits downtime, safety requirements or disposal obligations.
research_questions: Are asset records, reporting policies and useful-life categories complete and consistent across sites?
Can extraction reproduce material quote and lease terms without unflagged errors?
Which assets show the largest differences between assumed and realised useful life or residual value?
Does a pilot reproduce approved schedules and investment comparisons while materially reducing review and preparation time?

grok.short: Set depreciation lives and advise whether to buy, lease or sell an asset.

today.trigger: Accounts payable capitalises an invoice, a site sells or scraps a truck or forklift, or a lease quote needs a view before a purchase.
steps: Read the invoice and pick an asset class, a commercial life and a residual value.
Enter the asset in AFAS and set a fiscal life, often in a side calculation.
Check that the fixed-asset subledger still ties to the general ledger.
For a material item, build a buy-versus-lease or keep-versus-replace sheet in Excel.
Tell the site and FP&A what depreciation and cash to expect.
drudgery: Keying lives onto assets that belong in a class with a standard life.
Reconciling the register to the ledger by site.
Rebuilding the same lease comparison for another forklift or trailer.
today.time_sinks: Lives were set once and never revised, and the fiscal value often lives in the year-end Excel file rather than on the asset.

lenses.faster: An invoice that matches an approved class takes that class's commercial life, residual, fiscal life and ledger accounts. The controller stops rating each forklift, trailer and racking line.
lenses.autonomous: Capitalising a purchase invoice proposes the class. Repeat assets in an approved class depreciate on the register. A disposal recorded by a site opens the gain or loss and parks it if it is over the threshold.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every asset at the three sites would carry a current economic life, and idle trucks and forklifts would be visible before the company orders another one.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses keying a life onto a repeat asset. The work worth keeping is the keep-or-replace call on a fleet, made with the site.
lenses.options: A material request can show buy, finance lease and operating lease, or extend the life versus replace, with depreciation, fiscal deduction, cash and the site result.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the class policy and the capitalisation threshold, and deals with new classes, changed lives, impairments and material disposals.
reach: Capitalise-or-expense calls that the bookkeepers now make alone on supplier invoices.
Depreciation and capex for the FP&A forecast, taken from the register.
A list of idle assets for the site leads before a new truck or forklift is ordered.

grok.human_edge: A new class, a change of useful life, an impairment, and the buy, lease or sell decision on a material asset.
grok.pattern_why: Life, residual value and method sit on the asset class, and AFAS posts the amount from those rules, with no model in the path. The controller handles the exceptions and the advice above the threshold.

in_practice.trigger: Accounts payable capitalises a purchase invoice, a site records a disposal, or a lease quote arrives.
steps: Match the invoice to an asset class and propose commercial life, residual, fiscal life and ledger accounts.
Post depreciation for assets in a class the controller has already approved.
Park a new class, a change of life, an impairment, a component split, a material lease and a disposal over the threshold.
Attach the cash and result comparison for a parked buy, lease or sell.
The controller decides the exception and the outcome is sent to the site and to FP&A.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves each new class, any change of life, any impairment, and every buy, lease or sell above the threshold. Repeat assets in an approved class post on their own.
data_needed: The asset-class policy and the capitalisation threshold
Whether the jaarrekening is under RJ or IFRS, and the fiscal lives the adviser has accepted
The fixed-asset subledger and the general-ledger balance
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS asset record for routine postings, and a one-page memo in the SharePoint capex folder for every exception.

Buy-versus-lease advice for a Dutch logistics fleet still depends on the reporting framework and on the fiscal lives the adviser accepts. Those are not confirmed for this company.

Commercial and fiscal lives have to stay separate. Using one life for both misstates either the jaarrekening or the return.
