opus.short: Check, code and release supplier and staffing agency invoices in AFAS for the Rabobank payment run.

today.trigger: Invoice arrives in the AP mailbox or an agency portal; weekly payment run on Thursday.
steps: Open PDF or UBL invoice from Outlook and register it in AFAS Profit
Match to purchase order or contract; for agency invoices match hours and rates to the agency portal and site timesheets
Chase site managers by mail for approval of unmatched invoices
Code GL account, cost centre (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) and VAT
Build payment batch in AFAS and upload to Rabobank for approval
drudgery: Retyping invoice lines
Comparing agency hours line by line against portal exports
Reminder mails for approvals
today.time_sinks: Flex worker invoices from three agencies with different layouts, rate differences against the CAO pay scale, and approvals stuck with shift managers.

lenses.faster: Extraction, PO and hours matching and coding happen on arrival; the accountant only opens invoices that fail a match rule.
lenses.autonomous: Each new invoice triggers capture, three-way match and routing to the right approver; matched invoices within tolerance queue for the payment run without a touch.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours, CAO scale and surcharges instead of sampling, and recover overbilling that today goes unseen.
lenses.joy: No retyping or chasing; what remains is resolving real disputes with agencies and suppliers.
lenses.options: For a disputed agency invoice, get three resolutions drafted: credit note request, partial payment, or rate correction with the calculation attached.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the match rules, tolerances and the touchless rate, and tunes them monthly from the exception log.
reach: Bookkeeper AP invoice entry and coding
Credit and Collections Officer duplicate payment checks
Payroll Specialist checks of flex hours against payroll cost

opus.human_edge: Judging disputed charges, negotiating with agencies and suppliers, and approving the payment batch under four-eyes control.
opus.pattern_why: Several steps across AFAS, portals and mail with exceptions; payment must stay behind a human approval.

in_practice.trigger: New invoice in AP mailbox, Peppol inbox or agency portal export.
steps: Extract header and lines from PDF or read UBL directly
Match to PO, goods receipt or agency hours export with tolerance rules
Propose GL, cost centre and VAT code from history
Route exceptions to the approver in AFAS workflow with the mismatch explained
Queue matched invoices for the weekly batch; accountant and Finance Director approve in Rabobank
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant reviews exceptions and the batch summary; payment released with two signatures in Rabobank.
data_needed: Agency hours exports and agreed rate cards
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice workflow history plus an exception log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: AP automation products capture invoices, match them to POs and route exceptions
Dutch OCR and invoice extraction services feed bookkeeping systems
Matching agency invoices to hours and CAO rates with an LLM plus rules is feasible

risks: Supplier bank detail change fraud passing a touchless flow
Agency invoices contain flex worker names and hours: personal data under AVG/GDPR, needs a processing record
Wrong VAT code at scale
research_questions: What share of invoices today has a PO or a matching hours export, and so could pass touchless?
Do the three agencies deliver structured hours files or only PDFs?
How much overbilling did last year's agency invoices contain on a sample of 200?
Does AFAS Profit's invoice workflow accept an external matching result through its API?

sol.short: Check supplier and staffing agency invoices and get approved payments ready in AFAS.

today.trigger: An invoice arrives in Outlook, AFAS or a staffing agency portal; the payment run approaches.
steps: Collect the invoice and check supplier details, invoice number, VAT and possible duplicates.
Compare charges with the purchase approval, delivery evidence or approved agency hours and rates.
Check the AFAS booking and ask the site manager or bookkeeper to resolve differences.
Prepare approved invoices for the payment batch and obtain the required authorisations.
Check payment status against Rabobank records and file supporting evidence.
drudgery: Downloading agency invoices and hours files.
Comparing invoice lines with approved hours and rate tables.
Chasing missing approvals and attachments.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: most effort sits in exceptions, missing approvals and agency rate differences; actual volumes and touch times are unknown.

lenses.faster: Extract invoice fields once and run duplicate, VAT and matching checks automatically. The accountant receives a short list of differences with the supporting documents attached.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice receipt starts checking and approval routing without a reminder. The workflow prepares a batch only from invoices that have passed the required approvals.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours, contracted rates and applicable allowances. Show repeated errors by agency and site so Finance can fix the cause.
lenses.joy: Remove portal downloads, copying fields and routine chasing. Keep supplier disputes, unusual charges and decisions that need commercial judgment.
lenses.options: Compare payment dates against due dates, available discounts and the cash forecast. Present the cost and cash effect of each permitted schedule.
lenses.altitude: Own invoice control rules, exception thresholds and supplier data quality. Improve the percentage of invoices processed without touch.
reach: Bookkeeper: routine invoice matching and approval follow-up.
Controller: analysis of agency billing errors and recurring control failures.
FP&A Analyst: confirmed supplier payment inputs for the cash forecast.

sol.human_edge: Resolve disputed charges, interpret unusual contractual terms and recognise suspicious supplier changes. Authorised people retain payment release responsibility.
sol.pattern_why: Use llm_step for invoice extraction and deterministic_software for arithmetic, duplicates and matching. Payment preparation spans several systems, so approval is required before the batch proceeds.

in_practice.trigger: A new invoice enters the controlled intake queue, or the scheduled payment run starts.
steps: Retrieve the invoice through an approved connector or controlled import and retain the original.
Extract fields with source references, validate totals and apply duplicate and VAT checks.
Match against approved purchases or agency hours and versioned contract rates.
Route differences and missing approvals to named owners; prepare only approved items.
Present the proposed AFAS batch for authorisation and reconcile returned bank status.
in_practice.human_gate: Budget owners approve charges; the accountant reviews exceptions and the proposed batch. Authorised bank signatories release payments under the existing separation of duties; bank-detail changes require independent verification.
systems: Staffing agency portals or controlled exports
data_needed: Supplier master data and approved bank details.
Original invoices, purchase approvals and delivery evidence.
Approved agency hours and effective contract rates, including agreed allowance treatment.
VAT rules, approval limits, due dates and payment permissions.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice and approval records, with a restricted SharePoint evidence register recording checks, exceptions, authorisations and batch references.

evidence.claim: Structured invoice matching, duplicate detection and approval routing can use explicit rules; document extraction can supply fields for validation.
The proposed workflow could save 65% of accountant handling time and make completion twice as fast; these are untested estimates for Noordhaven.

risks: False matches or incorrect allowance rules can approve overbilling; use approved hours and contracted agency rates rather than assuming employee CAO rates apply directly.
Supplier bank-detail fraud and duplicate payments require controls independent of document extraction.
Agency files contain personal data; restrict fields, access and retention under AVG/GDPR.
Portal exports, AFAS imports and Rabobank batch interfaces may require manual steps or additional integration work.
research_questions: What share of accountant time concerns routine invoices versus exceptions already escalated by the bookkeepers?
Can all three agencies provide stable invoice and approved-hours exports with matching identifiers?
Which approvals and bank controls must remain manual, and how much elapsed time do they add?
Does a shadow pilot catch known duplicate, rate and VAT errors without excessive false alerts?

grok.short: Process supplier invoices and release the payment batch.

today.trigger: Invoices arrive daily by mail, from carriers, and from the three staffing-agency portals, and due dates fall on the Rabobank payment run.
steps: Collect PDFs and portal invoices from Outlook, SharePoint and the agency portals into AFAS Profit.
Code each invoice to a grootboekrekening, btw-code and kostenplaats, and match it to a purchase order or receipt where one exists.
Chase missing receipts, disputed flex hours and price differences with the bookkeepers or the agency.
Build the payment proposal in AFAS for invoices that are approved and due.
Export a SEPA batch and have a second authorised person release it in Rabobank.
drudgery: Re-typing invoice headers and VAT lines that a file already contains
Opening three agency portals to copy the same hours into AFAS
Holding a complete batch because one line is missing a receipt
today.time_sinks: Most of the 134 hours per accountant per year sits in coding, portal re-keying and exception chasing, not in the Rabobank release itself.

lenses.faster: Matched invoices are coded and proposed for payment without a person retyping them. The accountant only opens lines that fail a match, a VAT check or a duplicate check.
lenses.autonomous: A new e-invoice, mailbox PDF or agency file starts the match on arrival. The payment run is created on the agreed Rabobank day, not when someone remembers.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would post carrier and flex-worker cost to Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo in the week the work happened, so the forecast is not waiting for a lump invoice.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying portal lines into AFAS. What remains is the argument about a real price or hours dispute.
lenses.options: The accountant sees the batch under three cuts: pay all matched items, hold items over a Controller-set amount, and hold every new supplier.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains supplier rules, VAT defaults and the match tolerances, and reviews the exceptions, rather than coding each invoice.
reach: Straight-through coding now done by the bookkeepers on purchase invoices
Cash application of customer receipts, shared with the credit and collections officer
The payroll control-account side of agency invoices, shared with the payroll specialist

grok.human_edge: Judgment when a flex-hour invoice does not match the ordered shifts, and the decision to release company money.
grok.pattern_why: Capture, matching and the payment proposal can run as steps across AFAS, the mailbox and the agency files, but a SEPA batch must not count until a second person releases it.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice file lands in the AFAS purchase queue, or the payment calendar reaches the Rabobank run.
steps: Read the invoice into header, lines, IBAN, VAT and site from UBL or PDF, and from a line file where the agency provides one.
Match supplier, purchase order, receipt and amount. Apply the supplier's btw-code only when the line does not contradict it.
Park duplicates, new IBANs, VAT clashes and unmatched lines for the accountant, with the source file attached.
Build the payment proposal from due invoices that passed the match.
A second authorised person releases the SEPA batch to Rabobank.
in_practice.human_gate: No batch is sent to Rabobank without a named second person releasing it. New VAT treatments, new IBANs and unmatched invoices above the Controller's limit wait for the accountant.
systems: AFAS Profit accounts payable and workflow
data_needed: Supplier master with IBAN, default account, btw-code and kostenplaats
Open purchase orders and receipts in AFAS
Agency line files with hours, rate, site and invoice number
The Rabobank mandate and the AFAS authorisation matrix
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS posting and workflow log, plus the released pain.001 file stored in the finance SharePoint close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit registers purchase invoices, routes them through workflow and creates SEPA payment proposals.
Rabobank business banking accepts SEPA bulk payment files from accounting software.
Dutch invoice-capture products such as Basecone and Klippa read header and line fields from PDF invoices.
A stable agency hour file can be matched to site cost without a model.

risks: A wrong btw-code on international transport (zero rate or verleggingsregeling) creates a VAT error the Belastingdienst will still charge to Noordhaven.

evidence.claim: Stable account mappings can run as explicit rules, with model suggestions reserved for descriptions that do not match those rules.

sol.short: Improve and document our AFAS accounting workflows and the links to reporting and bank systems.

today.trigger: A control gap, manual workaround, reporting need or system change requires a workflow improvement.
steps: Describe the problem and map the current records, controls and handoffs.
Agree requirements with Finance, IT and affected payroll or site owners.
Design configuration, imports, validations or reporting changes.
Test representative cases and failure handling outside production.
Obtain approval, release the change and document operation and ownership.
drudgery: Writing repetitive specifications and operating instructions.
Preparing sample data and test cases.
Maintaining manual exports and spreadsheet handoffs.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: understanding integration limits, coordinating owners and validating safe changes take more time than drafting documentation.

lenses.faster: Use AI to draft specifications, validation scripts and operating instructions from an agreed process. Reuse tested components for imports, reconciliations and exception queues.
lenses.autonomous: Approved integrations can run on schedules and report failed imports or changed data formats. Design choices and production releases stay with named owners.
lenses.ambitious: Replace fragile spreadsheet handoffs with reproducible data flows that feed both the close and forecast. Make recurring controls run during the month rather than only at month-end.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive documentation and small amounts of repetitive coding. Keep solving process problems and seeing fewer errors reach colleagues.
lenses.options: Compare AFAS configuration, a Microsoft 365 workflow and a small custom integration. Show operating cost, controls, maintenance needs and recovery arrangements.
lenses.altitude: Become the finance process and data-control owner. Set standards for interfaces, evidence, exception handling and safe change.
reach: Controller: design and maintenance of finance controls.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: specifications for payroll-to-finance interfaces.
FP&A Analyst: reliable actuals feeds and reporting definitions.
IT application support: finance acceptance criteria and operational runbooks.

sol.human_edge: Translate accounting obligations into system requirements and decide whether a design is safe and usable. Coordinate ownership and acceptance across Finance, IT and the sites.
sol.pattern_why: AI can help create specifications, code and documentation, but system design and acceptance require accounting and operational judgment. The resulting routine workflows should use deterministic_software wherever rules are sufficient.

in_practice.trigger: An approved improvement request identifies a measurable accounting problem.
steps: Define the outcome, current effort, control requirements and accountable owners.
Compare implementation options against confirmed interface and permission limits.
Draft configuration, code and documentation in a development environment using synthetic or minimised data.
Test totals, permissions, duplicate handling, failure recovery and representative accounting cases.
Obtain Finance and IT acceptance, release through change control and monitor the agreed outcome.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves accounting behaviour; IT reviews security and operation; the Controller or designated owner authorises production release. Bank and ledger permissions remain subject to separation of duties.

Rabobank approved interfaces or test files
data_needed: Current process maps, requirements and measured error or handling rates.
Confirmed AFAS, Microsoft 365 and bank interface specifications.
Accounting controls, access roles and retention requirements.
Representative test cases, source control totals and recovery procedures.
in_practice.logs_to: The approved change register and version-control repository, linked to SharePoint requirements, acceptance evidence, release decisions and operational runbooks.

evidence.claim: AI can assist with specifications, code and documentation; reliable accounting automation still requires interface validation, testing and accountable release decisions.

risks: Generated code or configuration can look correct while mishandling totals, duplicates or failed submissions.

Development access can accidentally bypass production accounting controls.
Sending live payroll or supplier data to unapproved AI services can breach confidentiality and AVG/GDPR obligations.

Which manual handoff has enough recurring cost or error impact to justify maintenance?

Highlight missing information, changed estimates and unresolved accounting questions.
Route the complete package through accounting review, directors' approval and the applicable audit and filing process.

Controlled statement generation and validation software

steps: Define the review scope and applicable financial, legal or contractual requirements.

Preparing repetitive question lists.
Turning notes into evidence-linked review records.

sol.human_edge: Build trust, ask sensitive questions fairly, recognise context and distinguish a process failure from an unsupported allegation against an individual.

Build an evidence-linked transaction timeline and draft neutral questions.
Have the accountant conduct interviews and record proportionate notes.
Compare explanations against records and identify corroboration or contradictions.
Draft the review record for factual checking, accountant approval and appropriate escalation.

Proportionate interview notes and corroborating evidence

Pick the sample and note what is missing or coded oddly.
Arrange a short conversation with the warehouse clerk, the planner or the bookkeeper who knows the job.
Write down what they said and whether the booking should change.
Send the correction to the bookkeeper and put it on the close file.
drudgery: Opening booking after booking to find the attachment.
Building the sample list by hand.
Writing up conversations that all started from the same questions.
today.time_sinks: The time splits between pulling records and reaching shift staff who are not at a desk during the close.

lenses.faster: The sample, the missing attachments and a short question list are ready before the conversation. The conversation stays on the accountant's calendar.
lenses.autonomous: A failed tie-out or a VAT exception assembles the file and names the role that is likely to know. It does not contact the employee.
lenses.ambitious: Coding and cutoff questions would be settled with the site in the same week, so the year-end sample is small and the same Venlo cutoff does not return every January.
lenses.joy: The attachment hunt goes. A clerk explaining a real shipment is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: For the same exception, prepare a VAT question list, a cutoff question list and a cost-centre question list, and let the documents decide which one is used.

reach: Bookkeeper: a vendor-statement difference that needs a phone call

grok.human_edge: Talking with a clerk on a shift so the question is about the booking, and hearing the explanation that is not in the attachment.
grok.pattern_why: The record pull and the question list can be prepared. The conversation, the reading of what the person means, and the decision to change a booking stay with the accountant.

steps: Assemble the booking, the invoice, the goods receipt and prior exceptions of the same type.
Draft a short question list aimed at the missing fact.
Name the role that is likely to know, and send nothing to that person.
After the conversation, write up the fact in the accountant's words and propose the correction.

The site and the role of the person who entered it, used only for this check
The CAO or VAT rule the booking is being tested against

probe.rule_why: several steps over a stream of cases, with exceptions

opus.short: Build projections of costs and revenues per site and customer from AFAS and agency data, and advise the Controller.

today.trigger: Quarterly reforecast, a request from the Finance Director, or a large customer contract change.
steps: Export the general ledger and the open AR and AP from AFAS into Excel
Collect flex worker hours and invoices from the three agency portals
Adjust the drivers (volumes, hourly rates, CAO indexation) by hand in the forecast workbook
Write a short note on trends and risks for the Controller and FP&A
drudgery: Re-mapping AFAS exports into the forecast workbook every quarter
Downloading and matching agency invoices per site
today.time_sinks: Data collection and reconciling the agency figures with AFAS take most of the time; the analysis itself is short.

lenses.faster: A nightly pipeline already loads AFAS and agency data into a driver model, so the accountant starts from a populated forecast instead of exports.
lenses.autonomous: When the month closes in AFAS, an agent refreshes the projection and flags drivers that moved more than a set threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling 13-week cash and cost forecast per site and per large customer, updated weekly instead of four times a year.
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste of exports; the time goes into asking site managers why volumes shift.
lenses.options: Three scenarios each time (peak season flex demand high, base, customer loss) with the effect on margin and cash.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the driver model and its assumptions log and checks the agent's output against actuals each month.
reach: FP&A Analyst: first-pass reforecast
Credit and Collections Officer: cash-in projection from DSO trends

opus.human_edge: Knowing which customer contracts are about to change and which site figures the business does not trust; signing off the assumptions.
opus.pattern_why: Several sources, exceptions in agency data and judgment on drivers; the projection should not reach management until the accountant approves it.

in_practice.trigger: Month close status set to closed in AFAS, plus quarterly reforecast date.
steps: Pull GL, AR, AP via AFAS GetConnectors and agency hours/invoices into a staging table
Recalculate driver-based projection per site in the model
Draft a variance-and-trend note with the top five movements
Accountant reviews assumptions and edits the note
Publish to the Power BI forecast page and send to Controller
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves assumptions and the note before publishing.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or a Claude-based agent
data_needed: GL actuals per site and cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Assumptions log on SharePoint with version per forecast run

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit exposes data through GetConnectors (REST) for extraction
Copilot in Excel can propose formulas and summarize trends in a workbook
An LLM can draft a reliable trend note from a structured variance table

risks: Agency data in inconsistent formats breaks the pipeline
Management trusts a polished projection more than its assumptions deserve
Customer data shared with an external model without a processing agreement (AVG)
research_questions: How far off were the last four quarterly forecasts, and which drivers caused the error?
Can all three agency portals deliver hours and invoices as a file or API, or only PDF?
Would FP&A accept a shared driver model owned by the accountants?

sol.short: Explain site cost and revenue trends and prepare the financial outlook with FP&A.

today.trigger: A forecast round, investment proposal or management question about Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo.
steps: Export financial actuals and commitments from AFAS and retrieve the latest approved forecast.
Collect explanations from site managers and obtain staffing costs and operational drivers where available.
Clean mappings and compare revenue, labour, agency spend and other costs in Excel.
Project revenues and expenses, checking assumptions with FP&A and the Controller.
Prepare a short explanation of the outlook, uncertainties and recommended actions.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same site and account mappings.
Copying actuals into forecast workbooks.
Chasing explanations and reconciling different workbook versions.
today.time_sinks: Finding consistent inputs and explaining differences between accounting actuals, agency commitments and operational assumptions.

lenses.faster: Reconcile AFAS actuals and approved commitments automatically, then draft a source-linked variance explanation. Repeated exports, mapping and spreadsheet assembly disappear.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly extract passes reconciliation checks, refresh the outlook and flag material changes. Ask managers only for missing assumptions or unexplained movements.
lenses.ambitious: Produce a rolling site outlook every week, including agency labour and cash implications, if the underlying operational data supports it.
lenses.joy: Remove workbook repair and repeated requests for figures. Keep the conversations about why costs moved and what the business can change.
lenses.options: Compare base, peak-volume and downside cases with different agency hours, rates and customer volumes. Show which assumptions change the result most.
lenses.altitude: Own the forecast reconciliation rules, assumption register and explanation quality instead of assembling every analysis.
reach: FP&A: prepare reconciled actuals and first-pass forecast scenarios.
Controller: maintain a financial commitments register.
Site management: quantify proposed staffing and spending changes.

sol.human_edge: Judge whether commercial and operational assumptions are credible, challenge managers and explain uncertainty without presenting a scenario as a promise.
sol.pattern_why: Several sources and follow-up questions are involved. Deterministic calculations should produce the numbers; an LLM can draft explanations, with human approval of assumptions and advice.

in_practice.trigger: A validated nightly AFAS extract arrives during a forecast cycle, or an accountant requests a scenario.
steps: Check extract freshness, reconcile totals to AFAS and apply versioned site and account mappings.
Combine approved commitments and operational assumptions, clearly marking unavailable or estimated inputs.
Calculate the outlook and scenarios using controlled formulas.
Draft explanations linked to source figures and route unanswered questions to the accountant.
After approval, save the forecast version and publish the agreed analysis.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant and FP&A approve assumptions and explanations; the Controller or Finance Director approves the official forecast under existing authority.
data_needed: Actuals by period, site and account.
Approved forecast versions and mapping tables.
Open commitments and agency hours and rates.
Operational volumes and pricing assumptions where available.
Materiality thresholds and named assumption owners.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint forecast register containing source timestamps, model versions, assumptions, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh, financial measures and comparisons across sites and periods.
Controlled calculations and source-linked drafting could reduce repeated forecast preparation.
The proposed workflow, 60% time saving and 2.5 times speedup are untested estimates for Noordhaven.

risks: The nightly extract cannot support claims about today's transactions.
Missing operational volumes or incomplete commitments can make projections misleading.
Generated explanations may invent causes unless each causal claim is confirmed.
Detailed payroll and customer data require restricted access and an approved processing arrangement.
research_questions: Can AFAS actuals and commitments be reconciled by site without manual mapping repairs?
Which operational drivers exist, who owns them and how current are they?
Does a pilot reduce total preparation and review time while preserving forecast accuracy?
Which responsibilities belong to the accountants versus the two FP&A Analysts?

grok.short: Review costs and revenues after the close and say what the forecast should assume.

today.trigger: The monthly AFAS close locks, or FP&A asks before the forecast lock what a cost line should assume. Typical lines are flex labour, fuel, warehouse overtime and site housing.
steps: Export the profit and loss from AFAS by site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo), cost centre and account.
Add open purchase commitments, the lease schedule and the three agency contracts.
Compare actuals in Excel with last year and with the latest forecast.
Separate one-offs such as a damage claim, a CAO back-pay or a single large spot job.
Send the controller and FP&A a short note on what next period should assume.
drudgery: Rebuilding last month's workbook from a copy.
Re-aligning cost centres that moved since the budget.
Rewriting the same variance sentences for fuel, flex and overtime.
today.time_sinks: Waiting for a site manager to explain a spike, and discovering that flex labour sits in three agency accounts while the forecast holds one line.

lenses.faster: The bridge from actuals to a run-rate, and a first note on what to assume, are ready the morning the close locks. The accountant checks the bridges and the one-off tags.
lenses.autonomous: The AFAS period lock starts the pack. Nobody has to remember to refresh the workbook.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep a weekly view, by site, of flex labour, fuel and warehouse overtime that FP&A can drop into the forecast the sites are asked to trust.
lenses.joy: The copying and the repeated sentences go away. What remains is the call on which spike is structural.
lenses.options: Each pack carries five assumption sets: volume flat, peak season, a CAO wage step, an agency rate change, and a fuel move, each tied to an account.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets the rules for a one-off and the drivers the projection must use (orders, shifts, kilometres), and reviews the cases those rules get wrong.
reach: First-pass driver commentary that FP&A now writes after the close.
Simple flux lines the controller asks the bookkeepers to explain.

grok.human_edge: Knowing which Rotterdam peak is a customer pattern and which is a one-off claim, and whether a site explanation is complete enough for a forecast the business will trust.
grok.pattern_why: Actuals and a mechanical run-rate can be built from the nightly extract. The sentence that enters the forecast is a judgment, so the accountant or the controller signs the pack before FP&A uses it.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period lock, or a named FP&A request before the forecast lock.
steps: A job reads the nightly AFAS extract by site, cost centre and account, plus open commitments and the lease register.
Rules apply the one-off list and compute run-rate against the latest forecast.
The draft is a one-page projection and five driver scenarios, each figure tied to an account and a period.
The accountant reviews flagged bridges, edits the advice, and sends breaks back to the site or to FP&A.
The signed pack is filed on SharePoint and linked from the forecast file.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant or the controller signs the pack before FP&A loads it. Any variance above the agreed euro amount stays open until a person has tagged it.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and the cost-centre map by site
Lease schedule and agency rate cards
in_practice.logs_to: The close folder on SharePoint, with the approver, the time, the forecast version and the account list written on the pack.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reports actuals by administration, cost centre and period, and can store a budget next to those actuals.
Power BI supports a scheduled refresh and variance visuals on a finance dataset.
Noordhaven already refreshes a finance Power BI dashboard from a nightly AFAS extract, so the actuals path is in place.

risks: A wrong cost-centre map produces a clean pack that moves the forecast the wrong way.
CAO wage steps and agency rate cards are not in the ledger. A model that only reads actuals misses the commitment.
Site managers stop explaining spikes if the pack looks finished before they have spoken.

How often does the controller reject a one-off tag after the site has explained it?

grok.short: Compare budgeted cost with actual cost and keep the budget maintained.

today.trigger: Each month, after the AFAS close, the controller wants budget versus actual before the management meeting.
steps: Export actuals from AFAS and open the budget FP&A holds in AFAS or in Excel.
Map accounts and cost centres that moved after the budget was set.
Compute the variance by site and by cost type: own staff, flex, housing, fleet.

Write one line on every variance the meeting is likely to ask about.

Copying tables into a slide pack.

today.time_sinks: The budget structure and the ledger structure differ, so a large part of the hour is mapping rather than reading the variance.

lenses.faster: The join of budget to actuals, in the ledger's own structure, is refreshed when the period locks. The accountant writes only on the lines outside the threshold.
lenses.autonomous: The period lock refreshes the pack. No one opens last month's file to start the new one.

lenses.joy: The remapping and the formatting go away. What remains is deciding which overrun is timing and which one a site must explain.
lenses.options: The pack shows the original budget, the latest forecast and the actual, so the meeting can see whether the gap is an old budget or a new miss.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the account map and the threshold rules, and checks the map when FP&A revises the budget or a cost centre changes.
reach: The monthly variance table FP&A rebuilds for the management pack.
The first explanation of a cost-centre miss that bookkeepers now prepare ad hoc.

grok.human_edge: Seeing whether a variance is an agency invoice in the wrong period or a real overrun. The report can show the euros. The accountant still makes that call on material lines.

probe.rule_why: several steps over a stream of cases, with exceptions

opus.short: Check payroll against contracts and the loonaangifte: WW premium rates, WGA/ZW risk, wage tax and agency liability.

today.trigger: Year end, an audit request, a Belastingdienst query, or a change in premium rules.
steps: Export payroll journals and employee contract data from AFAS
Check per employee whether the low WW premium is justified by a written permanent contract
Reconcile payroll journal with GL and the loonaangifte totals
Check agency invoices for G-account and chain liability (ketenaansprakelijkheid) requirements
Report differences to Payroll Specialist and Controller
drudgery: Matching contract types with premium codes for 1,200 employees by hand
Reconciling journal totals line by line
today.time_sinks: Contract-to-premium checks across many employees and many contract changes in the flex season.

lenses.faster: A script compares every employee's contract type, hours and premium code and lists only mismatches.
lenses.autonomous: After each pay run, reconciliations run on their own and mismatches go to the Payroll Specialist before the loonaangifte is filed.
lenses.ambitious: Monthly full-population checks instead of a yearly sample, avoiding back-payments of the high WW premium.
lenses.joy: No more line-by-line matching; the accountant handles the cases that need judgment.
lenses.options: For each mismatch, the possible corrections and their cost are shown.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the rule set as premium and tax rules change each January.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pre-filing checks
HR Administrator: contract data quality fixes

opus.human_edge: Interpreting Dutch premium and tax rules in edge cases, and agreeing corrections with Payroll and the tax advisor.
opus.pattern_why: Core checks are rules, but reading scanned contracts and agency documents needs an extraction step and corrections must be approved.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll run approved in AFAS, before the loonaangifte is filed.
steps: Pull payroll journal, contract and premium data from AFAS
Run rule checks (WW premium, hours, Zvw, GL reconciliation)
Extract contract facts from scanned documents where AFAS fields are empty
List mismatches with proposed correction
Accountant and Payroll Specialist approve corrections
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Payroll Specialist approve each correction before filing.
in_practice.logs_to: Payroll audit register in SharePoint per pay period

evidence.source: Belastingdienst guidance on WW premium differentiation

risks: Payroll data is sensitive personal data under AVG; access and processing must be limited

sol.short: Check payroll taxes, social insurance premiums and payroll liabilities against Dutch rules and both CAOs.

today.trigger: A payroll reconciliation, year-end review, premium decision or audit request.
steps: Obtain AFAS payroll results, relevant contract fields and payroll-to-ledger reconciliations.
Collect current tax guidance, premium decisions and applicable CAO provisions.
Sample payroll calculations and check relevant classifications, allowances and liabilities.
Investigate differences with the Payroll Specialist and HR.
Document findings and submit corrections for authorized review.
systems: AFAS Profit HR, payroll and general ledger
drudgery: Matching payroll reports to ledger postings.
Repeating premium and allowance calculations.
Locating the rule version that applied to a specific pay period.
today.time_sinks: Resolving rule applicability across employment situations, the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO.

lenses.faster: Reconcile payroll totals to the ledger and recalculate selected premiums using dated, approved rules. Present differences with the relevant employee fields and rule references.
lenses.autonomous: Run checks when a payroll run is finalized or an approved rule changes. Route exceptions to the Payroll Specialist and accountant.
lenses.ambitious: Check all eligible payroll records rather than a small sample, and quantify the exposure from each confirmed configuration error.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated report matching and arithmetic. Keep interpretation of difficult cases and prevention of recurring errors.
lenses.options: Model the financial effect of alternative classifications where the legal treatment is uncertain. Have the Payroll Specialist or adviser resolve the correct treatment before correction.
lenses.altitude: Maintain a payroll assurance framework with dated rules, coverage checks and evidence of corrections.
reach: Payroll Specialist: provide independent payroll-to-ledger assurance.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: quantify allowance and premium effects.
Controller: support payroll liability and provision reviews.

sol.human_edge: Interpret Dutch payroll obligations and CAO scope with specialists, resolve ambiguous employment facts and take responsibility for audit conclusions.
sol.pattern_why: Reconciliations and recalculations are deterministic once applicability is settled. People must approve legal interpretations and payroll corrections; an LLM may help locate clauses but cannot establish the rule.

in_practice.trigger: A finalized payroll run, year-end reconciliation or approved change to payroll rules.
steps: Retrieve the minimum payroll and contract fields needed and reconcile them to the general ledger.
Apply approved, effective-dated checks for wage tax, AWf, Aof, Whk and other relevant liabilities.
Test applicable CAO allowances and financial sick-pay obligations where included in scope.
Create evidence packs for exceptions and quantify potential corrections.
Record specialist decisions and verify authorized corrections in a subsequent payroll run.
in_practice.human_gate: The Payroll Specialist validates applicability and corrections; material or disputed tax and CAO interpretations go to the responsible adviser and authorized finance approver.
systems: Controlled calculation workbook or rules service
data_needed: Payroll components, taxable bases and ledger postings.
Relevant contract type, hours and CAO assignment.
Current employer premium decisions and effective-dated Dutch rules.
Approved allowance and sick-pay rules, without medical diagnoses.
Agency agreements where liability concerning flex workers is in scope.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted payroll assurance register containing rule versions, exception references, decisions and correction evidence.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit includes payroll processing and financial administration.
Independent premium recalculations and payroll-to-ledger checks can use approved, effective-dated rules.
The proposed workflow, 50% time saving and two times speedup remain untested.

risks: US workers' compensation concepts do not map directly to Dutch employee insurance and employer liabilities.
Outdated premium rates or incorrect contract and CAO classifications can invalidate calculations.

grok.short: Check payroll liabilities, premium wage bases and wage-tax compliance.

today.trigger: The payroll specialist posts the period journal, a quarterly or year-end premium true-up is due, or the auditor samples the wage liability. A Whk rate letter or a Belastingdienst query starts the same work.
steps: Take the AFAS payroll journal, the loonaangifte summary and headcount by site.
Check which wage components, including CAO allowances such as shift premiums, enter the premium wage base.
Keep agency flex workers in the agency cost and outside Noordhaven's own Awf, Aof and Whk base.
Tie wage tax, the pension funds the two CAOs require, the leave and vakantiegeld provision, and the sick-pay accrual to the balance sheet.
Send breaks to the payroll specialist and sign the liability that enters the close.
drudgery: Adding up wage components by site.
Rebuilding the leave and vakantiegeld workbook.
Searching mail for the latest Whk rate letter.
today.time_sinks: A wage-component map that was not updated after a CAO change, and flex and own staff mixed on the same cost centre.

lenses.faster: The bridge from payroll components to the loonaangifte and to the balance-sheet accruals is calculated when the journal posts. The accountant reviews the breaks.
lenses.autonomous: Posting of the payroll journal starts the tie-out. A break above the set amount opens a case for the accountant and the payroll specialist.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every wage component would be reconciled every period, and the Whk, leave and sick-pay accruals would stay current so the auditor does not rebuild them at year-end.
lenses.joy: Adding up allowances by site goes away. What remains is the grey wage component, and the talk with payroll when the filing and the ledger disagree.
lenses.options: The pack shows the accrual at the current Whk rates and at the rate on a letter that may still be revised, so Finance sees the range before it books one number.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the wage-component map (premium-bearing or not, own staff or flex) and the accrual method, and reviews the map when the CAO or a rate letter changes.
reach: The payroll accrual journal the bookkeepers post from a payroll summary.
The first check that an agency invoice reflects inlenersbeloning, a check that now falls between Finance and HR.

grok.human_edge: Deciding how to treat a component the CAO and the tax rules describe differently, and signing the liability in the close. A wrong premium base becomes a Belastingdienst assessment.
grok.pattern_why: The tie-out is a set of rules on AFAS wage components, but the signed liability is a tax and premium position. The accountant approves each period before the amount is booked. Sick-pay detail under the Wet verbetering poortwachter stays with payroll.

in_practice.trigger: The payroll specialist locks the period and posts the payroll journal in AFAS.
steps: The job reads wage-component totals by site and cost centre, the loonaangifte summary, and the balance-sheet accounts.
The wage-component map classifies each component for Awf, Aof, Whk, pension and the leave provision, and excludes agency flex from the own-staff base.
Breaks above the threshold, and any component not on the map, open a case.
The accountant and the payroll specialist clear the cases. The accountant signs the accrual, including leave, vakantiegeld and sick-pay cost, using totals only.
The signed tie-out is filed in the close folder with the map version and the rate letter used.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the period liability before it is booked. The payroll specialist keeps the payroll run, the loonaangifte filing and the individual employee file.
data_needed: Payroll journal and loonaangifte totals by wage component and site
Latest Whk rate letter and pension rates from the CAOs
Headcount split between own staff and agency flex
Leave, vakantiegeld and sick-pay accrual rules
in_practice.logs_to: The payroll tie-out in the close folder on SharePoint: map version, rate letter, accounts, approver and time.

today.trigger: The daily collection review starts or a payment promise expires.

Checking whether nightly dashboard figures are still current.
Manually removing paid or disputed invoices from follow-up lists.

Take off items already promised or marked disputed.
Compare the list with the Power BI ageing from the nightly extract.
Build the day's call and mail list by hand.

Reconciling the live ledger with a dashboard that is one night old.

reach: The AR bookkeepers' unallocated-cash list, which uses the same open items.

The FP&A weekly cash forecast.

Publish the queue for the officer on the finance dashboard.

Payment terms and dispute flags on the debtor or the item.

sol.short: Send reminders and call customers whose overdue invoices need personal follow-up.

today.trigger: An invoice reaches a reminder threshold or a customer misses a payment promise.
steps: Verify the unpaid balance, contact details and previous reminders.
Check for disputes or recently received payments.
Write and send a reminder or call the customer.
Record the response and schedule the next action.
drudgery: Editing the same reminder wording.
Attaching invoices and repeating payment details.
Preparing call notes from scattered correspondence.
today.time_sinks: Preparing accurate reminders and call briefings, finding the correct contact, and logging the outcome.

lenses.faster: Prepare reminders with checked balances, invoice attachments and contact history. Give the officer a brief before each call.
lenses.autonomous: Approved templates can handle routine reminders under explicit rules. Disputes, sensitive relationships and stronger wording require review.
lenses.ambitious: Follow up consistently across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo while tailoring contact to each customer's agreed terms.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive drafting and attachment gathering. Preserve the calls where a person can uncover and solve the problem.
lenses.options: Offer a neutral reminder, a promise follow-up and a firm escalation draft using the same verified facts.
lenses.altitude: Design the reminder sequence, contact limits and exception rules, then assess their effect on receipts and complaints.
reach: Improve customer billing instructions with the Bookkeeper.
Prepare recurring payment-friction findings for customer-facing teams.

sol.human_edge: Reading tone, maintaining trust and judging when a call will work better than another message.
sol.pattern_why: Preparing contact requires several checks and documents. An agent_with_gate lets the officer approve each outgoing contact during initial deployment.

in_practice.trigger: A verified overdue item reaches an approved contact milestone.
steps: Check current balances, disputes, collection pauses and recent contact.
Select a verified recipient and the approved reminder stage.
Prepare a factual message and retrieve the relevant invoice attachments.
Present the message or call briefing to the officer for approval.
Send the approved reminder and record its outcome and next review date.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve each outgoing reminder initially and conduct calls personally. Only validated routine templates should later move to exception-based sending.
data_needed: Verified billing contacts and language preferences
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS collection history and the Outlook sent message, linked to the approval and source balance timestamp.

grok.short: Remind overdue customers by mail or phone and ask them to pay.

today.trigger: A customer on the day's list is past the house grace, or a promise date has been missed.
steps: Take the next customer and gather the open invoices from AFAS.
Find the billing contact in the dossier or in old mail.
Send a reminder from a Word or Outlook template, or call.
Write down what was sent or said and when to try again.
For a few large shippers, check with sales before making contact.
drudgery: Assembling the invoice list and the attachments for a standard reminder.
Looking up the right contact and the language for that customer.
Logging the send so the next reminder does not go too soon.
today.time_sinks: The 130 hours sit mainly in preparation and in calls. Personal visits are rare; contact is mail and phone, with an occasional meeting when sales asks.

lenses.faster: The standard reminder, with the right invoices and the right language, goes out from the policy, and the call starts from a one-page brief.
lenses.autonomous: When an item crosses the agreed day count and is not disputed or flagged, the template reminder sends and logs itself. A broken promise or a balance above the threshold waits for the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Every delinquent account would get a timely notice that matches the contract and, where it applies, the statutory collection-cost rules, so a later incasso file is already in order.
lenses.joy: Mail-merge and hunting for the invoice PDF can go. A call that actually settles a dispute is the work worth keeping.
lenses.options: For a sensitive account, three drafts: a short Dutch reminder, an English statement of account, and a call script with the open items.
lenses.altitude: The officer writes the reminder policy with the controller: timing, amounts, language, cost line, and which customers sales may block.
reach: The AR bookkeepers' requests for a statement of account.
The file an external incassobureau asks the controller to assemble.
A first-pass reply to sales when they ask whether a shipper may book.

grok.human_edge: The phone call, the decision to wait a few days for a long-standing shipper, and the judgment to involve sales before a hard reminder goes to a key account.
grok.pattern_why: A reminder can start a legal clock and can damage a shipping relationship. The standard steps are repeatable, and a person releases anything outside the policy and makes the calls.

in_practice.trigger: An item crosses a step in the reminder policy, or a promise date passes with the item still open.
steps: Select accounts that crossed the step and are not disputed or flagged by sales.
Fill the reminder in the debtor's language with the open items and the cost line the policy allows.
Send the reminders that sit inside the pre-agreed rule and log them on the debtor.
Prepare a one-page brief for every account that needs a call.
The officer calls, then the outcome and the next date are written back to the dossier.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer agrees the rule in advance, releases any account sales has flagged, and makes every call. A disputed account stays out of the automatic batch.
data_needed: The approved timing, thresholds, and cost line.
Billing contact and language on the debtor.
Open items, prior reminders, and dispute status.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS dossier and the sent-items folder of the collections mailbox.

Compare the stack with the room left in the site budget and the contingency.
Write the resource figure, the assumptions and the gaps.
drudgery: Building a cost stack from a blank workbook because the last one is private.

today.time_sinks: Finding comparable actuals and restating them for the new case takes longer than the judgment about whether the company should do it.

lenses.ambitious: Every serious operational idea would arrive at the management meeting with a cost and a margin, including the smaller ones that are skipped today because nobody has the hours.

lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the cost-stack templates and the rate library, and reviews stacks that need a rate the library does not hold.
reach: A first cost, including lost productive hours, for a certificate wave (forklift, VCA, and food safety where a site handles food) that the learning specialist can use.
The accrual shape the accountant needs when a program straddles the month end.

grok.human_edge: Challenging the operational case: volume counted twice, a flex rate that will not hold when labour is tight, or a saving that is real only after the works council has been consulted.

List missing drivers and any rate that is outside the library.

sol.short: Summarise funding requests and recommend which ones management should approve.

today.trigger: A budget owner requests new funding or a change to an approved spending envelope.
steps: Collect the request, business case and relevant budget position.
Check affordability, expected benefits, timing and approval authority.
Compare the request with competing demands and available funding.
Write a recommendation, including conditions or reasons to decline.
Submit the decision pack and record management's decision.
drudgery: Reformatting business cases into approval papers.
Repeating affordability calculations.
Finding missing attachments and tracking decision status.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are incomplete requests, inconsistent benefit claims and clarification rounds before an approver can decide.

lenses.faster: Generate a consistent decision pack from validated models, current budget headroom and the approval matrix.
lenses.autonomous: A complete request triggers affordability checks and a draft recommendation. The analyst approves the recommendation before submission.
lenses.ambitious: Assess requests together as a portfolio, showing cash constraints, operational dependencies and displaced priorities.
lenses.joy: Remove paper assembly and repeated calculations. Keep the judgement about whether a request deserves scarce funding.
lenses.options: Present approve, phase, reduce scope, defer and decline options with comparable financial effects.

reach: Prepare the Finance Director's investment and funding review materials.
Help the Controller maintain a consistent funding-decision register.

sol.human_edge: Funding choices involve strategy, service reliability and competing interests. The analyst must challenge benefit claims and make a defensible recommendation.
sol.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: the workflow assembles evidence and drafts recommendations, but financial judgement and funding authority remain explicit human gates.

in_practice.trigger: A funding request has a named owner, completed model and required supporting evidence.
steps: Validate completeness, approval authority and links to the underlying cost model.
Calculate budget headroom and cash effects, accounting for existing approved commitments.
Compare feasible options against approved financial and operational criteria.
Draft a recommendation that separates verified evidence, assumptions and judgement.
Have the analyst approve the pack, route it to the authorised decision maker and record the decision.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst owns the recommendation; only the manager specified in the approval matrix can approve funding.
data_needed: Current budget headroom and approved commitments
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint funding register with recommendation versions, approver identity, decision, conditions and supporting evidence.

evidence.claim: SharePoint lists and document libraries can hold structured request records and versioned approval documents.
Automated preparation and gated recommendations could save 60% of task time; strategic deliberation remains human work.

risks: A convincing draft may conceal weak evidence or uncertain benefits.
Stale commitment data can overstate available funding.
A scoring model can undervalue safety, compliance or service resilience.
Workflow routing could be mistaken for approval or exceed delegated authority.
research_questions: How much time is spent assembling packs versus deciding what to recommend?
Are commitments and the approval matrix reliable enough for automatic affordability checks?
Would retrospective packs preserve the key concerns raised in previous funding decisions?

grok.short: Sum up a funds request and recommend a yes or a no.

today.trigger: A manager asks for extra budget (overtime, flex, a repair, equipment, a small project), or the monthly transfer list arrives.
steps: Read the request and the budget still left on that cost center.
Check commitments, year-to-date spend and the forecast.
Write a short summary with a yes, a no, or a yes inside a cap.
Send the recommendation to the controller or the finance director, depending on the mandate.
File the decision so the same euros are not promised again.
drudgery: Restating the remaining-budget arithmetic in every mail.
Chasing a missing amount, period or cost center.
Keeping a private list of approvals so the contingency is not used twice.
today.time_sinks: The summary maths and the search for what is left take longer than the recommendation. The sensitive part is a no, and the explanation to someone senior.

lenses.faster: Remaining budget, commitments and a first recommendation are attached when the request arrives. Rebuilding the 'what is left' table drops out.
lenses.autonomous: A form submission or a request mail starts the summary on its own. The recommendation does not leave until a person releases it.
lenses.ambitious: Small requests inside a pre-agreed envelope would be answered the same day, and the free contingency would stay visible through the peak.
lenses.joy: Rewriting the remaining-budget paragraph is no loss. The hard recommendation, and a no that the manager can understand, stays with the analyst.
lenses.options: The note carries approve, approve inside a cap, defer to the reforecast, or refuse, each with the effect on the site forecast and the contingency.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the envelope rules for what can be approved inside the budget and what must go to the finance director, and reviews the refusals and the exceptions.
reach: A short note to the credit and collections officer when the request also worsens cash or days sales outstanding.
The transfer instruction the accountant books after the mandate holder has decided.

grok.human_edge: A refusal a site manager will accept because the reason is fair, and a yes that does not spend the same contingency twice. Safety, a customer penalty or a CAO entitlement needs a different ear from ordinary overspend.
grok.pattern_why: The figures and a draft recommendation can be prepared from written rules, but an approval or a refusal carries a name. A person releases it, and the mandate holder confirms it.

in_practice.trigger: A funds request is submitted on a form or by mail.
steps: Read the cost center, amount, period and reason, and send the request back if one of those is missing.
Attach remaining budget, commitments, year-to-date, forecast and the free contingency.
Draft the recommendation from the envelope rules.
The analyst edits the wording and releases the recommendation to the controller or the finance director.
The decision and any AFAS budget transfer are logged before another request can use the same room.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is approved, refused or transferred until the analyst releases the recommendation and the person with the mandate confirms it.
data_needed: Remaining budget and commitments by cost center
The contingency balance and its earmarks
in_practice.logs_to: A funds-request log: request, recommendation, decision, mandate holder, and the budget version that was updated.

steps: Scan Power BI dashboards and AFAS actuals for variances

lenses.ambitious: A standing savings pipeline with owners, euro values and progress, reviewed monthly by the MT, instead of ad hoc ideas that fade.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet merging and dashboard trawling; more time on the floor in Venlo or Tilburg understanding why the numbers move.

sol.short: Find practical ways to lower site costs and improve margins.

steps: Review Power BI trends and reconcile material movements to AFAS.

Discuss possible causes and improvements with site managers and Finance.
Estimate benefits, propose a trial and track agreed actions.

Rebuilding variance bridges for each site.
Chasing explanations and updating action trackers.
Reformatting the same findings for monthly reviews.

lenses.autonomous: After each successful nightly extract, rules identify persistent exceptions and prepare investigation packs. Site-specific thresholds and human triage control which findings become actions.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling opportunity pipeline across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, with measured trials and benefits reflected in the forecast only when supported.
lenses.joy: Remove recurring report assembly and tracker maintenance. Keep the site conversations, problem solving and visible improvements.

sol.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes correlation from a workable intervention, earns site managers' trust and balances cost with service, safety and workforce constraints.

Track observed results and submit supported forecast changes through the normal approval process.

Analysis at individual employee level (overtime, absence) touches AVG/GDPR and may need OR agreement
A labour-cost idea is sent to operations as if it were only a finance variance, without HR or the works council.
The three sites do different work, so a league table of cost per order treats unlike warehouses as the same.
Recommendations could reduce service or safety, or shift costs elsewhere.
Different customer mixes, service requirements or accrual timing could make site comparisons misleading.
The list chases booking noise, and after a few false alarms the site leads stop reading it.
An idea that was never accepted is still written into the forecast, and the business trusts the next one less.
Too many false-positive flags and the channel gets ignored
Savings estimates by AI overstated and erode trust with the MT

research_questions.text: Are Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo comparable on the drivers we would watch, or does customer mix make a ranking misleading?
Can agency hours be matched to AFAS cost centres reliably today?
Do site leads already have a Power BI view they ignore, and what would a shortlist have to show to be used?
Which of the likely leaks sit outside the nightly extract, such as agency invoices, damage, and empty kilometres?
How many savings ideas from last year were implemented and what did they deliver?
Are comparable throughput, service and quality measures available for all three sites, and who owns them?
Can current reports separate rate, volume, mix, productivity and accounting timing effects reliably?
How many flagged exceptions lead to actions with measurable benefits rather than explanations alone?
Can a controlled trial demonstrate savings without worsening service, safety or workforce outcomes?
Of the improvement notes written in the last year, how many changed a forecast or a cost, and how many were commentary only?
Which anomaly rules would site managers find useful rather than noise?

evidence.claim: Power BI has built-in anomaly detection on line charts and smart narrative summaries.
Power BI supports scheduled refresh and rule-based dashboard alerts, subject to configuration and supported data sources.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI scheduled refresh and data alerts

evidence.claim: Power BI can hold a refreshed actual-versus-budget model and raise a threshold alert, so the monthly scan does not have to start from a blank export.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI; model knowledge of product scope

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit management information already shows actuals against budget for finance users, which is the feed this search starts from.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit; model knowledge of product scope

evidence.claim: LLMs can write variance explanations from structured driver data.
Combining agency and payroll hours exposes flex cost savings in warehousing.
Governed variance calculations and model-assisted hypotheses can reduce investigation preparation, but cannot establish causality by themselves.
Turning a variance into a profit idea that a warehouse or transport lead will own is still a conversation; the tool is better at finding the gap than at getting it accepted.

A labour idea kept at site and cost-centre level, and decided by a person, stays outside automated decisions about individual workers. Ranking named employees would be a different, and riskier, system under the EU AI Act.
A 35% time reduction is a provisional estimate; realised profit improvement has not been established.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS refresh lands in Power BI, or a labour, margin, or cash driver crosses a threshold the analyst has set.
steps: Compare actuals with the forecast on a fixed driver set: labour per order, flex premium, overtime, subcontracted transport, warehouse cost, and DSO.
Rank gaps by euro effect, drop anything explained by a known one-off, and keep gaps that repeated last month.
Draft a few candidate moves per material gap, each with a euro range and the extra fact that would confirm it.
The analyst removes the false ones and keeps a short list for the site lead or the Controller.
Record which ideas were accepted, measured, or killed, and feed the accepted ones into the next forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: No idea goes to a site or into the forecast until the FP&A analyst has marked it as worth a conversation. Anything that changes staffing goes through the HR Business Partner and, where the WOR requires it, the works council.
data_needed: Driver definitions agreed with the Controller
Forecast and budget by site and cost centre
Flex hours and rates, and overtime hours
in_practice.logs_to: An opportunity log the Controller can open: driver, euro range, owner, status, and whether it changed the next forecast.

opus.short: Look for cost savings and margin gains, like overtime, agency hours, idle trucks, per site.

today.trigger: A margin dip, a board request, or the analyst spots something in the monthly figures.
steps: Pull costs and volumes per site from Power BI and AFAS
Compare agency invoices and hours from the staffing portals
Look for outliers in Excel (overtime, absence, cost per pallet or per km)
Discuss findings with site managers and the Controller
Write up ideas with estimated savings
drudgery: Merging agency portal exports with AFAS data by hand
Building the same comparison tables each month
Scanning long lists for outliers
today.time_sinks: Joining data from AFAS, agency portals and Power BI; most time goes to preparing data, little to finding causes.

lenses.faster: A monthly join of AFAS, agency hours and invoices, and volumes shows cost per unit and outliers per site, ready to read.
lenses.autonomous: Outliers above a set threshold, such as agency hours above plan or invoice hours not matching ordered hours, are flagged to the analyst and site manager automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every site gets a monthly driver review with a tracked list of savings ideas and their realised euros, instead of ad hoc hunts.
lenses.joy: No more spreadsheet merging; time goes to site visits and working out with managers why a number moves.
lenses.options: For each finding, the assistant drafts several possible causes and actions with rough euro effects to test with the site.
lenses.altitude: The analyst defines the cost drivers and thresholds and runs the savings pipeline, rather than hunting for outliers by hand.
reach: Bookkeeper: agency invoice versus hours checks
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: overtime and absence cost analysis
Controller: margin analysis per site

opus.human_edge: Understanding operations on the floor and persuading site managers to change how they work.
opus.pattern_why: The data join and outlier flags are deterministic, but finding real causes and winning support for change are human work; AI widens the search and drafts options.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and monthly agency invoice upload complete.
steps: Pipeline joins AFAS costs, agency hours and invoices, and volumes per site
Rules flag outliers against thresholds and plan
Assistant drafts possible causes and questions per flag
Analyst checks with the site manager and records the idea in the savings tracker
Realised savings are measured in the following months
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst decides which flags become savings ideas; site managers and the Finance Director approve actions.
data_needed: AFAS costs and hours per cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Savings tracker in SharePoint with flag, idea, owner and realised euros

evidence.claim: Agents gather data and flag records that do not tie; people decide what to act on.
Copilot in Power BI can answer questions and summarise reports on a prepared semantic model, with English as the supported language.
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%).

risks: Overtime and absence data per person is personal data under AVG; works council involvement is needed if it monitors staff
Flags without context lead to blame instead of improvement
Agency data formats differ across the three portals and break the join

How much did agency invoice versus hours mismatches cost last year?
Does the works council need to give consent (WOR art. 27) for site-level overtime and absence analysis?
